backgroundFluff.name: Tournament Competitor
entries: You have dedicated a portion of your life to the games hosted in Yatamon's Grand Tournament Arena, becoming a Quadai, one of the games' most experienced athletes. The tournament is a spectacle of skill, endurance, and fierce competition, where athletes from across Obojima test their mettle to honor the four great river spirits. Whether you specialized in feats of strength, acrobatics, or an unconventional fighting style, you have a reputation to uphold. Perhaps you are a celebrated champion whose career is winding down, or maybe you're a young upstart trying to make a name for yourself. Whatever the case, the call of the arena will always stir in your blood.

backgroundFluff.name: Reporter
entries: You are a reporter who has traveled across Obojima or combed the streets of Yatamon, seeking out stories that matter. You may have worked in-house for the Yatamon Daily Observer, chasing down scoops throughout the city, or you may be an independent journalist gathering stories and selling them. You have an unquenchable desire to know the truth, and you're willing to take the risks to get to the bottom of a good story.

backgroundFluff.name: Raised by Cats
entries: By a twist of fate, you were discovered as an infant and raised by a clowder of awakened cats within Yatamon. These intelligent felines took you in, showed you love, and taught you their ways—the beauty of relaxation, the thrill of the chase, and subtle hints of the supernatural just beyond your sight. You learned to value independence and to trust your keen senses above all else. Though you are now an adventurer that has forged your own identity, a part of you will always be a cat at heart.

spell.name: Airbag

time.condition: which you take when you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage

entries: You momentarily create an airbag in the target's space, absorbing some of the incoming damage. The triggering damage is reduced by {@dice 1d6}. The airbag then disappears.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The amount of damage the airbag absorbs increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Avian Courier
entries: You conjure a magical bird, which picks up one object you can see within range that isn't being worn or carried. The object can weigh no more than 50 pounds. The bird carries it to a destination of your choice on a surface within 200 feet of you, as long as there is an unobstructed path to the destination. The bird arrives at the start of your next turn, and then vanishes.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The maximum weight of the object increases by 50 pounds, and the maximum distance to the destination increases by 100 feet, for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Borrow Magic
entries: You touch a willing creature, pulling from its pool of magical energy to fuel your spellcasting. The target expends a level 1 spell slot, temporarily lending it to you. Once before the start of your next turn, you can cast a spell using the borrowed spell slot instead of your own. If you don't expend the borrowed spell slot before then, it is lost. Once a creature has lent three spell slots in this way, it can't do so again until it finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The maximum level of spell slot that can be lent to you in this way increases when you reach levels 5 (level 2 slot), 11 (level 3 slot), and 17 (level 4 slot).

spell.name: Bait
entries: You create a floating, spectral lure that resembles a flying fish of your choice and lasts for the duration. The fish appears within range in a space of your choice, and you can immediately move it up to 20 feet. Each creature that can see the lure and is within 5 feet of it as it moves by must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is either baited or dragged (your choice for each creature).

items.name: Baited
entries: The creature lashes out at the lure. If the creature takes the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on its next turn, the number of attacks it can make is reduced by one (to a minimum of no attacks).

items.name: Dragged
entries: The creature moves with the lure, following it for the rest of the lure's movement, provided it doesn't have a {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of 0; this movement provokes {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. At the start of the creature's next turn, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by the number of feet the lure caused it to move.
As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your later turns, you can move the lure up to 20 feet.

spell.name: Charge
entries: You touch a machine, temporarily powering it and allowing it to function as if it were whelmed by a spirit or permanently enchanted. A machine targeted by this spell stays powered for the duration before shutting off. For a machine to function using this spell, it must still be in working condition.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The spell's duration increases with a spell slot of level 3–4 (1 day), 5–6 (7 days), 7–8 (30 days), and 9 (1 year).

spell.name: Correspondence

m.text: a ball of wax worth 10+ GF, which the spell consumes; a blank piece of paper; and an envelope

entries: Choose a creature within range. The target speaks a message up to 100 words long, which is recorded on the paper used as a Material component in the spell's casting and then sealed in the envelope with the ball of wax. While holding the envelope, the intended recipient (designated when you cast the spell) can open it as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action. The envelope can also be opened if it's targeted by a {@spell Knock|XPHB} spell or similar magic. When it's opened, the recorded message is magically read aloud in the target's voice; the spell then ends.

If a creature other than the intended recipient attempts to open the envelope by nonmagical means, it must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature fails to break the seal. On a successful save, the envelope is destroyed. When the envelope is destroyed, the spell ends.

spell.name: Demon Lure
entries: You place the totem used as a Material component at a point you can see on the ground within your reach. The totem can be picked up and moved, and it becomes magically enticing to demons (Fiends) for the duration. A demon that doesn't have {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} from the totem and starts its turn in a 150-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from it must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the demon has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition until the spell ends. This effect ends early if the demon comes within 5 feet of the totem or if it's no longer on the same plane of existence as the totem.
While {@condition Charmed|XPHB} in this way, a demon must take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action and move toward the totem by the safest route on each of its turns unless there is nowhere to move.

If the demon takes any damage or if another creature uses an action to shake the demon out of its stupor, it repeats the save, ending the spell on itself on a success. A demon that succeeds on a save against this spell is {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|immune} to its effects for the duration.
When used in games other than Obojima, the caster can choose to affect one of the following creature types of their choice: Aberrations, Fey, Fiends, or Undead (at the GM's discretion).

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: If you cast this spell using a level 5+ spell slot, the size of the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} increases: 300-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} (level 5–6 slot), 500-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} (level 7–8 slot), or 1,000-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} (level 9 slot).

spell.name: Detect Curse
entries: For the duration, you sense the presence of curses within 30 feet of yourself. If you sense a curse, you can take the {@action Magic|XPHB} action to see a faint aura around any visible creature or object in the area that bears the curse, and if a curse was bestowed by an item or spell, you learn what item or spell caused it and its rarity or spell level.
This spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

spell.name: Fire Hydrant
entries: You create a Small fire hydrant in an unoccupied space on a solid surface you can see within range. The hydrant expels a continuous stream of pressurized water in a direction you choose. The stream is a {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} that is 20 feet long and 5 feet wide. Each creature in the {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed to the nearest unoccupied space at the end of the {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. A creature that enters the {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} for the first time on a turn or ends a turn there must make the same save.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your later turns while you're within range, you can change the direction in which the stream blasts from the hydrant, causing the previous stream of water to cease.

The hydrant has an {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} equal to your spell save DC, 30 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and Psychic damage. Reducing the hydrant to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} destroys it, ending the spell early.

spell.name: Gotcha!
entries: A capsule toy machine appears in a small explosion of confetti in an unoccupied space within range. The machine's appearance is accompanied by brief but energetic sounds of slide whistles and noisemakers. The machine produces a random potion from {@filter Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass|items|source=obojimatallgrass|type=potion|miscellaneous=}, which you can immediately retrieve or allow to be gently deposited on the ground. The machine then vanishes.

When you cast the spell, choose either the {@filter Combat|items|source=obojimatallgrass|type=potion|property=combat|miscellaneous=}, {@filter Utility|items|source=obojimatallgrass|type=potion|property=utility|miscellaneous=}, or {@filter Whimsy|items|source=obojimatallgrass|type=potion|property=whimsical|miscellaneous=} potion list and roll {@dice 1d20} on that list. The potion produced by the machine corresponds to the number you rolled. This potion can be used by any creature, but it disappears if it isn't used within 1 hour.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: If you cast this spell using a level 2+ spell slot, you can choose to add 10 to your {@dice d20} roll.

spell.name: Graffiti Trap

m.text: a jar of paint worth 5+ GF, which the spell consumes

entries: You paint an arcane trap that later unleashes a magical effect. You graffiti a surface (such as a section of a wall, floor, or table) within range with the paint. The graffiti can cover an area no larger than 5 feet in diameter. If the surface is moved more than 10 feet from where you cast this spell, the paint becomes nonmagical, and the spell ends without being triggered.
The graffiti appears mundane and requires a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check against your spell save DC to determine that it's magical.

The trap is triggered when a creature enters the area within 5 feet of the graffiti or when you choose to trigger it as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action. When you cast this spell, you can designate creatures that don't trigger the trap when they enter its area. Once the trap is triggered, you are magically made aware that it was triggered (provided you're on the same plane of existence as it), and this spell ends.

When triggered, the trap erupts in an explosion of color, sending tendrils of magical paint toward the target. Alternatively, if you trigger the trap as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can target a creature you can see within 10 feet of the graffiti. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw.

On a failed save, the target is pulled to the surface that bears the graffiti and has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. It can take an action to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check against your spell save DC, freeing itself on a success. The paint becomes nonmagical, and the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition ends after 1 minute or when the creature has at least one gallon of water splashed on it.
On a successful save, the creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is instead halved until the start of its next turn.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The spell's duration increases with a spell slot of level 3 (8 hours), 4 (1 day), 5 (7 days), and 6+ (30 days).

spell.name: Identify Curse

m.text: a small Kyojin Candle worth 50+ GF, which the spell consumes

entries: Using the special properties of a Kyojin Candle, you uncover the inner workings of a curse. Choose one of the following options.

items.name: Creature or Object
entries: The spell reveals the many aspects of any curses on a creature or object you touch. This includes the effects of the curse, who or what caused the curse, and how the curse can be ended (for example, by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} or {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} spell).

items.name: Area
entries: The spell reveals the effects of a curse affecting the area within a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you. If the area isn't cursed, the spell instead reveals whether a cursed creature or object has passed through the area within the past 24 hours.

spell.name: One-Way Street
entries: You create an image of a paved road on the ground within range, which lasts for the duration. The road is a {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} and can be up to 15 feet wide and 120 feet long. When you cast the spell, choose one direction along the road. A creature moving on the road in any other direction must spend 3 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves.

spell.name: Soda Pop
entries: In the final weaving of the spell's Somatic components, you summon a can of soda in your hand, which you throw into a space within range. When the spell ends, the can pops, and each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} originating from the can makes a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes Force damage equal to the total accumulated damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. The spell ends early if the can is being carried by a creature at the end of a turn.
At the end of each of your turns, the radius of the spell's {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} increases by 5 feet.

The spell's base damage is {@damage 8d4}. If the can is moved more than 20 feet or a creature within 5 feet of it takes a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to shake the can, the spell's damage increases by {@dice 1d4} (to a maximum of {@damage 14d4}). Once the damage increases in this way, it can't do so again until initiative count 30 on the next round.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The base damage and maximum damage increases by {@dice 1d4} for each spell slot level above 3.

spell.name: Stop Sign
entries: You conjure a spectral stop sign in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you, which disappears at the start of your next turn. One creature of your choice within range must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target is unable to move toward the stop sign for the duration.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The number of creatures you can target with the spell increases when you reach levels 5 (two creatures), 11 (three creatures), and 17 (four creatures).

spell.name: Summon Ompo Swarm
entries: You summon a swarm of mouselike spirits called ompo, which appears in a 10-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} within range. The spirits consume all Small or smaller nonmagical objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried, destroying them; you can designate any objects for the spirits to ignore. They then disappear.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The size of the {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} increases by 5 feet for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Taxi Service
entries: You conjure a Huge spectral taxi within range, which moves up to 120 feet in a {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. Each Medium or smaller willing creature of your choice within 5 feet of the {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} is pulled into the taxi as it passes by the creature. The taxi (and any creature it's carrying) passes through objects in its path but immediately stops before attempting to pass through 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead. Each creature carried by the taxi exits to an unoccupied space of its choice within 5 feet of where the taxi ends its movement, after which the taxi vanishes.

spell.name: Unearth Demon
entries: Using techniques developed by the nakudama, you magically detect and uncover information about Demons in the area. Choose one of the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} sizes listed below; you learn the associated information in that area.

items.name: 1,000-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}
entries: You learn the exact number of Demons within the area.

items.name: 500-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}
entries: You learn the exact number of Demons within the area, and you learn the direction and distance to each of their locations.

items.name: 250-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}
entries: You learn the exact number of Demons within the area, the direction and distance to each of their locations, the kind of Demon each of them is, and their respective {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB|Challenge Ratings}.

When used in games other than Obojima, the caster can choose to learn this information regarding one of the following creature types of their choice: Aberrations, Fey, Fiends, or Undead (at the GM's discretion).

spell.name: Vine Ladder

components.m: a stem, leaf, or other piece of a plant

entries: You conjure a ladder composed of vines on a solid surface up to 15 feet tall that you can see within range. The ladder remains stationary for the duration. If you create a new ladder with this spell, the first ladder vanishes.

spell.name: Warding Barrier
entries: A 15-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on a point you can see within range becomes warded against certain creatures for the duration. Choose one creature type. Whenever a creature of that type with a {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} of 2 or lower attempts to move into the area, it must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the creature has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, and it can't enter the area for the rest of the turn.

If such a creature starts its turn in the area, it must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is shunted to the nearest unoccupied space outside the area, has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, and takes {@damage 2d8} Force damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The maximum {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} of creatures the spell can affect increases by 1 for each spell slot level above 2.

feat.name: Born in Yatamon

prerequisite.other: Lived in Yatamon for at least 1 year

entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: First Age Aficionado
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Salvage|ObojimaTallGrass} skill, or {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} if you already have proficiency in it.

entries.name: Melting Pot
entries: You learn {@language Naku Naku|ObojimaTallGrass} and {@language Torum|ObojimaTallGrass} if you don't already know them.

entries.name: Mixed with Magic
entries: When you are targeted by a level 1+ spell cast by yourself or an ally, you can choose to regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice the spell's level. You can use this benefit twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Yatamon's Blessing
entries: You learn one cantrip of your choice from the {@filter Wizard spell list|spells|level=0|class=wizard|components & miscellaneous=}.

feat.name: Connoisseur
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Gastronomic Bliss
entries: If you eat a satisfying meal as part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can choose to gain {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} or a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal {@dice 1d10} + your character level (your choice) at the end of the rest.

entries.name: Impressive Banter
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma checks at any formal event, such as a banquet or tea ceremony.

entries.name: Kitchen Skills
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item Brewer's Supplies|XPHB} or {@item Cook's Utensils|XPHB}. In addition, you can spend 10 minutes with an ingredient or potion to determine its properties without making an ability check.

feat.name: Feline Instincts
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Balance Adept
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks and saving throws to avoid the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, and you spend a maximum of 10 feet of movement to remove that condition.

entries.name: Second Tongue
entries: You can communicate with felines as if by the {@spell Speak with Animals|XPHB} spell.

entries.name: Uncanny Senses
entries: You can add half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} (round down) to any Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check you make, even if you're already adding your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to that check.

feat.name: Haggler
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Opportunist
entries: When a creature you can see within 10 feet of yourself fails a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} using Charisma, you gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next Charisma ({@skill Intimidation} or {@skill Persuasion}) check you make against that target in the next hour. Alternatively, you can choose to gain {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB}, and you can't gain it in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Saving Face
entries: Whenever you fail a Charisma check or Charisma saving throw, you can roll the {@dice d20} again and you must use the new roll. When you do so, the DC for the check or save increases by 3.

entries.name: Silver Tongue
entries: When purchasing a good or paying for a service, you receive a 5 percent discount on it. In addition, when doing so, you can expend {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} and roll {@dice 1d10}. The cost of the good or service, is reduced by an additional percent equal to 10 plus the number rolled on the die.

feat.name: Motorist
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Defensive Driver
entries: Vehicles you operate gain a +1 bonus to their AC.

entries.name: Maneuver Master
entries: You add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to all Maneuvering checks you make with a vehicle. Additionally, all vehicles with a Size Modifier of 2 or smaller are considered to have the Nimble and Simple properties when you are operating them.

entries.name: Offensive Driver
entries: When using a vehicle to ram, you add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} when calculating the save DC.

feat.name: Yoka Scout
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Close Combat Ally
entries: Whenever an ally misses an attack roll against a creature you can see within 10 feet of you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to allow the ally to reroll the attack. If the attack roll then hits, you immediately regain the use of your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}. You can regain the use of your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} in this way a number of times equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} (round down), after which this ability always consumes your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Competitive
entries: When you make an ability check that you've seen an ally succeed on in the last minute, you gain a +2 bonus to the roll.

entries.name: Well-Researched
entries: Whenever you take the {@action Search|XPHB} action, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the check if it is related to a Demon.

feat.name: Pouncing
entries: Whenever you move 15 feet or more toward a creature immediately before making an attack against it with a Melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you gain a +2 bonus to the attack roll. If you instead use the {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Grapple} or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Shove} option of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against the creature, the DC for the saving throw it makes increases by 2.

subclassFeature.name: Neko Duelist
entries: As a cat stalks a mouse, Fighters who practice the neko duelist tradition bide their time until the perfect moment to pounce upon a foe with drawn steel. These Fighters weave through battle, engaging multiple enemies at once, ready to dart out at any moment to deliver a staggering blow through their signature pounce technique. The neko duelist tradition is secretive, and it may trace its origins to antiquity—possibly even early in the Age of Humanity.

What separates the neko duelist approach to combat from other fighting traditions is that most of its practitioners are cats. From time to time, a master of the style will agree to take on a bipedal student. Such Fighters are immersed in cat culture and taught the ways of the feline blade—above all, the art of the pounce. Though it may appear to others that these Fighters take on cat-like attributes, this is strictly a matter of technique.

There's an unspoken rule that those who wish to become master duelists must be instructed in the tradition by an awakened cat. To attempt to pry knowledge of the style from a non-cat teacher is to incur the enmity of cats.

entries.name: Building the Basics
entries: As a non-cat neko duelist, it often takes years to be taught even the most basic skills and attributes of the cat. Students spend countless hours with their masters honing their timing, strengthening their bodies, and sharpening their perception. It's commonly said that, as a bipedal disciple, one must reimagine who they are and allow the qualities of the cat to become part of their nature before ever being instructed to pick up a blade.

A cat's supernatural senses are also not beyond teaching. Master Togi Obata, a legendary neko duelist, described cats' innate sixth sense as "a coin hidden within a riverbed." Some beings have a naturally shallow river, making their coin easy to find, while others have deep rushing waters, where the coin's existence is beyond comprehension. If cats have calm, shallow streams, then beings such as humans have dangerous rapids. That does not mean it is impossible to find the coin; it simply takes dedication.

entries.name: Celebrity
entries: Becoming a neko duelist is a feat worth honoring in cat culture. There's a level of mysticism that surrounds the role, and their combat prowess is seen as beyond the natural. For non-cat duelists, there is an added degree of dedication and hardship that must be endured, which warrants a certain amount of respect. As a result, a duelist, cat or not, is treated with admiration in most instances and as a celebrity in others.

entries.name: The Feline Blade
entries: The blade of a cat is unlike any weapon crafted on Obojima, and though its form is familiar, the subtle details push the duelist's blade into a category of its own. These tools are so perfectly fitted to the cat's body that many non-cat neko duelists choose to abandon the blade type altogether for something more familiar.

subclassFeature.name: Cat Whisperer
entries: You can comprehend and verbally communicate with felines. You can use any of the {@action Influence|XPHB} action's skill options with them, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any checks you make against them as part of that action.

subclassFeature.name: Feline Nature
entries: Your training alongside your master has earned you the attributes of the cat. You gain the following benefits.

items.name: Catlike Agility
items.entry: You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. In addition, when you fall and don't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, you always land on your feet, and you can subtract up to 20 feet from the fall when calculating the damage you would take.

items.name: Nine Lives
items.entry: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} but not killed outright, you can immediately use your Second Wind feature (no action required) to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} before falling {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Outsized Trickery
entries: You're adept at using the weight of your foes against them. You can use the Shove option of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against any creature, regardless of its size. In addition, your shoves are more potent, imposing the following additional effect on a failed save, depending on whether you choose to push the target or cause it to have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Push
items.entry: The target is pushed an additional 5 feet away from you, and it takes Bludgeoning damage equal to half your Fighter level (round up) plus your Strength modifier.

items.name: Prone
items.entry: The target takes Bludgeoning damage equal to half your Fighter level (round up).

subclassFeature.name: Evasive Maneuvers
entries: Your quick thinking and agile reflexes make you a formidable foe, even when outnumbered. You gain the following benefits.

items.name: Deft Cover
items.entry: While at least two Small or larger enemies are within 5 feet of you, you have {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover}.

items.name: Nimble Redirect
items.entry: When you're hit by an attack made with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the damage you take by an amount equal to your Fighter level. When you do so, you can cause a creature or object within 5 feet of you to take damage equal to the amount you reduced from the attack. Once you take this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Vigilant Reflexes
entries: You can't be {@status Surprised|XPHB}, provided you don't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. In addition, immediately after rolling {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}; before or after moving in this way, you can also take the {@action Hide|XPHB} action as part of the same {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Cautious Tenacity
entries: You gain two additional uses of your Second Wind feature. Whenever you use your Second Wind to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you also gain the benefits of the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Swatting Flurry
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a target with a Melee weapon as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can unleash a flurry of swift strikes. Make up to five additional melee attack rolls, using the same weapon against the target, immediately stopping if you miss. For each of these attacks that hits, the target takes {@damage 1d10} damage of the weapon's type; these attacks can't apply any additional damage or effects that you or your weapon would normally impose.

subclassFeature.name: Fortune Rogue
entries: Some rogues practice skulking in the shadows; others study where and when to strike—but you? You've got luck on your side.

For reasons no one fully comprehends, fortune favors you in ways that defy explanation. You trip into treasure, stumble onto the missing key, or escape death by inches, surviving odds that would make a gambler faint.

But your luck isn't magic, and it isn't something you control. You're a leaf on the breeze in the winds of fortune, and although you live a charmed life, you've learned that chance is as fickle as fate and that not every gamble you make pays off.

entries.name: Favor Finds Conflict
entries: Though your luck brings about all manner of creature comforts, favorable deals, and unlikely wins, it also has a way of making enemies. Whether they are covetous bandits, jealous friends, or spiteful spirits, those with your fortune frequently find themselves at the wrong end of a blade more often than they'd like to admit. Yet it's in these dangerous situations that you've discovered your unorthodox way of combating danger and overcoming enemies. While your skill with a sword or a dagger might be great in its own regard, you find that your luck has a funny way of catching your foes off guard. These "sneak attacks," as you might call them, present themselves to you as clear as day—fortuitous opportunities when your foe opens their defenses and allows you to land a pivotal strike. Those unfamiliar with combat might misinterpret these attacks as measured assaults, but any skilled warrior would be astonished by your good fortune.

Players who are unfamiliar with the game, or those who prefer a straightforward style of play, may wish to choose a different subclass. The Fortune Rogue asks that both the player and the GM collaborate in a fashion that might require more improvisation than other character options. We recommend speaking with your GM about the Fortune Rogue before choosing it as your subclass.

entries.name: The Will of Obojima?
entries: Tales throughout Obojima's history have represented luck as a palpable force from which its great heroes have knowingly or unknowingly tapped into—it's said that, like magic, it exists all around us and can be called upon by a chosen few. Others receive its favor as a reward for their good deeds or as retribution for unjust actions taken against them.

Some believe luck is the manifestation of Obojima's will. Like the Great Beasts, they see luck as another tool that the island uses to guide and protect its people. Others believe it is a force of nature, like an intangible wind that sweeps across the Physical Realm, blessing those who stumble into its path.
No matter which interpretation holds more truth, a great number of Obojimans can agree that luck is as real as the sun and the sky.

subclassFeature.name: Beyond Coincidence
entries: You have a knack for making things inexplicably go your way. This luck is represented by your Fortune Dice, which are d20s. You have a number of Fortune Dice equal to half your Rogue level (round up). You regain all expended Fortune Dice whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

You can expend your Fortune Dice to make Luck checks, which are Charisma checks that you have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in. No spell, effect, or other ability—positive or negative—can alter your Luck checks.

items.name: Favored Talent
items.entry: Whenever you make an ability check, you can expend one of your Fortune Dice to instead make a Luck check, using that result for the ability check.

items.name: Lucky Break
items.entry: You can attempt to make luck strike at just the right moment, specifying the way in which your character's fortune shapes their circumstances. To do so, you take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and expend one of your Fortune Dice to make a Luck check, describing the desired outcome. The GM then sets a DC based on the likelihood of the specified scenario, with the outcome transpiring on a success.

entries.caption: Luck Check DC Examples
rows: A nearby sneeze obscures a different sound. A merchant hands you back too much change. A performer bites their tongue while singing.
A coin purse is forgotten at a table. A local knows the person you're looking for. You overhear an enemy plot.
A key falls out of someone's pocket. A guard is asleep at their post. A bandit loses grip on their sword.
A fire breaks out nearby. You stumble onto the exact group of ingredients you need. You fall from a rooftop onto a soft pile of bedding.
A spirit suddenly crosses into the Physical Realm and stops an assailant in their tracks.

entries.name: Lucky Break Example
entries: The Rogue is trying to find a letter addressed to an important wizard and stop it from being delivered. During their search, they bump into a postal knight, whom they believe might have the letter they need.

In that moment, the Rogue player asks the GM if they can make a Luck check, asking that the letter somehow drops from the postal knight's courier bag. As with any ability check, the GM sets a DC. This time, however, the DC is based on how likely the situation described by the player is to occur.
In this circumstance, the GM decides the outcome is unlikely and tells the player the DC is 16. With the DC established, the player makes their Luck check and rolls a 19, succeeding on the check.

The GM then describes how the postal knight turns a corner and accidentally slams into a spirit walking in the opposite direction. As the postal knight hits the ground, the contents of the bag go skittering across the pavement.

subclassFeature.name: Cup Half Full
entries: Whenever you or a creature within 60 feet of you rolls a 20 on a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you regain one expended Fortune Die. At the GM's discretion, you can't regain a Fortune Die in this way if the result of the {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} is inconsequential, such as winning a friendly game of cards.

subclassFeature.name: Lucky Strike
entries: When you make an attack roll against a creature, you can expend a Fortune Die to make a Luck check in place of the normal attack roll. On a hit, this attack triggers your Sneak Attack even if it normally wouldn't, provided you haven't already used it this turn.
If you use the Withdraw option of your Cunning Strike on this attack, you don't have to expend any Sneak Attack damage dice.

subclassFeature.name: Boon of Fortuity
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, roll two {@dice d20}s and record the numbers rolled. Whenever an effect created by a creature you can see forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw, you can replace the DC for that effect with one of these fortuitous rolls. You must choose to do so before any targets of the effect make their saves, and you can replace a save DC in this way only once per turn. Each fortuitous roll can be used only once. When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you lose any unused fortuitous rolls.

subclassFeature.name: The Skin of Your Teeth
entries: Tales of your legendary luck abound, guiding you and your allies. Roll three {@dice 3d20|d20}s for your Boon of Fortuity feature rather than two. In addition, whenever you or an ally within 60 feet of you takes 100 damage or less, you can replace the damage that creature takes with the number rolled on one of your fortuitous rolls.

subclassFeature.name: Coven Patron
entries: Belonging to a witch coven is more than being part of a club; a coven member shares a bond with their covenmates that permeates the very magic they wield. For most witches, this magical bond is subtle, showing itself during gatherings or in times of arcane collaboration. For some, however, their bond is the very source of their power. These Warlocks form pacts with their covens, allowing them to tap into the ambient magic that flows through the collective, granting them access to the coven's secrets, skills, and, more importantly, its spellcraft. In exchange for this power, they serve as an emissary for their covens.

entries.name: Historic Title
entries: The "Ambassador Pact" is an arcane tradition passed down from a bygone era of witchcraft. In a time when covens did not always see eye to eye and conflicts among them would stir unrest across the island, an agreement was made between covens for the betterment of Obojima—disputes would be settled by an individual rather than the many.

Covens would form a unique pact with a chosen witch, channeling their vast knowledge and specialized magics into a single spellcaster. This ambassador would act as the coven's voice and body, fighting for its place within the arcane arts.

Centuries later, the Ambassador Pact is still used in modern magic, though its role has changed slightly. Now, covens often make several pacts at the same time, splitting their power and knowledge across a handful of talented Warlocks. These skilled mages are often sent across the island to represent their coven in all manner of ways, from challenges and festivals to dangerous quests and secretive meetings.

entries.name: Collective Strength
entries: Although larger covens naturally generate more ambient magic from which they can flow into their chosen Warlock, smaller covens are still able to form the Ambassador Pact with one of their members. So long as a coven has at least three spellcasters, it can choose to share its magic with a fourth. The potential of a coven's ambassador is limited only by the combined strength of the collective; more members do not necessarily equate to a more powerful ambassador. That said, as a coven grows in membership, its pool of knowledge and power deepens, granting its ambassador access to more resources.

entries.name: Your Coven
entries: You have made a pact with one of Obojima's witch covens. These organizations are crucial for the growth of the island's arcane traditions and studies and are relied upon by communities of all sizes across the island. From soothsayers and potion brewers to curse binders and enchanters, the members of Obojima's greatest covens are often highly regarded individuals, and you have now taken up one of the coven's most pivotal roles.

Choose which coven you've joined or determine it randomly using the coven table. If the coven you've joined isn't listed on the table, choose one of the following covens as a surrogate for determining which abilities this subclass grants you.

subclassFeature.name: Coven Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Coven Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Coven Spells
rows: {@spell Animal Friendship|XPHB}, {@spell Bless|XPHB}, {@spell Borrow Magic|ObojimaTalesYatamon}, {@spell Mirror Image|XPHB}, {@spell Shared Vision|ObojimaTallGrass}

subclassFeature.name: Collective Knowledge
entries: You can call on your coven's knowledge of the arcane at a moment's notice. You gain the following benefits.

items.name: Borrowed Talent
items.entry: When you make an ability check using a skill or tool you don't have proficiency with, you can choose to gain proficiency with that skill or tool (no action required). Alternatively, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to learn one language of your choice. You retain this proficiency or language until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Once you use this ability to gain a proficiency or language, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Spell Swap
items.entry: Over the course of 10 minutes, you can perform a ritual to telepathically commune with another witch in your coven and swap a spell with them. While doing so, you can ask one question that can be answered with yes, no, or unclear. The witch you're communing with answers to the best of their ability. At the completion of the ritual, choose one level 1+ Warlock spell you have prepared and one spell of your choice of the same level or lower from the {@filter Druid or Wizard|spells|level=!0|class=druid;wizard} spell list. Until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you no longer have that Warlock spell prepared, replacing it with the chosen Druid or Wizard spell. In addition, you can cast the chosen spell once without expending a spell slot. Once you perform this ritual, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Coven's Bond
entries: Like the bond to your coven, you're able to bind a creature to yourself. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can forge a bond between you and another creature you can see within 60 feet of you, as specified in the bond. The bond lasts for 1 hour, and once you forge this bond, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. While bound to a creature in this way, you can use the effect below that corresponds to your coven. You can use this effect a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once) before the bond ends. If either creature dies, the bond ends early.

items.name: Crowsworn & Fish Head Coven
items.entry: You forge this bond with an enemy. When you take damage, you can cause the damage you take to be halved (round down); the bound creature takes the same amount of damage.

items.name: Cloud Cap Coven & The Tall Hats
items.entry: You forge this bond with a willing creature. When you fail a saving throw, you can choose for the bound creature to make the same save and use its result instead. Alternatively, when the bound creature fails a saving throw, you can choose to make the same save and allow it to use your result instead.

items.name: League of the Gilded Gourd & Patchwork Robe Coven
items.entry: You forge this bond with a willing creature. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the bound creature, or cause it to teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you, provided it's willing. Alternatively, when you use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can cause both creatures to teleport, swapping places, provided they're willing and within 60 feet of one another.

subclassFeature.name: Distant Protections
entries: Whenever you take 10 or more damage from an enemy, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to call upon your coven's defensive magic, which they prepare for you each day. You immediately regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 1d10} plus your Charisma modifier, and you gain one of the following benefits of your choice until the end of your next turn.

items: You gain a +5 bonus to AC.
You have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries: This feature is used automatically when you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} but not killed outright. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Voice of the Many
entries: Your important role within your coven has garnered you respect and a modicum of sway within the organization, allowing you to call on powerful coven members and tap into secretive powers. You gain one of the following benefits, determined by your coven. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Fish Head Coven & League of the Gilded Gourd
items.entry: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you briefly become the vessel of a powerful coven member, allowing their magic to flow through you. Choose a level 6 or lower Evocation spell from the {@filter Druid or Wizard|spells|level=!0;!7;!8;!9|class=druid;wizard|school=v} spell list that doesn't require a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cast. As part of the same action, you cast that spell without expending a spell slot or needing Material components.

items.name: Cloud Cap Coven & Crowsworn
items.entry: A trio of witches from your coven share their defensive attributes with you from afar. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, roll three {@dice d6} and assign the numbers rolled as bonuses to your AC and two saving throw bonuses of your choice. This effect lasts for 1 minute.

items.name: Patchwork Robe Coven & The Tall Hats
items.entry: The same magic that binds you to your coven, can also be used to share spells. When you or a creature that you can see is targeted by a spell of level 6 or lower, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cause the spell to also target any other creature of your choice that you can see.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Delivery

entries: Deliverance through delivery.

This is the code of the Courier Brigade, the beloved group of intrepid couriers and courageous knights, who, for the last several centuries, have devoted themselves to the safe delivery of the island's packages and mail. Postal Knights, as these brave individuals have become known as, are renowned for their dedication to their organization, and the people it serves. This dedication, in its truest form, comes with a blessing from the island—delivered as a package of magical gifts that only the greatest of postal knights may receive. These gifts shape the knight, often forming them into the brigade's greatest heroes and granting them the title of Paladin.

entries.name: Historic Line of Knights
entries: The Courier's Tomes, a written history of the Courier Brigade, claims that the first of the postal knights and the four founders of the organization each embodied one of the Paladin's core tenets. These individuals would go on to inspire generations of young Obojimans and craft a movement that profoundly changed the island of Obojima for the better.
This still rings true to this day, as those who strive to be like those individuals are beloved by the people and blessed by the island.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Delivery Spells
entries: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Delivery Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Oath of Delivery Spells
rows: {@spell At Your Side|ObojimaTallGrass}, {@spell Pass without Trace|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Tenets of Delivery
entries: The tenets of the Oath of Delivery Paladin are followed by all postal knights. However, the Paladins who uphold these tenets must never waver, as only the most dedicated of knights are blessed with the Paladin's gifts.

entries.name: Deliverance through Delivery
entries: Always look to serve others before yourself.

entries.name: No Call Unanswered
entries: There is no job too far or path too dangerous to take.

entries.name: Humility Before Conflict
entries: I will not allow my hubris to bring me to conflict with others.

entries.name: Leader of the Bold
entries: I will not abandon my comrades, even if it means my life.

subclassFeature.name: Courier's Seal
entries: Immediately after you hit a creature with an attack, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to place a magical stamp on the target that is visible only to you and creatures that can see invisible objects. Alternatively, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to touch an object as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and stamp it in this way. If the object is being worn or carried by an unwilling creature, that creature can make a Dexterity saving throw, preventing you from placing the stamp on a success; the creature automatically fails the save if it isn't aware of your presence.

The stamp lasts for 1 hour. For the duration, you always know the target's location, provided it's on the same plane of existence as you. While you have this knowledge, the target can't become hidden from you, and if it has the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition, it gains no benefit from that condition against you.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while the target is within 1 mile of you, you can teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of it; if you're riding a steed or Mounted vehicle, it teleports with you (other riders are left behind). The stamp vanishes early if you teleport in this way, if you use this feature again, or if the stamp is targeted by a {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB} spell or similar magic. When the stamp vanishes, these effects end.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Deliverance
entries: You and allies within your Aura of Protection gain the following benefits:

items: {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against you take a penalty to their attack rolls equal to the Paladin's Charisma modifier (minimum of −1). If an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} hits, the damage is reduced by the same amount.
Whenever you gain the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to right yourself, provided your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} isn't 0.

subclassFeature.name: Brigade's Bond
entries: Whenever you cast Divine Smite, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} Radiant damage if one of your allies is within 5 feet of it.

In addition, while a target is stamped by your Courier's Seal, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cast {@spell Scrying|XPHB} without expending a spell slot or needing Material components, targeting the creature or object that bears the stamp. The target automatically fails its save against the spell. If the target is an object, the spell's sensor is created within 10 feet of the target and moves with it. Once you cast the spell in this way, the stamp vanishes.

subclassFeature.name: Paragon of Deliverance
entries: You have become the exemplary model of a postal knight, which the island has rewarded. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can imbue your Aura of Protection with power, gaining the following benefits for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

items.name: Brigadier's Mark
items.entry: Your Courier's Seal feature doesn't require you to expend a use of your Channel Divinity to use it. In addition, whenever one of your allies in the aura hits a creature with a melee attack, you can place a stamp on the target (no action required), as if by your Courier's Seal feature.

items.name: Captain's Sacrifice
items.entry: Enemies within the aura have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against your allies.

items.name: Courier's Cavalry
items.entry: When you use this feature, and at the start of each of your turns for the duration, you can cause each Medium or smaller creature of your choice in the aura to immediately become mounted on its own spectral steed (using the statistics of a {@creature Riding Horse|XMM} from the {@spell Phantom Steed|XPHB} spell), provided the creature is willing. If one of these steeds takes damage, and it isn't in your Aura of Protection, the rider is forced to dismount, and the steed immediately disappears.

item.name: Airbag Shield
entries: While holding this Shield, you can cast the {@spell Airbag|ObojimaTalesYatamon} spell from it, targeting only yourself. Once the spell is cast in this way, it can't be cast from the Shield again until the next dawn. A creature can also restore the item's use of this spell by touching the Shield as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and expending a level 1+ spell slot.

item.name: Bubble Blowtorch
entries: These First Age torches have been magically altered to use potions as their fuel. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can pour a potion of any rarity into the glass vessel of a Brewer's Torch. As long as a potion is in the vessel, you can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to activate the torch's corresponding effect, as detailed below, consuming the potion from the vessel.

entries.name: Bubble Blowtorch
entries: A stream of glistening bubbles floats from the tip of the torch, coating a loose object within 5 feet of you. If the object weighs 100 pounds or fewer, the bubbles lift it up to 10 feet into the air. The object hovers in place for 1 minute or until you choose to end the effect (no action required), after which the bubbles disappear and the object falls. While the object is hovering, it can be moved as if it weighed no more than 5 pounds, and if weight is added to the object that would bring it over 100 pounds, it falls.

item.name: Butterfly Blowtorch
entries: These First Age torches have been magically altered to use potions as their fuel. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can pour a potion of any rarity into the glass vessel of a Brewer's Torch. As long as a potion is in the vessel, you can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to activate the torch's corresponding effect, as detailed below, consuming the potion from the vessel.

entries.name: Butterfly Blowtorch
entries: A flutter of colorful butterflies pours from the tip of the torch, swarming a creature or object within 5 feet of you. If the target is a creature, one effect causing it to have the {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, or {@condition Pacified|ObojimaTallGrass} condition (your choice) ends. If the target is an object, the butterflies repair a single break or tear in it, as if by the {@spell Mending|XPHB} cantrip.

item.name: Water Jet Blowtorch
entries: These First Age torches have been magically altered to use potions as their fuel. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can pour a potion of any rarity into the glass vessel of a Brewer's Torch. As long as a potion is in the vessel, you can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to activate the torch's corresponding effect, as detailed below, consuming the potion from the vessel.

entries.name: Water Jet Blowtorch
entries: A jet of water blasts from the tip of the torch at a target within 15 feet of you. If the target is a creature, it must make a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 2d4} Slashing damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. If the target is an object or surface made of metal, stone, or wood that is no more than 1 foot thick, the water cuts a {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} through it up to 5 feet long and 1 inch wide, provided it isn't being worn or carried.

item.name: Demon Rattle
entries: While this rattle is on your person, you have a +1 bonus to saving throws against effects created by Demons (Fiends).

As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can shake this rattle. At the end of your turn while shaking it, each Demon in a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw, provided it can hear the rattle and isn't already affected by it. On a failed save, the Demon has the {@condition Pacified|ObojimaTallGrass} condition. This effect ends on an affected Demon if you don't take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action on your turn to continue shaking the rattle, if the Demon takes any damage, or if the Demon can no longer hear the rattle. Once you stop shaking the rattle, ending this effect, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

item.name: Healing Patch
entries: You can attach up to three Healing Patches to your clothing or equipment over the course of 1 hour. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to rip a patch off your person and regain {@damage 1d8 + 3} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}; doing so destroys the patch and leaves a charred mark in its place. If you have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition, an ally within reach of you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to rip the patch off your person instead.

item.name: Healing Patch (2nd Class)
entries: You can attach up to three Healing Patches to your clothing or equipment over the course of 1 hour. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to rip a patch off your person and regain {@damage 2d8 + 6} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}; doing so destroys the patch and leaves a charred mark in its place. If you have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition, an ally within reach of you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to rip the patch off your person instead.

item.name: Healing Patch (1st Class)
entries: You can attach up to three Healing Patches to your clothing or equipment over the course of 1 hour. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to rip a patch off your person and regain {@damage 4d8 + 12} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}; doing so destroys the patch and leaves a charred mark in its place. If you have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition, an ally within reach of you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to rip the patch off your person instead.

item.name: Soda (Cursed)
entries: This soda is cursed. Consuming it curses you until you are targeted by a level 5+ {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic, or until you consume a pound of {@item Black Cinnamon|ObojimaTallGrass} and bathe in a still pool of water.

Each day while cursed, at a random time, one random spell slot you have or one random spell that can be cast from a magic item you are attuned to is expended (GM's discretion). If you have no spell slots or applicable magic items available, you instead take {@damage 2d10} Necrotic damage.

item.name: Press Pass
entries: While holding this Press Pass, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to press it against a wooden, plaster, or stone surface (such as a wall, ceiling, or floor) that is no more than 5 feet thick. When you do so, you open a doorway on the surface, creating a passage to the other side that is 3 feet wide and 7 feet tall. The passage remains for 10 minutes or until you take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to touch the Press Pass, at which point it closes and the doorway disappears, leaving behind no trace.
Once used, the Press Pass can't be used in this way again until the next dawn.

item.name: Welders Shawl
entries: While wearing this shawl, you gain a +3 bonus to Intelligence ({@skill Mechanics|ObojimaTallGrass}) checks. In addition, whenever you repair a vehicle, it regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the result of the check –5 (minimum of 3 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}), instead of –10.

item.name: Whiskered Nakurina
entries: While playing this nakurina, you can attempt to manipulate a Demon's actions at the risk of your own well-being. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, choose a Demon (Fiend) that can hear the nakurina and make a Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check. The Demon must then succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against a DC equal to the result of your check (maximum {@dc 20}). On a failed save, you choose whether the Demon drops an item of your choice, moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} in a direction of your choice, or makes an attack against a creature of your choice within {@b 5 feet} of it. On a successful save, the Demon resists your control, and you take {@damage 2d4} Psychic damage.

item.name: Canned Cat
entries: Much like soda slimes, this peculiar cat-shaped creature—aptly named the canned cat—is known to form inside colorful metal cans, which are kept pristine by the magics of the First Age and Obojima. You can find canned cats all over the island in old storehouses, convenience stores, and pantries.

item.name: Slice of Melon Bird
entries: If you plan to use melon bird in a potion recipe, you'll have to be quick, as the moment you slice into the creature, its magic begins to fade. Most witches believe you have less than an hour to use melon bird in a potion, but that has never been confirmed.

item.name: Dried Pilot Leech
entries: Dried Pilot Leech is hard to come by, as collecting the nasty thing can be quite a harrowing task. Because of this, most witches leave the hunting of pilot leeches to adventurers and thrill seekers.

item.name: Tamh Gon's Confetti
entries: In Yatamon, Tamh Gon's Confetti can be found littered across the streets for months after his arrival, and the enigmatic festival spirit never stays away too long, making his confetti as common as fallen leaves.

item.name: Hair From a Yanari
entries: A pluck of yanari hair is a versatile ingredient that can be used in dozens of potions recipes. However, you won't find many witches using it, as the magical properties of the hair are a trade secret held closely by the vendors of the Yanari Market.

images.title: Airbag shields can be incredibly fickle to reset.
Crafted with Mu's blessed green clay.

itemGroup.name: Brewer's Torch
entries: These First Age torches have been magically altered to use potions as their fuel. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can pour a potion of any rarity into the glass vessel of a Brewer's Torch. As long as a potion is in the vessel, you can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to activate the torch's corresponding effect, as detailed below, consuming the potion from the vessel.

itemGroup.name: Healing Patches
entries: You can attach up to three Healing Patches to your clothing or equipment over the course of 1 hour. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to rip a patch off your person and regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}; doing so destroys the patch and leaves a charred mark in its place. If you have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition, an ally within reach of you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to rip the patch off your person instead.
The number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} you regain when the patch is ripped off depends on the patch's rarity.

weapon.name: Ramming
entries: A creature controlling a vehicle can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to attempt to ram a target with the vehicle; this can't be attempted more than once per turn. If the target is a creature, it can make a Dexterity saving throw to avoid the vehicle; the DC for the save equals 8 plus the controlling creature's Dexterity or Intelligence modifier (its choice) and the vehicle's Size Modifier.

If the vehicle moved at least 10 feet in a straight line immediately before successfully ramming a target, the target takes {@damage 4d6} Bludgeoning damage. The target takes twice as much damage if the vehicle moved at least 20 feet before ramming it, or three times as much damage if the vehicle moved 30 feet or more before ramming it.

Immediately after the vehicle rams a Small or larger target, the vehicle's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced (as detailed in the {@variantrule Vehicle|ObojimaTalesYatamon|Controlling a Vehicle} section), and the vehicle takes {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it moved before ramming its target, to a maximum of {@damage 3d6}. This damage ignores the vehicle's {@variantrule Damage Threshold|XPHB}.

entries.name: Classification: Piloted
entries: The vehicle requires a creature to enter it in order to operate it. Creatures inside this vehicle have {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover}.

entries.name: Aquatic
entries: This vehicle can only move in the water.

entries.name: Wide
entries: When ramming a creature using this vehicle, each creature within 5 feet of the target must also make the Dexterity saving throw.

vehicleFluff.name: The Doomspine
entries: The Lionfish King's floating menace, the Doomspine, is a shoddily constructed vessel that he uses to raid and intimidate the western coast of the island. Made to resemble the top half of a sailship, which he had constructed from stolen docks and pillaged lumber, and the base of a First Age tug boat, the Doomspine is clunky looking, to say the least. Nevertheless, the ship is the most successful of any craft the Lionfish King has created—surviving numerous encounters with Captain Clintock's Pointue and emerging victorious in more than one of them.

images.title: An original drawing of the first Pointue, which features the nose spine that now decorates the Doomspine.

vehicleFluff.name: Flying Broom
entries: Cost: 500 GF

Flying brooms are a popular form of transportation for witches, wizards, and merchants across Obojima—the most common of which don't move faster than a walking pace and tend to lose stability at higher elevations. Faster brooms are often more valuable, as they take quite a bit of skill and understanding to craft. The highest-quality brooms are made in Yatamon, though many besom makers and broom squires in small towns and villages might disagree.

images.title: The recognizable sound of broom bells are used to notify those nearby that the rider is landing. The bustle/head is made from finely crafted Shuro (Hemp Palm) or collections of old fabric; on very fine brooms, Sheep Dragon Wool is used instead.

vehicleFluff.name: Trolley
entries: Trolleys, or street cars, aren't well known outside of Yatamon and are commonly confused with the iconic Wandering Line, or "spirit train" as some people refer to it. Within the city, the Municipal Trolley Line functions as a beloved service that the people cherish and use often. Beyond the city limits, there are trolleys found throughout the island; however, many of them, if not all, are used in other manners besides transportation, usually as places of business or shelter.

vehicleFluff.name: Flying Lantern
entries: The flying lantern of the Courier Brigade is well known by the people of Obojima and is considered by many to be the most iconic flying machine on the island—soaring above other notable crafts such as Rock Raley's glider or the Crowsworn's "Whirling Flock." The lantern itself is used sparingly by the postal knights due to its unorthodox fuel source, which makes its departure and arrival within the city that much more of a spectacle. When the lantern is used, it's often to deliver special packages, to send quick aid to knights in the field, or to participate in one of the many festivals that the Courier Brigade takes part in. Though the organization technically has two identical lanterns, only one is ever flown at a time to conserve the large candle that is used to power the lantern.

entries.name: Kyojin Candle
entries: The large candle that fuels the flying lantern is known as a Kyojin Candle, and it has been crafted in Yatamon by the Courier Brigade for just over three decades. The candles themselves are formed from a special pink wax used in potion brewing and certain traditional ceremonies held in the Gift of Shuritashi. The arcane properties that make the wax effective in potion brewing also make it ideal for the Kyojin Candle. After intricately braiding and weaving enchantments into the candle's wick, the waxwork practitioners of the Courier Brigade pour thin layers of wax into the Kyojin mold, sealing glyphs of Evocation magic each time. The practice of crafting a Kyojin Candle is held closely by the brigade, and the act of making one can take up to a year to complete.

images.title: Going "up a wick" or "down a wick" commonly refers to the pilot of a flying lantern lighting or extinguishing one of the Kyojin candles' three core wicks. Doing so will add or remove heat from the lantern's interior and cause the lantern to gain or lose elevation accordingly. As the Kyojin candle burns away, a crank and gear system can be used to raise the candle's height and maintain the needed heat in the core of the lantern.

vehicleFluff.name: The Pointue
entries: Captain Clintock's swordfish submersible, the Pointue, has explored the Shallows in some form or another for the last twenty years. It was created by the captain and his late wife, Kara, shortly after the two established the Mariners' Guild. Originally, the vessel was crafted from a dense wood, which was supported by internal steel plates and sealed with Yugi Sap°. This version of the Pointue sailed for just under four years before the Lionfish King sank it off the western coastline. Since then, the Pointue has been altered and upgraded by the Clintock family, with its newest form being the most advanced and capable iteration yet. Now the Pointue can dive indefinitely thanks to supportive magics. Its steel casing makes it the most defensible vehicle on the island, and the craft's swift form and spear-like nose ensure it is a formidable force against other ships and large creatures.

images.title: Although it's not desired, the Pointue's sharpened nose spike is designed in such a way that breaking it off in battle would not cause the submersible to sink.
The Pointue's interior features many First Age wonders, but none are as precious to Captain Clintock as his library of First Age books and film.

vehicleFluff.name: K-Truck
entries: Cost: 2,500 GF
This mini truck, also known as a kei truck, is often the prized possession of whomever is lucky enough to obtain one.

vehicleFluff.name: Small Car
entries: Cost: 2,000 GF
Because they're less common, cars are appreciated by most Obojimans, especially if they're visually unique.

vehicleFluff.name: Motorcycle
entries: Cost: 3,000 GF
Motorcycles are coveted by farmers and other tradespeople due to their speed and power, which make them a versatile tool in the field or when delivering goods.

vehicleFluff.name: Scooter / Vespa
entries: Cost: 500 GF
Scooters and Vespas are most commonly used in towns and villages with First Age roads or smooth paths.

vehicleFluff.name: Bicycle
entries: Cost: 50 GF
Bicycles are the most common vehicle found on the island due to the ease with which craftspeople can recreate them.

condition.name: Flipped
entries: A vehicle with the Flipped condition is one that is upside down, turned on its side, or otherwise unable to move in its current orientation. A Flipped vehicle has a Combat and Travel Speed of 0. A creature within 5 feet of a Flipped vehicle can take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to attempt to reorient the vehicle with a Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check. The DC for the check is based on the vehicle's Size Modifier: 1 ({@dc 10}), 2 ({@dc 20}), 3 ({@dc 30}), or 4+ ({@dc 40}).

If more than one creature attempts to reorient the vehicle simultaneously, each creature makes the required Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check, reducing the DC by 1 for each creature participating. As long as one creature succeeds on the check, the vehicle is reoriented. When a vehicle is reoriented, it returns to its proper orientation and loses the Flipped condition.

condition.name: Immobile
entries: If a vehicle is subjected to an effect that would cause the target to have the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} or {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition, it instead gains this condition and has a Combat and Travel Speed of 0. If the effect would normally allow the target to make an ability check or saving throw to end the imposed condition, the creature controlling the vehicle can instead take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to make a Maneuvering check against the effect's save DC. On a success, this condition ends on the vehicle.

condition.name: Locked
entries: Unlocking a vehicle with the Locked condition requires a creature within 5 feet of the vehicle's locked entry point to take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action. If the creature uses the appropriate key, the vehicle automatically loses that condition. Without the key, a creature can use {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB} to attempt to pick the lock with a {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check, causing the vehicle to lose the Locked condition on a success.

condition.name: Uncontrolled
entries: A vehicle has the Uncontrolled condition if it is in motion but no Crew are controlling the vehicle's movement. This can happen if the creature controlling the vehicle doesn't take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to continue operating it, either by choice or involuntarily (such as if it has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition).

When a vehicle gains the Uncontrolled condition, it continues moving in the same direction and at the same speed that it moved on the last turn that a creature was controlling it. On that creature's turn each subsequent round, the vehicle moves 10 fewer feet in that direction than it did the previous round until it is no longer moving.
A vehicle loses the Uncontrolled condition when it stops moving or when a creature regains control of the vehicle.

trait.name: Deft Cover
entries: While at least two Small or larger creatures (excluding the awakened cat) are within 5 feet of the awakened cat, it has {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover}.

trait.name: Feline Agility
entries: When the awakened cat falls and doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, it always lands on its feet, and it can subtract up to 20 feet from the fall when calculating the damage it would take.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The awakened cat makes two attacks, using its Dagger or Shortsword in any combination.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Shortsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) Piercing damage.

reaction.name: Nimble Redirect
entries: {@actTrigger} The awakened cat is hit by an attack made with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. {@actResponse} It reduces the damage it takes by 5, and it can cause a creature or object within 5 feet of it to take 5 damage of the attack's type.

trait.name: Master Canden's Discipline
entries: The student has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws it makes to avoid or end the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

trait.name: Master Moon's Footwork
entries: When an enemy the student can see within 10 feet of it misses with a melee attack roll, the student can move up to 5 feet without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

trait.name: Vigilant
entries: When the student rolls {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, it can immediately draw a weapon and move up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} (no action required).

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The student makes two Training Blade attacks.

action.name: Training Blade
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) Piercing damage.

reaction.name: Parrying Blade
entries: {@actTrigger} The student is hit by an attack roll. {@actResponse} The student adds 5 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

trait.name: Secretary's Swiftness
entries: While mounted, the postal knight has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws and on any ability check it makes to remain mounted.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The postal knight makes two attacks, using Field Spear, Longsword, or Light Crossbow in any combination. Alternatively, the postal knight can make its mount attack twice.

action.name: Field Spear
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/90 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Longsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Light Crossbow
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 4} to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) Piercing damage.

bonus.name: Package Snatch
