entries: While mounted, the postal knight picks up and carries an ally or object within its reach that weighs no more than 250 pounds, provided it has a hand free to grab the target; the target's weight counts toward the mount's carrying capacity rather than the postal knight's. If the target is an object that is being worn or carried by an unwilling creature, that creature can make a {@dc 13} Strength or Dexterity saving throw (it chooses which), preventing the object from being taken on a success. The postal knight can choose to release the target at any time (no action required.)

reaction.name: Brother in Arms
entries: {@actTrigger} A friendly creature within 5 feet of the postal knight takes damage. {@actResponse} The postal knight and the target each take half of the damage dealt, splitting the damage between them.

entries.name: HP below 25
entries: The postal knight moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} if mounted, toward an enemy. If the postal knight ends this movement within 5 feet of an enemy it can make a melee attack against that creature. {@hom} that creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll it makes against the postal knight before the end of its next turn.

entries.name: HP below 5
entries: The postal knight dismounts (if it's mounted) and it commands its mount to immediately move up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

trait.name: Confidence in Numbers
entries: The scout has a +2 bonus to its attack rolls while it can see at least 2 of its allies.

action.name: Baseball Bat
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3} (with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} if the target is a Demon [Fiend]) to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage, or 8 ({@damage 2d6 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage if the target is a Demon (Fiend).

action.name: Sling
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 3} (with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} if the target is a Demon [Fiend]) to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage, or 6 ({@damage 2d4 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage if the target is a Demon (Fiend).

bonus.name: Quick Thinking
entries: The scout takes the {@action Influence|XPHB}, {@action Search|XPHB}, or {@action Study|XPHB} action.

reaction.name: Near Miss
entries: {@actTrigger} The scout is hit by an attack roll. {@actResponse} The damage the scout takes from that attack is reduced by 3.

variant.name: Traps
entries: If the Yoka Scout was prepared for this fight, they may have set a simple but well-hidden booby trap before the battle began, gaining the Reaction option detailed below. This trap can be mechanical, magical, or some combination of the two. It is no larger than a 5-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube}, and it can be hidden on any solid surface that is large enough for it. No matter what the trap may be, it requires a successful DC 13 Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check to discern its presence.

{@actTrigger} A creature enters the area within 5 feet of the scout's trap. {@actResponse}-{@actSave dex} {@dc 13}, 13, the triggering creature. {@actSaveFail} The creature takes 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Bludgeoning damage or has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the start of its next turn (the scout's choice). {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} The trap is then rendered inert.

trait.name: Distant Mimicry
entries: The crow can mimic simple sounds it has heard, such as a whisper or chitter, creating the sound at a point of its choice within 30 feet of itself. A hearer can discern that the sounds are imitations with a successful {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check.

trait.name: Trinket Obsession
entries: The crow is mesmerized by a specific Tiny object (GM's choice), such as a coin, button, or bauble. The crow has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) checks that involve that object.

spellcasting.name: Chattering Charm
headerEntries: The crow casts {@spell Charm Person|XPHB}, requiring no Somatic component and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 10}). The spell ends early if the crow uses this action again. If a target's saving throw is successful or the spell ends for it, that target is immune to the Chattering Charm of all Button Crows for the next 24 hours.

spellcasting.name: Trickery
headerEntries: The crow casts {@spell Duplicate|ObojimaTallGrass}, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 10}).

bonus.name: Consume Trinket
entries: The crow consumes the object from its Trinket Obsession. If the object is nonmagical, it is destroyed, and the crow gains 3 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

trait.name: Mesmerize
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 11} Any creature that starts its turn within 5 feet of the canned cat and is aware of it. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition until the start of its next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to the canned cat's Mesmerize for 24 hours.

trait.name: Too Sweet To Eat
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 10} A creature that consumes the canned cat. {@actSaveFail} The target gains 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level.

trait.name: Reactive Heads
entries: The hydra has four extra {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} that can be used only for {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

trait.name: Ooze Concoction
entries: At the start of each of the hydra's turns, one of the following potion types of its choice bubbles to the top, determining its form:

items.name: Combat
entries: The hydra has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} until the start of its next turn.

items.name: Utility
entries: The hydra sprouts legs from its cauldron, gaining a {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of 30 feet. It then creates four illusory copies of itself (as if from the {@spell Minor Illusion|XPHB} spell; save {@dc 13}) in unoccupied spaces within 30 feet of it, which appear to have walked there. The effects end at the start of the hydra's next turn.

items.name: Whimsy
entries: When the hydra hits a creature with a Pseudopod attack, roll a {@dice d4} to determine the effect it's subjected to; the target can't be subjected to another effect in this way for 24 hours:

items: For the next hour, the target is under the effects of the {@spell Feather Fall|XPHB} spell and weighs no more than 1 pound.

The target transforms into the child version of itself for 4 hours: it is one size smaller (to a minimum of Small), and its Strength and Dexterity scores are 10 unless those scores were already lower.

One random object the target is wearing or carrying is assigned a signature sound that accompanies the object when it's used. This effect lasts until removed as if a curse by the {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell
For the next hour, the target's speech sounds like that of a random person it's not familiar with.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The hydra makes five Pseudopod attacks. If it's in Utility form, it can use its Transposition after each attack.

action.name: Pseudopod
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4} (with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} in Combat form) to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Acid damage.

action.name: Dragon's Breath (Combat Form Only)
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 13} Each creature in a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} The target takes 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Acid damage, 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Cold damage, 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Fire damage, 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Lightning damage, and 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Poison damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

action.name: Transposition (Utility Form Only)
entries: The hydra teleports, imperceptibly swapping places with one of its illusory copies, which appears in its previous space.

reaction.name: Polymorph (Whimsy Form Only)
entries: {@actTrigger} An enemy touches the hydra or hits it with a melee attack roll. {@actResponse} {@actSave wis} {@dc 13} The triggering creature. {@actSaveFail} The target magically transforms (as if by the {@spell Polymorph|XPHB} spell; no {@status Concentration|XPHB} required) into a {@creature Frog|XMM} until the end of its next turn.

monster.name: Graffiti Golem
languages: Understands Common plus one other language but can't speak

trait.name: Death Burst
entries: The golem bursts when it dies, covering surfaces in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} with magical paint for 1 minute. {@actSave dex} {@dc 13} Each creature that moves across a surface in the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there. {@actSaveFail} The target leaves a visible paint trail where it moves for {@dice 1d12} hours. A creature can remove the paint by dousing the target in water or by manually clearing it off over the course of 1 minute.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: If the golem is motionless at the start of combat, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on its {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll. Moreover, if a creature hasn't observed the golem move or act, that creature must succeed on a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check to discern that the golem isn't ordinary graffiti.

trait.name: Golem Sense
entries: The creature that created the golem can perceive through its senses, as long as they are on the same plane of existence.

trait.name: Immutable Form
entries: The golem can't shapeshift.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The golem has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Two-Dimensional Movement
entries: The golem can only move across solid contiguous surfaces. It doesn't fill the space it is occupying (except with regard to other graffiti golems).

trait.name: Water Susceptibility
entries: The golem takes 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Cold damage for every 5 feet it moves in water or for every gallon of water splashed on it.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The golem makes two Rend attacks.

action.name: Rend
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 0 ft. (one target touching the surface the golem is on), one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d6 + 4}) Slashing damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Force damage.

action.name: Graffiti Spray {@recharge 5}
entries: A flurry of colors trails along all surfaces emanating from the golem, leaving a rainbow pattern behind. {@actSave dex} {@dc 13} Each creature touching a solid surface in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Acid, Cold, Fire, or Lightning damage (roll a {@dice d4} to determine the type for each target). {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

trait.name: Ambusher
entries: In the first round of a combat, the howler has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against any creature that is {@status Surprised|XPHB}.

trait.name: Common Mimicry
entries: The howler can mimic speech that sounds like Common (but isn't). A hearer can discern that the speech is an imitation with a successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check.

trait.name: Deceptive Appearance
entries: If a creature hasn't discerned the howler for what it is, that creature must take a {@action Study|XPHB} action and succeed on a {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check to discern that the howler isn't a Humanoid ({@creature Commoner|XMM}); the creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this check if it's within 30 feet of the howler.

trait.name: Sleep-Deprived
entries: The howler has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws it makes to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} conditions.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The howler makes two attacks, using Chomp, Dagger, or Hand Crossbow in any combination. It can forgo one attack to take the {@action Hide|XPHB} action.

action.name: Chomp
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) Piercing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Poison damage.

action.name: Hand Crossbow
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 5} to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) Piercing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Poison damage.

bonus.name: Deft Escape
entries: The howler takes the {@action Dash|XPHB} or {@action Disengage|XPHB} action.

reaction.name: Discouraging Chuckle
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature misses the howler with an attack. {@actResponse} The next time the attacker makes an ability check or an attack roll before the end of its next turn, it must subtract {@dice 1d4} from the total.

entries.name: HP below 15
entries: The howler can immediately attempt to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving, making an ability check or saving throw as needed. If able, it then moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

trait.name: Emotional
entries: The living memory can use its Impulsive Reactions (triggered by its Disposition) without taking a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

trait.name: Not Yourself (Fury Only)
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 13} The first creature the living memory deals damage to each turn. {@actSaveFail} The target must take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on its next turn.

trait.name: Overwhelming Aura (Joy Only)
entries: {@actSave int} {@dc 15} The first time a creature sees the living memory on each of its turns. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Pacified|XPHB} condition until the end of its turn.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The living memory makes two Slam attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d10 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Mental Haze {@recharge 6}
entries: The living memory emits a near-undetectable mental static that passes over nearby creatures. {@actSave wis} {@dc 13} Each creature of the living memory's choice in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the living memory. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. While {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition and a {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of 0. The effect ends for the target if it takes any damage or if another creature uses an action to shake the creature out of its stupor.

bonus.name: Misery Loves Company (Sorrow Only)
entries: The living memory creates a statuelike copy of itself in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of it. This copy is immobile and is easily understood to be a lifeless duplicate. The copy can be dispelled as if it were created by a level 3 spell, and it's destroyed after 1 hour or when it takes 10 or more damage from a single source. The living memory gains a +1 bonus to all its save DCs for each of its copies within 300 feet of it, to a maximum of {@dc 16}.

entries.name: HP below 90
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 15} Last creature dealt damage when this Impulsive Reaction was triggered. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition for 1 minute.

entries.name: HP below 75
entries: The save DC for Overwhelming Aura decreases to 14.

entries.name: HP below 60
entries: The living memory cast {@spell Otto's Irresistible Dance|XPHB|Irresistible Dance}, using Constitution as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 14}); when cast in this way, the spell doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

entries.name: HP below 45
entries: The save DC for Overwhelming Aura decreases to 13.

entries.name: HP below 30
entries: The living memory uses Mental Haze and then moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. Creatures affected by this version of Mental Haze dance in place while {@condition Charmed|XPHB}.

entries.name: HP below 10
entries: The living memory moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: HP below 90
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 13} Each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the living memory. {@actSaveFail} On the target's next turn, it can take either an action of a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, not both.

entries.name: HP below 75
entries: The living memory immediately uses its Misery Loves Company ability twice.

entries.name: HP below 60
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 13} The creature that reduced the living memory past this Threshold. {@actSaveFail} The target gains 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level.

entries.name: HP below 45
entries: The living memory moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and takes the {@action Hide|XPHB} action.

entries.name: HP below 30
entries: Each enemy in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from The living memory and its statue-like copies takes a -10 penalty to its {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count for the resto of the combat.

entries.name: HP below 10
entries: The living memory moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: HP below 90
entries: The living memory moves up to half its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and makes one Slam attack.

entries.name: HP below 75
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 13} Each creature in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the living memory. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: HP below 60
entries: The creature that reduced the living memory past this Threshold takes 16 ({@damage 3d10}) Psychic damage. Until the end of the living memory's next turn, that creature has {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to damage dealt by the living memory.

entries.name: HP below 45
entries: The living memory makes up to three Slam attacks against objects and structures within its reach.

entries.name: HP below 30
entries: The living memory moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and makes a Slam attack against up to two different targets.

entries.name: HP below 10
entries: The living memory moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} toward the enemy that has the fewest {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} within that distance and then makes a Slam attack against it.

trait.name: Hold Breath
entries: The turtle can hold its breath for 2 hours.

trait.name: Prone Susceptibility
entries: If the turtle has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition on land, it can't move. To end the condition, it must spend all of its movement to right itself, rather than an amount equal to half its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

trait.name: Radiant Illumination
entries: The turtle sheds {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 30-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 30 feet. A creature that starts its turn in the {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} or enters the area for the first time on a turn takes 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Radiant damage. The turtle can choose to produce only its {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in a 30-foot radius or resume shedding its {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} (no action required).

trait.name: Realm Projection
entries: While the turtle is only shedding {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}, it can choose to project an illusory copy of the Spirit Realm where it overlaps the turtle's {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}, including creatures and objects on that plane. It is clear that the projection is an illusion, retaining a faint warm glow from the turtle's light.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The turtle makes two attacks, using Chomp or Lantern Bolt in any combination.

action.name: Chomp
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d8}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Lantern Bolt
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 4} to hit, range 60 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d6}) Radiant damage.

action.name: Repelling Flare
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 12} Each creature within the turtle's {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Pacified|XPHB} condition until the end of the turtle's next turn. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} The turtle's Radiant Illumination trait ceases to function until the end of its next turn, and it can't use its Lantern Bolt for the duration.

bonus.name: Aggressive Rotation
entries: While in the water, the turtle automatically escapes from up to two grapples. {@actSave dex} {@dc 13} The grapplers. {@actSaveFail} 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

trait.name: Death Burst
entries: The melon bird explodes when it dies, creating {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} in a 5-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} on the ground below it, which lasts for 1 minute. When a creature moves into or within this {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} for the first time on a turn, it must succeed on a {@dc 11} Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: If the melon bird is motionless at the start of combat, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on its {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll. Moreover, if a creature hasn't observed the melon bird move or act, that creature must succeed on a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check to discern that the melon bird isn't an ordinary melon.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature and the melon bird moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

bonus.name: Seed Flourish {@recharge 4}
entries: The melon bird spins rapidly, spitting seeds around itself. {@actSave dex} {@dc 11} Each creature in a 5-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the melon bird. {@actSaveFail} The target takes 1 Bludgeoning damage. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} The target can't make an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} against the melon bird for the rest of the turn.

monster.name: Pilot Leech
languages: Understands Common and Torum but can't speak

trait.name: Bestial Shroud
entries: Beasts have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks to detect the leech.

action.name: Infect
entries: {@actSave int} {@dc 11} One Beast within 5 feet of the leech. {@actSaveFail} The leech attaches itself to the target, infecting it. The leech controls the target, and can't be targeted by any attack or effect. They share the statistics of an infected beast but temporarily retain the Beast's original size; its size increases by one category every 24 hours until it is Gargantuan.

trait.name: Demonic Control
entries: If the infected beast dies, its pilot leech detaches and takes a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. If the leech dies, the Beast is no longer infected, and it drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} but is {@variantrule Stable|XPHB}. A Beast that is no longer infected returns to its normal form over the course of 30 days.

trait.name: Kojo Aversion
entries: If the infected beast consumes an entire {@item Kojo Root|ObojimaTallGrass}, its pilot leech is repulsed. {@actSave con} {@dc 10} The infected beast. {@actSaveFail} The pilot leech immediately detaches.

trait.name: Leech Weakness
entries: The pilot leech attached to the infected beast has its own pool of 10 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. It can't be targeted directly, but if the infected beast is subjected to Psychic damage, the leech takes that damage instead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The infected beast makes two Natural Weapon attacks.

action.name: Natural Weapon
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}22 ({@damage 4d8 + 4}) Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage (as appropriate for the infected beast).

trait.name: Insatiable Appetite
entries: If the swarm ends its turn in the same space it started, it can choose to consume any Medium or smaller nonmagical objects of its choice in a 5-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} within 5 feet of it, provided they aren't being worn or carried. If an object is larger than that (such as a wall or a door), it eats through a 5-{@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} portion of the object, but it stops if it eats through 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; or 1 inch of metal. If an object is destroyed in this way, the swarm regains 3 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

trait.name: Spry Body
entries: Nonmagical {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} doesn't cost the swarm extra movement.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny mouse. The swarm can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, except via its Insatiable Appetite and Deteriorate abilities.

action.name: Chomps
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d8 + 2}) Piercing damage—or 6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) Piercing damage if the swarm is {@status Bloodied|XPHB}—plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Necrotic damage.

action.name: Static
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 4} to hit, range 15 ft., one target. {@h}14 ({@damage 4d6}) Lightning damage, or 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Lightning damage if the swarm is {@status Bloodied|XPHB}.

action.name: Deteriorate {@recharge 6}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 12} Each creature and structure in a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the swarm. {@actSaveFail} 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Necrotic damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} If a structure collapses due to this damage, the swarm gains 10 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

trait.name: Leaping Glide
entries: While the bird is falling and doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, it descends at a rate of 10 feet per round and can travel up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} horizontally, and it takes no damage from the fall.

trait.name: Sturdy
entries: The bird has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and to avoid being pushed, pulled, or otherwise moved against its will.

action.name: Stomp
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d10 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature and the bird moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. {@hom} The bird doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} for the rest of the turn.

entries.name: HP below 15
entries: The bird jumps up to 20 feet in the air. It then glides up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, as per its Leaping Glide trait. It can end this movement eartly to slam back to the ground, kicking up a cloud of dust. Each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the bird must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of the bir's next turn.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The siphon fish can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Arcane Siphon
entries: At the start of each of the siphon fish's turns while it's attached to a creature, it attempts to drain some magical essence. {@actSave con} {@dc 12} The target that the siphon fish is attached to. {@actSaveFail} The target loses one random spell slot or one use of a random spell it can cast a limited number of times per day, and the siphon fish gains a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the level of the spell slot or spell lost. If the target has no spell slots or spells available to lose, it instead gains 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level, and the siphon fish immediately detaches.

trait.name: Magic Sense
entries: The siphon fish can sense the presence of magical effects, as if by a {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} spell, as far as it can see.

action.name: Attach
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Piercing damage, and the siphon fish attaches to the target. While the siphon fish is attached, it can't make Attach attacks, the target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet, and the magical properties of the target's {@filter Uncommon|items|rarity=uncommon} and {@filter Common|items|rarity=common} magic items don't work. The siphon fish can detach itself by spending 5 feet of movement. The target or a creature within 5 feet of it can take an action to try to detach the siphon fish, doing so by succeeding on a {@dc 14} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check.

action.name: Consume Spell
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 12} One creature within 5 feet of the siphon fish that is currently under the effects of a spell; if the siphon fish is attached to a creature, it must target that creature with this effect. {@actSaveFail} The spell immediately ends on the target, and the siphon fish gains a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the spell's level.

trait.name: Blind
entries: The stalker always has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition. It doesn't suffer the effects of this condition against creatures within the area of its {@sense Blindsight|XPHB}.

trait.name: Doku Moss
entries: While the stalker is on a ceiling, a tendril of this moss hangs down in a 20-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} below the stalker. While the stalker is on the ground, the moss instead curls around it in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. The stalker has {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} in the moss's area. If a creature hasn't observed the stalker move or act, that creature must succeed on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check to discern the stalker's presence within the moss.

trait.name: Poison Fetters
entries: While the stalker is on the ground, the area of the stalker's Doku Moss is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} for creatures unless they have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

trait.name: Poison Pillar
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 13} A creature that enters the area of the stalker's Doku Moss while the stalker is hanging from the ceiling (a creature with {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition automatically succeeds on this save). {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition, and it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The stalker can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an Ability Check.

action.name: Chomp
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) Piercing damage plus 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Poison damage. If the target has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition, it also gains 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level. A creature that gains {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} from a spindle stalker's Chomp can't gain it again in this way for 24 hours.

action.name: Tendril Tracking
entries: While on the ground, the stalker whips its moss around itself to detect and hinder nearby creatures. {@actSave dex} {@dc 13} Each creature in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} (a creature with {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition automatically succeeds on this save). {@actSaveFail} The target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved until the end of its next turn. {@actSaveFailBy 5} The target also has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition for the duration. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} Until the end of the stalker's turn, it has {@variantrule Blindsight|XPHB} in the area; its {@variantrule Blindsight|XPHB} returns to normal if it leaves the area.

trait.name: Festival Aura
entries: Tamh Gon produces an aura of festivities in a 500-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from itself. The aura produces a slow but persistent downfall of Tamh Gon's Confetti, which materializes 30 feet above the ground, and the air is filled with a soft, subtle drum beat. Creatures that enter the aura feel a euphoric splendor. {@actSave con} {@dc 20} A creature other than Tamh Gon that starts its turn in the aura. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Pacified|XPHB} condition until the start of its next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to Tamh Gon's Festival Aura for 24 hours.

trait.name: Inscrutable
entries: No magic can observe Tamh Gon remotely or detect its thoughts without its permission. Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) checks made to ascertain Tamh Gon's intentions or sincerity are made with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If Tamh Gon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: Tamh Gon has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Physical Binding
entries: Tamh Gon can't fly higher than 120 feet above the ground while in the Physical Realm. Additionally, while Tamh Gon is within 120 feet of a {@item Tears of the Moon|ObojimaTallGrass|Tear of the Moon}, Tamh Gon can't teleport or travel to another plane of existence by any means short of a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell.

trait.name: Speech Bubble
entries: Tamh Gon can't verbally communicate, but instead produces illusory speech bubbles above its head. The text that appears in these bubbles is in the {@language Torum|ObojimaTallGrass} language. All creatures with an Intelligence of 5 or higher can comprehend what Tamh Gon is saying—provided Tamh Gon is aware of the creature's presence—even if the creature can't read {@language Torum|ObojimaTallGrass}, can't normally speak a language, or can't see the speech bubble.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Tamh Gon casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 20}):

1e: {@spell Tamh Gon's Fiery Festival Feast|ObojimaTallGrass} (as an action)

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Tamh Gon makes two Bell Slam attacks and uses one of its Chimes. It can replace one attack with a casting of one of its At Will spells.

action.name: Bell Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 11} to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}15 ({@damage 3d6 + 5}) Bludgeoning damage plus 13 ({@damage 3d8}) Thunder damage.

action.name: Chimes
entries: Tamh Gon uses one of the following chimes, affecting each creature of its choice (other than itself) in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from itself:

items.name: Blast Chime
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 20} Each affected creature. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Blessed Chime
entries: Each affected creature regains 9 ({@damage 2d8}) {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

items.name: Resonant Chime
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 20} Each affected creature that is wearing or carrying a metal object. {@actSaveFail} The target drops all metal objects it's holding. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} The target takes 13 ({@damage 3d8}) Thunder damage.

items.name: Restorative Chime
entries: Tamh Gon magically removes one of the following effects from each affected creature: 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level, the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition, or a curse (including the target's attunement to a cursed magic item).

action.name: Spirit Shift
entries: Tamh Gon enters the Spirit Realm (Ethereal Plane) from the Physical Realm, or vice versa.

legendary.name: Festival King
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 20} One creature Tamh Gon can see within 60 feet (the target succeeds automatically if it has immunity to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition). {@actSaveFail} Until the end of the target's next turn, it magically can't take an action or a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and instead gives all of its attention and admiration to Tamh Gon. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} Tamh Gon can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.

legendary.name: Phase
entries: Tamh Gon teleports up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.

legendary.name: Tintinnabulation
entries: Tamh Gon uses one of its Chimes.

trait.name: Ethereal Sight
entries: The spirit can see 60 feet into the Spirit Realm (Ethereal Plane) while in the Physical Realm and vice versa.

trait.name: Noise Sensitivity
entries: While the spirit is in the Physical Realm, a creature within 30 feet of it can take an action to shout or scream at it. When this happens, the spirit must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Sonic Emergence
entries: If a creature in the Physical Realm creates a sufficient amount of noise (at the GM's discretion) while within 60 feet of the spirit's corresponding location in the Spirit Realm, the spirit immediately returns to the Physical Realm.

action.name: Illusory Clatter
entries: The spirit creates a sound within 30 feet of itself, as if by the {@spell Minor Illusion|XPHB} spell (save {@dc 11}). If it is in the Spirit Realm, the sound can be heard in the Physical Realm.

action.name: Shift
entries: The spirit enters the Spirit Realm (Ethereal Plane) from the Physical Realm or vice versa.

monsterFluff.name: Awakened Cat Neko Duelist
entries: In Yatamon's fervent cat culture, neko duelists are highly regarded. Though these awakened cat warriors aren't considered masters of the neko duelist fighting style, their proficiency as duelists still places them at the top of their class. Unlike their bipedal counterparts, traditional neko duelists can utilize the fighting style's techniques to their fullest potential, as the style itself was shaped by the natural movements of a cat.

entries.name: A Symbol
entries: Neko duelists are often held to a high standard, both by themselves and those around them. The story of the first duelist, whichever version it may be, is well known among awakened cats; in it, the duelist is a warrior of the people, helping those around them and defending Yatamon from a great danger. Because of this, today's duelists are expected to act in the same manner.

monsterFluff.name: Canden & Moon's Advanced Student
entries: The advanced students of Yatamon's very own sword masters, Canden and Moon, are, in many regards, icons of the city. From youthful upstarts with a passion for the blade to skilled warriors who desire more knowledge, this formidable group of swordsmen is as close to mastery as a group of students can get before taking their final exam.
Although most would say these pupils are on the cusp of greatness, a majority of students remain at this level for years before finally gaining mastery of the school's special technique.

monsterFluff.name: Postal Knight Cavalry
entries: The postal knight cavalry is a small but skilled collection of knights who, through many years of service to the brigade, have been given a "secretary" they call their own. To train the postal knights' mount of choice, the secretary bird, is no small effort, as it takes years of conditioning by the courier brigades' stable masters, making the role of cavalry a fairly impressive position within the ranks.

Normally, mounts are given to an individual based on the task at hand and returned after the objective is complete, so to have a secretary of your own means you, above all others, have earned the right to take a mount into the field, no matter the mission.

entries.name: Red Foot Ranch
entries: In the southernmost part of the Gale Fields, directly north of Yatamon, are the Courier Brigades' taming grounds and the largest secretary stable on the island, Red Foot Ranch. Here, Stable Masters Aspen and Nonomi Fike tame, stow, and train secretary birds brought in from the wild. The two former postal knights, now a married couple, have run the stables for over 15 years and are said to have worked with every secretary currently active in the brigade. In addition to their slew of accolades, the two are well known for the ceremony and blessing they offer to a knight when they are gifted a mount tamed at Red Foot Ranch—a cherished moment for anyone lucky enough to experience it.

monsterFluff.name: Yoka Scout
entries: Though a Yoka Scout, by their own words, should never be afraid to combat a dangerous foe on their own, most scouts travel in groups of three to five—using scrappy resourcefulness, hidden traps, and clever team planning to take on singular targets beyond their individual capabilities. This devious style of fighting might be considered underhanded and unprincipled if it weren't for the fact that the Yoka Scouts primarily focus their efforts on dispelling demons from the city. However, rivalry between the Yoka Scouts and other groups, such as the students of Canden and Moon's sword school, has led to street skirmishes and challenges that highlight the scouts' dishonest methods.

entries.name: Planning
entries: Despite their youth, the Yoka Scouts are tactical in their approach to conflict. Each scout party usually has one member in their late teens or early twenties who acts as the party leader. Before taking on a major challenge, this individual will work with their party to craft a plan, assign roles, divide resources, and create escape routes—all of which can take hours, if not days. The culmination of this hard work and understanding of their group's skill set allows the scouts to arise victorious from combat, even after unforeseen obstacles surface during the battle.

entries.name: Tools & Tricks
entries: Every charm, talisman, and nakurina the Yoka Scouts can obtain is put to good use within their ranks. A group of scouts always tries to carry one or more magical trinkets that can help them discover, trap, or slay demons, though finding these objects is easier said than done. Despite the difficulty the scouts have had obtaining demon charms and objects like them, a handful of powerful artifacts have been secured by the organization. These tools are often shared among the scouts, depending on the individual needs of each party. When they're not in use, the highest-ranking members are charged with protecting them and will often keep them on their person.

monsterFluff.name: Button Crow
entries: Button crows are a special type of pest spirit known for their intelligence and obsessive personalities. Each button crow usually fixates on one particular trinket during its life and spends most of its days collecting that item. These objects can vary widely, such as keys, paper, coins, glass, brooches, and gems—the most common of these curios being buttons. When an object is chosen by the button crow, a magical pact of sorts is naturally formed between the creature and the bauble. This pact is non-verbal and unwritten and is instead willed into being by the crows' obsessive nature. When this occurs, the crow undergoes several physical changes, including the evolution of its eyes to match the likeness of its chosen trinket and a gradual shift in its diet, which forces it to consume the beloved objects it collects.

Button crows can be found across the island in villages and merchant camps, often following the flow of people. It's said that when a group of 20 or more people gather, a button crow is sure to follow and try to swindle some poor soul out of the fasteners on their shirt or the laces in their boots.

monsterFluff.name: Canned Cat
entries: Canned cats were first discovered in the city of Yatamon during the Age of Nakudama. The first record of them comes from an explorer who uncanned one of the curious creatures during an expedition of the once-dangerous city. She claimed she first tried to commune with the tiny cat, but after several hours of silence, decided to eat it instead. Her tales of the gelatinous feline sparked widespread curiosity, and soon canned cats became highly sought after.

Hundreds of years later, canned cats are used in potion brewing, balms, and as the base of many Yatamon stews. Although they have grown rarer over time, it's still common enough for scavengers and explorers to occasionally uncover one of these unique creatures.

monsterFluff.name: Cauldron Hydra
entries: At Yatamon's famous school of witches, the Witchery, there's a saying that many of the teachers tell their students: a messy witch is a recipe for danger. The maxim was coined by the school after numerous incidents involving the erratic Cauldron Hydra. Cauldron hydras are formed from the concoction of potion remnants left in witches' cauldrons after repeated use. There is no exact recipe, but most experienced witches grow concerned if a cauldron hasn't been cleaned in more than a few months. Should a cauldron hydra bubble into existence, it's best to keep your distance—the creatures can become very aggressive and often attack within minutes of coming to life.

entries.name: Research
entries: Cauldron hydras aren't found in the wild, unless a witch or wizard abandons their unwashed cauldron. When studied intentionally, the time spent with the creature is often short-lived due to their volatile and dangerous nature. There are few, if any, records of them being kept in captivity, and the general consensus among witches is that the creature is a nuisance, unworthy of further attention. Still, some wonder what potential the hydra might yet hold.

entries.name: Chance of Creation
entries: To determine whether a cauldron hydra is created in-game, the GM should roll a die each time a player brews a potion. If the die shows a 1, a cauldron hydra is crected. Use the table below to determine which die to roll.

monsterFluff.name: Graffiti Golem
entries: These two-dimensional creatures are painted images that have been animated by magic. The paint used to create them relies on a specific type of pigment commonly used in potion brewing. Some of these golems are created to patrol a single flat surface, such as a door or wall, while others travel from one flat surface to another to track their quarry. Most graffiti golems serve as spies or sentries, though students from the Witchery are known to create them for the pure joy of mischief.
City goers know they exist, but they aren't always easy to spot. Because the paint on a graffiti golem never truly dries, they are susceptible to being scrubbed away.

monsterFluff.name: Howler Skulker
entries: Most howlers live on the outskirts of society, inhabiting wildlands that only travelers pass through. In Yatamon, however, there are groups of howlers known as skulkers that have taken up residence in the city's subway and forested parks. Rather than hunting and raiding in the overt and flashy shows of power most howlers are known for, the skulkers prefer to stay hidden, using sneaky tactics and disguises to steal from the city in the late hours of the evening.

monsterFluff.name: Living Memory
entries: The many magics of Obojima that permeate both the island's Physical and Spiritual Realms also reach beyond the fabric to unite with the abstract concepts of life, such as fortune, devotion, time, and emotion. This special connection between the magics of the island and these cultural pillars manifests across the realms in a myriad of ways.

One such manifestation of this special connection is living memories—creatures born from the lingering emotions left by a person or people who have long since left this world. These living memories are the raw, unfiltered expression of pure emotion, whose purpose revolves around the display of the powerful memories that created them. These creatures often form in a physical space in which a singular momentous moment has occurred, or a shared experience by many has permanently marked the land.

entries.name: Dispositions
entries: Unlike other creatures, living memories require the use of Enemy Dispositions to be used in combat. In this instance, Dispositions are used to determine the type of emotion that manifests the creature.

entries.name: Manifestations
entries: Living memories often take on the form of a humanoidlike creature, using abandoned objects and found clothing to construct their bodies. The lingering emotion from which they are derived can also cause a variety of quirks and tics, which they wear on their sleeves, often making it easy for a passerby to discern the type of memory they are.

monsterFluff.name: Lanternback Turtle
entries: Thought to originally be nature spirits from a millennium ago who, in an effort to be closer to the Physical Realm, chose to take the form of a beast, lanternback turtles are now a rare wonder of the island. Their numbers are so sparse, in fact, that a sighting of one of these beloved giants is considered a blessing of the island and can even draw good fortune to your side. And yet, even with their rarity, the lanternback turtle is famous among Obojimans. Statues, clothing, toys, and even tools are adorned with their iconic visage, while craftsfolk and guilds use the turtle to represent themselves across the island.

monsterFluff.name: Melon Bird
entries: Farmers across Obojima lean on magic to help them grow crops. Occasionally, this magic leads to the spontaneous creation of an animated crop that behaves more like a ravenous beast than a plant. For some reason, melons tend to be more sensitive to this transformation, and the melon birds that result have been known to drive off their farmer creators.

The transformation that occurs in crops can take a considerable amount of time and may even happen days or weeks after the crop has been harvested. Due to this delay, melon birds are known to erupt into chaotic scenes in markets, caravans, and restaurants. In Yatamon, it's even considered bad luck to leave a melon uneaten, and if you were to do so, you would surely get scolded by your aunt or granny.

monsterFluff.name: Pilot Leech
entries: The flesh of an animal that has died from a curse is quite toxic. Its taste is putrid and is sure to sicken most who eat it, if not worse. In the case of a minor spirit who consumes the meat, its fate is most certainly worse.

Pilot leeches are created when a minor spirit eats the flesh of a cursed creature. If the spirit doesn't die, it transforms into a demon, which takes on the likeness of a dark purple leech. In this form, the demon will attach itself to a beast, taking control of its mind, and using its body to feast on the creatures and plants nearest to it. The beast itself gains demonic qualities after being taken over by the pilot leech, the most glaring of them being the beast's unnatural size.
Witches and druids often seek out pilot leeches for their potion crafting qualities, but most stay clear if the beast has grown too large.

monsterFluff.name: Infected Beast
entries: When a beast is infected by a pilot leech, it begins the final stage of its life. Its body starts to grow beyond its means, and quickly takes on unnatural and demonic features. In a short time, it transforms from its animal form into a gargantuan monster, whose driving force is to consume and feed the leech that has attached itself to the creature. With this metamorphosis also comes the fast decay of the beast's body. As the beast grows bigger, it struggles to carry its own weight, and eventually, as its body refuses to grow anymore, it becomes too bloated and too sick to rest. In tragic fashion, the animal will eat itself to death, so long as it's not hunted down first.

monsterFluff.name: Scrap Demon Swarm
entries: The mouse-like spirits known as ompo have serviced Yatamon since people began to congregate in the city. These energetic creatures collect at the bottoms of trash cans and in heavily populated areas, consuming any waste they might find. Ompo often live short and happy lives, as they're cherished and well fed by locals. However, like most spirits, Ompo are not immune to demonic transformation. If their hunger ever becomes gluttonous, their docile nature suddenly shifts, making them aggressive and self-serving—their desire for sustenance is no longer restrained by morality, and a newfound fixation drives them to consume, no matter the cost. Worse still is the nature of this demonic form, as its cursed aura can cause this transformation in other ompo, a tragedy no citizen would ever desire.

monsterFluff.name: Secretary Bird
entries: These large running birds live throughout the island, but predominantly within the sweeping hillsides and grasslands of the Gale Fields. Their lanky stature allows them to easily see over the tall grass, and their quick speed and moderate flying capabilities make them well suited to combating the dangerous predators that call the fields home.

Although horses and mopeds are the most common forms of transportation across Obojima, the secretary bird is still quite popular, albeit harder to ride initially. Nonetheless, these birds are loved for their fearless nature, loyalty, and ability to glide, making them a staple among merchants and postal knights.

monsterFluff.name: Siphon Fish
entries: Resembling the common sucker fish, these flying sea pests feed on magic, draining objects and creatures of their enchantments and arcane properties to sustain themselves. Yatamon, being a city overflowing with magic, attracts siphon fish in droves, with buildings and large structures being prime targets. When this happens, neighborhoods often rally to dispatch the creatures, as the draining effects of the siphon fish are known to cause buildings to collapse—a problem the citizens of Yatamon don't take lightly. On occasion, siphon fish are raised by witches for specific tasks, but most of the time, these fish are regarded as a real nuisance.

monsterFluff.name: Spindle Stalker
entries: The dangling pillar of the spindle stalker's duko moss is a sight no traveller wishes to see. These larger carnivorous creatures, known for the paralyzing moss that grows off their backs, are one of the island's most dangerous hunters. Named for their resemblance to their tiny counterpart, the spindle leg spider, whose webs are a well-known potion ingredient, the spindle stalkers' reputation is much more infamous. Tales of the creatures' deadly attacks against groups of howlers in the Brackwater Wetlands or the devastating battles members of AHA had to face while exploring the subway beneath Yatamon, have painted the stalker as a horrifying visage, matched only by the urugama. Luckily for most, these monstrous creatures aren't often seen above ground or in well-traveled areas. The average islander often goes their entire life without ever seeing a spindle stalker, a fact most agree is a blessing from Obojima.

monsterFluff.name: Tamh Gon
entries: Tamh Gon, or as many people refer to him as "The Great Festival Spirit," is a centuries-old being that has blessed the people of Obojima with his exuberance and electric aura for nearly a millennium. The elder spirit shows up at no particular time and on no particular day, breaking the normalcy of the day and sending the inhabitants of any city, town, or village into a sporadic celebration of life, music, food, and drink.

Many have tried to predict when Tamh Gon will show up, but there seems to be no rhyme or reason. He does as he pleases, appearing on any plane, at any time, with the simple desire to celebrate, making many Obojimans view him less like an elder spirit and more like a force of nature.

entries.name: Desires
entries: Plenty of people have tried to understand Tamh Gon's desire to celebrate, with numerous rumors and speculations being shared over the years. The most popular of which claims that Tamh Gon feeds on the joy and elation of others, and is the reason for the elder spirit's lengthy life.

entries.name: Eldest Spirit
entries: Tamh Gon is one of the oldest, if not the oldest, spirits on Obojima, though he never claims to be. Records of Tamh Gon's presence can be found in songs, books, and paintings less than 300 years after the beginning of the Age of Humanity. During this time, Tamh Gon was not seen as an elder spirit, and the form he took, although similar, was not the massive lantern we know today. Still, his presence was palpable, and he quickly grew a reputation among the early humans as the "Festival Spirit."

entries.name: AHA's Attempts
entries: Since its inception, members of AHA have attempted to work with Tamh Gon to better understand the past through his firsthand accounts of major events—and though they have gleaned some knowledge from the elder spirit, Tamh Gon has proven to be difficult to work with.

Whether it be his old age or eccentric personality, members of AHA have struggled to speak with Tamh Gon on an even playing field, as, beyond festivities, it's difficult to understand what the spirit desires and how one might convince him to set aside his partying and help with the task at hand.

entries.name: Reputation
entries: Across the island, in major cities, small towns, local villages, and even the heartiest campsite, anticipation of Tamh Gon's arrival is always on the back of people's minds. To Obojimans, Tamh Gon is the manifestation of festivity and a needed reminder to let go of your frustrations and celebrate with your neighbors. He's revered by most, loved by many, and considered an honorary member of towns and villages of every size.

Still, there are those who only tolerate the Great Festival Spirit rather than love him. Sticklers and rule followers often grind against Tamh Gon's abandonment of the schedule, while other powerful elder spirits have been known to disapprove of his festivals, seeing them as a blemish on Obojima's calm beauty.
No matter your opinion on Tamh Gon, most have one, which speaks to the reach of the elder spirit's presence in both realms.

entries.name: Domain
entries: Most elder spirits settle in a singular location in the Physical or Spirit Realm. While there, their powerful magic slowly seeps into the land around them, forming their domain. Within an elder spirit's domain, the world is altered to the spirit's liking, and their magic becomes even more potent. Tamh Gon, however, breaks this norm. Rather than staying in one location, Tamh Gon is constantly moving, bringing his domain along with him like an aura. Additionally, Tamh Gon's domain does not physically alter the world around him, though its effects can be felt within moments of the elder spirit appearing. To this day, the features of Tamh Gon's domain aren't fully known.

entries.name: Attack on Tamh Gon
entries: Tamh Gon's power is great, and by many standards, the elder spirit is one of the most powerful beings on the island—a great deal of this reasoning is due to Tamh Gon's four bells, each of which wields a unique and overwhelming magic. Over the years, this has inspired bandits, thieves, and demons alike to attempt to steal the bells, leading to many failed attempts and unfortunate skirmishes, with only a handful coming even remotely close.

monsterFluff.name: Yanari
entries: Yanari are pesky, humanoid spirits about the size of a raccoon, that feed on loud noises. Wherever there's a steady diet of audible ruckus, such as markets, taverns, busy kitchens, and festivals, a yanari is likely to be nearby, feasting on the clamor.

Although yanari make their own noise, it cannot sustain them. They must seek out the noises of others to satisfy their craving. In silence, yanari become irritable and insubstantial, fading away to the Spirit Realm as they bark and screech with frustration.

Normal, everyday noise like singing, a babbling brook, or a bustling household is not enough to bring them into form, so yanari seek spaces that amplify sounds; thus they can often be found in empty pots, urns, and cabinets. Yanari are at their most aggravating when they are attempting to provoke those around them to make loud noises by being annoying, but with some patience, yanari infestations can usually be eliminated by maintaining a few days of strict silence—an ordeal that yanari cannot bear for long.

table.name: Empty House Trinket
rows: A First Age radio that crackles into life if it is whelmed or powered by a spell.
A well-worn First Age sweatshirt with a cute pig character on it.
An Old trolley token from the days of the First Age.
An Old dagger, tattered bedroll, and calligraphy brush set, all from the Age Of Nakudama.

table.name: Signature Flair
rows: A flurry of glistening snowflakes blows by in a gust of cold wind.
A series of colored smoke rings puffs out of the bottle.
A bud emerges from the bottle and blooms into a sweet-smelling lotus flower.
A bunch of tiny spirits leap from the bottle and run to the shadows.
A golden butterfly made of light flies out of the bottle.
A watery belch erupts from within the bottle.
A chant of "{@i Chug! Chug! Chug?}" can be heard coming from the bottle.
A tiny hourglass spins above the bottle before disappearing in a puff of smoke and a "{@i Ding?}"
A small ring of mushrooms sprouts around you as you open the bottle.
A stream of bubbles comes out of the bottle, chiming as they pop.
A flock of tiny, colorful birds flutter from the bottle.
A tiny, shimmering tornado spins above the bottle before sputtering out.
A soft breeze blows by, smelling of wildflowers and cherry blossoms.
Anyone holding the bottle is filled with static electricity which causes their hair to stand on end.
A jaunty tune jingles from within the bottle and then ends on a slide whistle.
When opened, a low, deep voice within the bottle says, "{@i Ohhh yeahh.}"
Before opening the bottle, a spirit hand appears to slap your wrist.
A deep, omniscient voice intones: "{@i And in that moment... everything changed.}"
When opening the bottle, a voice says, "{@i A pleasure to be of servicer}"
A soft voice hisses from the bottle, "{@i I've missssssed you.}"

table.name: Vehicles Table
footnotes: 1 obe is = to 1 mile / 1 oph is = 1 mph

table.name: List of Dispositions
rows: Any creature can have one of these Dispositions:
Only a creature with an Intelligence of 7 or higher can have one of these Dispositions:

variantrule.name: Operating Vehicles
entries: Though there are many unique aspects to the different types of vehicles, there is a general set of rules that apply when driving any of them. Vehicle properties, which are listed later in this section, allow certain vehicles to ignore or alter some of the rules detailed in this section.

entries.name: Driving & Riding in a Vehicle
entries: All vehicles have a Crew, which is the number of creatures required to operate the vehicle. Each type of vehicle also has a maximum number of Passengers, which is the number of other Small and Medium creatures that can be transported by the vehicle at a time, in addition to its Crew.

entries.name: Mounting or Entering a Vehicle
entries: During your move, you can enter, exit, mount, or dismount a vehicle by spending an amount of movement equal to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} (round down). You can't enter or mount a vehicle if it already has its maximum number of Crew and Passengers within or on it. You also can't enter a vehicle if it has the Flipped or Locked condition (see Vehicle Conditions).

entries.name: Controlling a Vehicle
entries: If you wish to serve as a member of a vehicle's Crew, you must have at least one free hand, and you must take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to operate the vehicle on each of your turns. If the vehicle must first be powered on, you can do so as part of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you take to begin operating it. You can also power off such a vehicle at any point on your turn (no action required).
In order for two creatures to exchange control of a vehicle, one must take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action and the other must simultaneously take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to change places.

entries.name: Vehicle Movement
entries: Vehicles have two kinds of speeds: a Combat Speed for shorter-distance movement (measured in feet per round) and a Travel Speed for long-distance, out-of-combat movement (measured in miles per hour). While you're serving as a member of a vehicle's Crew or are a vehicle's Passenger, you ignore your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, instead moving with the vehicle as it moves.
A vehicle can never move more than its maximum Combat Speed in a round, regardless of whether another creature takes control of it.

If you're the sole member of a vehicle's Crew in combat, you spend its movement as you would typically spend your own movement, controlling where the vehicle moves on each of your turns; you can't take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action while controlling a vehicle to gain extra movement for the current turn. If a vehicle requires a Crew of more than one creature, one of those creatures must be designated to control the vehicle's movement.

entries.name: Running into Other Targets
entries: A vehicle's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved when it hits a creature or object that is smaller than it. It instead completely stops if the creature or object it hits is the same size as the vehicle or larger, or if the target is otherwise unable to be moved.

entries.name: Changing Direction
entries: Sharply turning a vehicle or reversing its direction during combat requires additional caution and effort. To do so, the creature controlling the vehicle must spend an amount of the vehicle's movement equal to half its Combat Speed (round down).

entries.name: Performing Complex Maneuvers
entries: If the creature controlling the vehicle wishes to perform a complex maneuver, it can make a Maneuvering check. To make this ability check, the creature rolls {@dice 1d20} plus its Dexterity or Intelligence modifier (its choice) and the vehicle's Size Modifier.

entries.name: Cargo & Towing
entries: All vehicles have a Cargo Capacity, which is the amount of weight the vehicle can carry. Cargo ignores the weight of the vehicle's Crew and Passengers, only factoring in the weight of any objects inside or on top of the vehicle that aren't otherwise being worn by a creature.

A vehicle can also tow or drag an additional amount of weight up to its Cargo Capacity. If a vehicle is carrying no cargo, it can therefore tow a total amount of weight up to twice its Cargo Capacity.

entries.name: Vehicles in Combat
entries: Vehicles use the following special rules in combat.

entries.name: Vehicle Armor Class & Hit Points
entries: Refer to the {@table Vehicles Table|ObojimaTalesYatamon} for each vehicle's AC and {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum. A vehicle is destroyed when it has 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Targeting a Vehicle
entries: Vehicles can be attacked like any other object. Spells and other effects that target creatures (such as the {@spell Fireball|XPHB} spell) can also target vehicles.

entries.name: Damaging a Vehicle
entries: Vehicles have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and Psychic damage. They also have a damage threshold, as shown in the {@table Vehicles Table|ObojimaTalesYatamon}.

entries.name: Massive Damage
entries: If a vehicle takes damage that equals or exceeds half its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum (round down) from a single attack or effect, it gains the {@condition Flipped|ObojimaTalesYatamon} condition (see Vehicle Conditions).

entries.name: Damage Threshold
entries: A creature or an object that has a damage threshold has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to all damage unless it takes an amount of damage from a single attack or effect equal to or greater than its damage threshold, in which case it takes that entire instance of damage. Any damage that fails to meet or exceed the damage threshold is superficial and doesn't reduce {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Saving Throws
entries: Vehicles always fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws, and they are immune to effects that require other saves as well as conditions that aren't detailed in the Vehicle Conditions section.
The Crew and Passengers of a Piloted vehicle automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws against effects that target them, but they take only half damage from such effects.

entries.name: Going Prone on a Mounted Vehicle
entries: If a creature on a Mounted vehicle gains the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, it can stay mounted on the vehicle, but the vehicle immediately stops and can't move until it is righted. While {@condition Prone|XPHB} on a vehicle, the creature can't crawl, and it spends an amount of the vehicle's movement equal to half its Combat Speed to end that condition, rather than spending its own movement.

entries.name: Ramming
entries: A creature controlling a vehicle can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to attempt to ram a target with the vehicle; this can't be attempted more than once per turn. If the target is a creature, it can make a Dexterity saving throw to avoid the vehicle; the DC for the save equals 8 plus the controlling creature's Dexterity or Intelligence modifier (its choice) and the vehicle's Size Modifier.

If the vehicle moved at least 10 feet in a straight line immediately before successfully ramming a target, the target takes an amount of Bludgeoning damage based on the vehicle's Size Modifier: {@damage 1d6} (Size 1), {@damage 2d6} (Size 2), {@damage 3d6} (Size 3), {@damage 4d6} (Size 4), {@damage 5d6} (Size 5), or {@damage 6d6} (Size 6). The target takes twice as much damage if the vehicle moved at least 20 feet before ramming it, or three times as much damage if the vehicle moved 30 feet or more before ramming it.

Immediately after the vehicle rams a Small or larger target, the vehicle's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced (as detailed in the Controlling a Vehicle section), and the vehicle takes {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it moved before ramming its target, to a maximum of {@damage 3d6}. This damage ignores the vehicle's damage threshold.

entries.name: Vehicle Conditions
entries: Vehicles can be subjected to the following conditions.

entries.name: Repairing a Vehicle
entries: Repairs to a damaged vehicle can be made while the vehicle is in a repair shop. Repairing 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} of damage requires 8 hours of work and costs 10 GF for materials and labor. Alternatively, a creature can repair a vehicle by making an Intelligence ({@skill Mechanics|ObojimaTallGrass}) check using {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB} over the course of 8 hours, which costs 5 GF for materials. Doing so repairs a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the result of the check –10 (minimum of 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}).

entries.name: Spirit-Whelmed Vehicles
entries: If a vehicle is operational, a spirit can whelm it, disappearing into the vehicle and powering it. To do so, the spirit must take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action while touching the vehicle. Additionally, the spirit's {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} must be equal to or greater than the vehicle's Size Modifier or the vehicle fails to power on. If multiple spirits attempt to whelm a vehicle, their combined CR must be equal to or greater than the vehicle's Size Modifier in order to power it; spirits with a CR of less than 1 count as CR 1/2 for the purpose of calculating their combined CR.

While whelming a vehicle, a spirit must take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to power the vehicle on each of its turns, and it ignores its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, instead moving with the vehicle as it moves. The spirit can see and use its other senses as if it were at the front of the vehicle. On the spirit's turn, it can choose to stop whelming the vehicle (no action required), exiting it and reappearing in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of it.

If the vehicle takes damage equal to or greater than the spirit's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum, or if the vehicle is destroyed, the spirit is shunted out of the vehicle, ending its whelm early.

entries.name: Spirits Controlling Vehicles
entries: If a spirit that is whelming a vehicle has an Intelligence of 7 or higher, it can control the vehicle as if it were a member of the vehicle's Crew (see Controlling a Vehicle). If a spirit is controlling a vehicle when the vehicle takes damage, it must make a Constitution saving throw to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}. The DC equals 10 or half the damage taken by the vehicle (round down), whichever number is higher, up to a maximum DC of 30. On a failed save, the spirit's whelm ends early.

A spirit that is whelming a vehicle that is already being operated can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to wrestle for its control (provided the spirit can normally power it). The creature currently operating the vehicle must make a Dexterity saving throw, or an Intelligence saving throw if it's whelming the vehicle. The DC for the save equals 10 + the CR of the intruding spirit. On a failed save, the intruding spirit takes control.

entries.name: Vehicle Classifications
entries: A vehicle's classification expresses how a character is situated in or on the vehicle while operating or riding in it. This classification determines how certain mechanics affect the vehicle as well as its Crew and Passengers.

items.name: Mounted
items.entry: The vehicle has no entry point and is straddled rather than entered.

items.name: Piloted
items.entry: The vehicle requires a creature to enter it in order to operate it. Creatures inside this vehicle have {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover}.

entries.name: Aquatic
entries: This vehicle can only move in the water.

entries.name: Encased
entries: This vehicle is completely closed off from the surrounding environment. Creatures inside it are {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB} and have {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} from creatures outside it.

entries.name: Feather
entries: This vehicle can't deal damage when it rams a target.

entries.name: Flying
entries: This vehicle can only move through the air.

entries.name: Nimble
entries: The creature controlling this vehicle doesn't need to spend any of the vehicle's movement to change its direction.

entries.name: Pedalled
entries: The creature controlling this vehicle can take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action to gain extra movement for the current turn.

entries.name: Simple
entries: This vehicle doesn't require the creature controlling it to take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on each of its turns; it still has the {@condition Uncontrolled|ObojimaTalesYatamon} condition if the creature controlling it has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. If the vehicle must be powered on in order to begin operating it, it still requires a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to do so.

entries.name: Wide
entries: When ramming a creature using this vehicle, each creature within 5 feet of the target must also make the Dexterity saving throw.

variantrule.name: Disposition System
entries: The Disposition System serves as a mechanical representation of a creature's emotional mindset and manifest as a series of {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} given to the creature's stat block. Dispositions can bring a level of depth and nuance to a combat encounter, especially to a creature that an adventuring party has already faced.

entries.name: Assigning a Disposition
entries: In addition to a creature's regular stat block, you might also find one or more Disposition tables.

Each table offers a special list of {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} (called "Impulsive Reactions") the creature can take during combat, which are indicative of the emotions or motivations the Disposition represents.
For example, if a bear is awakened while sleeping, you might choose to give it the Skittish Disposition.
It's important to note that, even though a Disposition is meant to offer a mixture of roleplay and mechanics, it can affect the Challenge Rating of a creature.

entries.name: Hit Point Thresholds
entries: Hit Point Thresholds represent a moment in combat when the creature makes a snap decision based on how it's feeling.
When a creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} are reduced to or below a specific Threshold, it gains access to one of the Impulsive Reactions from its Disposition table.
For example, the moment the bear drops to 25 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it triggers its Impulsive Reaction, which allows it to move up to 40 feet away from the creature that attacked it.

When a Threshold is reached, an Impulsive Reaction is triggered, and the creature must use the Impulsive Reaction by taking its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, if available. If the creature's {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} is not available, it loses its opportunity to use that Impulsive Reaction. Once a Hit Point Threshold has been reached, that Impulsive Reaction can't be triggered again (whether it was used or not) until the creature finishes a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
If damage from a single attack or effect causes multiple Thresholds to be reached at the same time, you can choose which of the triggered Impulsive Reactions the creature uses.

entries.name: Learning a Creature's Disposition
entries: To determine the Disposition of a creature, a character can take the {@action Search|XPHB} action to make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check, provided it can see the creature. The DC to determine the Disposition of a creature is equal to 10 plus half the creature's CR.
Learning the Disposition of a creature does not inform a character of the creature's Impulsive Reactions, but it may provide insight into how the creature might act during combat.

entries.name: Creating Your Own Dispositions
entries: Below you'll find a list of guidelines to follow when designing your own Dispositions:

items: A creature must have a {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} minimum of 20 or higher for it to gain a Disposition.
There must be a minimum of 20 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} between Hit Point Thresholds.
A Hit Point Threshold must be no less than 5 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} below a creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum.
Impulsive Reactions are meant to be an extension of the creature's feelings or personality.

Years ago, I was given the opportunity to build a world inspired by my favorite games and movies from my childhood, in a game system that I've loved for nearly two decades, and with a team that understands and supports my eclectic style of design and storytelling.

Throughout that process, I've learned a lot about what I want out of an artistic endeavor like this book, and as each day goes by, it becomes more and more clear to me that what I want more than anything is to make something that's impactful on a generation of gamers. Something that looks at TTRPGs in a different light, causes those who read it to reflect on tabletop games as a medium and how it can be used as a tool for personal growth, and above all else, inspires others to create something of their own.
Overall, that's a huge ask, and I'm not totally sure I've done that yet. However, Obojima and the community it's gathered make me feel like I'm taking the right steps.
Thank you all, and I hope you enjoy this book as much as I enjoyed making it.

data.name: Welcome to the City of Yatamon
