entries: {@b If you are reading this, then welcome to the world of Obojima and the great city of Yatamon!}

{@b You've made it to Obojima's largest hub, where all manner of adventures await you. Whether you are a player or a GM, we're sure you will enjoy this setting, which invites you to play in a world with a very distinctive flavor. From spirit festivals to abandoned convenience stores, Obojima and Yatamon are sure to hold a story worth telling.}
{@b We hope that as you explore the city and get to know its people and mysteries, you're able to experience D&D in a new and refreshing way.}
{@b Good luck, and may fortune be on your side.}
{@b Here are some guidelines and recommendations that we feel will give you the best experience when playing or running a game in the city of Yatamon.}

entries.name: Player & GM Facing Material
entries: As with most sourcebooks that describe a world, there are sections for all readers—players and Game Masters (GM) alike. In this book, there are sections to be read only by the GM. These sections for GM eyes only contain secrets better left unread by players, such as the Neighborhood chapter, which details information about adventures and NPCs.
As a player, we recommend reading through the following pages, but as a courtesy, always speak with your GM first.

items: Read pages to learn about {@book Yatamon and its people|ObojimaTalesYatamon|2}.

Read the first paragraph of {@book Old Yatamon|ObojimaTalesYatamon|3|Old Yatamon}, {@book Yatamon's Path|ObojimaTalesYatamon|3|Yatamon's Path}, and {@book The Subway System|ObojimaTalesYatamon|3|The Subway System}, to learn about the three notable areas of Yatamon.
Read to learn about {@book vehicle mechanics|ObojimaTalesYatamon|5}.
Read to learn about the {@book new player options|ObojimaTalesYatamon|6} from the book.

entries.name: Other Books
entries: If something is followed by an {@sup *}, it means it's an option introduced in a source other than {@i Obojima: Tales from Yatamon}, such as the 5.5E (2024) Basic Rules. If something is followed by a {@sup °}, it means it can be found in the {@i {@book Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass|ObojimaTallGrass}} core book.

entries.name: Live in the World
entries: Before you roll up your first character, we invite you to live in the world a little before you take the plunge and start rolling dice. Learn a bit about the city, read into its culture, look at the art, and allow your mind to make up stories in your head. Absorb the backgrounds and the factions sections to get a feel for what it's like to be an Obojiman in this idyllic, magical city filled with spirits and mysteries. If you're used to playing or running games in D&D, Obojima provides a potentially refreshing break into another realm of storytelling and roleplaying.

While fighting monsters and getting treasure can certainly be a part of any Obojima adventure, figuring out relationships, discovering clues to solve weird mysteries, and parlaying with elder spirits to appease their wrath are among the less combat-centric and more roleplaying-heavy aspects of gaming in this world. And so, really immersing yourself and becoming an Obojiman is something that we highly recommend.

GMs should be on the lookout for notes like this throughout the book. As writers, we often leave alternative interpretations, options, or thoughts on a topic. These notes are completely optional, so feel free to ignore them if you prefer the standard writing. With that, we bid our noble Game Masters happy storytelling! May you delight and surprise your friends at the table of imagination. And to our intrepid players, may you enjoy boundless adventures.

{@b Below is our conversion ruleset, as it best applies to the content in this book, using the official SRD rules available at the time of printing. As with any rule changes, you should discuss these alterations with your GM before using them.}

entries.name: Actions
entries: 5.5E created new names for the actions a creature can take. These specific actions don't change how you interact with the game mechanically. Rather, they each describe a category that many types of actions fall under.

items.name: Influence Action
entries: - Any Charisma or Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check used to interact with or change the attitude of a creature.

items.name: Magic Action
entries: - Casting a spell, creating a magical effect, or using a property from a magic item.

items.name: Search Action
entries: - Any Wisdom check (except {@skill Animal Handling}) used to discern something that isn't obvious.

items.name: Study Action
entries: - Any Intelligence check used to recall knowledge or discern clues about something.

items.name: Utilize Action
entries: - Using equipment or otherwise taking the {@action Use an Object} action.

entries.name: Bloodied
entries: "Bloodied" is a term used to describe a creature that has half its Hit Points or fewer remaining. This has no game effect on its own but might trigger other game effects.

entries.name: D20 Tests
entries: "D20 Test" is a term used to refer to all three of the main types of d20 rolls at once: ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws.

entries.name: Emanations
entries: "Emanation" is the term used for an area of effect that extends out to a certain radius from a creature or object in all directions, affecting a sphere around it. It moves with the target unless it is an instantaneous or stationary effect. The target isn't included in the area of effect unless its creator decides otherwise.

entries.name: Heroic Inspiration
entries: "Heroic Inspiration" is the new term used for inspiration.

entries.name: Speed
entries: Whenever the term "Speed" is used by itself (for example, without specifying "Fly Speed" or "Swim Speed"), it simply refers to the creature's walking speed.

entries.name: Species (Ancestries)
entries: Races are now referred to as "Species" in 5.5E (or Ancestries). In addition to the mechanics detailed in these options, you gain the following:

items: One ability score of your choice increases by 2, and another ability score of your choice increases by 1. Alternatively, three different ability scores of your choice increase by 1.
You can speak Common and one other language of your choice.

entries.name: Backgrounds
entries: If you use a 5.5E Background, you don't gain the ability score increases or Origin feat specified. In addition to the benefits granted by the background, you also gain the following:

items: You can speak one additional language of your choice (at the GM's discretion).
You gain one background feature of your choice from an existing 5E background (at the GM's discretion).

entries.name: Feats
entries: 5.5E Feats can be used by implementing the following rules:

items: Level prerequisites for feats can be ignored.
Origin feats can be chosen whenever you would select a feat; if you choose one, one applicable ability score of your choice increases by 1.
Fighting Style feats are considered to be Fighting Styles and can be selected only if you have access to the Fighting Style class feature.

entries.name: Weapons
entries: 5.5E weapons can be used by ignoring their mastery properties.

entries.name: Creature, Dispositions & Spells
entries: There are no changes or alterations that need to be made to creatures, dispositions, or spells.

entries.name: Subclass Changes
entries: The three subclasses found in this book have specific changes unique to them. If a feature isn't mentioned, its 5.5E version can be used in a 5E game without issue.

entries.name: Neko Duelist Fighter
entries: Outsized Trickery feature and Pouncing Fighting Style Feat are altered as detailed below.

entries.name: Outsized Trickery
entries: At 3rd level, you become adept at using the weight of your foes against them. You can attempt to shove any creature, regardless of its size. In addition, your shoves are more potent, imposing an additional effect when you win a contest to shove a creature, depending on whether you choose to push the target or knock it prone.

entries.name: Push
entries: The target is pushed an additional 5 feet away from you, and it takes Bludgeoning damage equal to half your Fighter level (rounded up) + your Strength modifier.

entries.name: Prone
entries: The target takes Bludgeoning damage equal to half your Fighter level (rounded up).

entries.name: Pouncing Fighting Style
entries: The Pouncing Fighting Style Feat becomes a Fighting Style. When a Fighter chooses the Neko Duelist subclass, they can choose to swap a Fighting Style they have with this Fighting Style. Alternatively, they can choose this Fighting Style if they later gain another one.

entries.name: Pouncing
entries: Whenever you move 15 feet or more toward a creature immediately before making a melee weapon attack or unarmed strike against it, you gain a +2 bonus to the attack roll. If you instead attempt to grapple or shove the target, you gain a +2 bonus to your Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check.

entries.name: Fortune Rogue
entries: The Lucky Strike feature is altered as detailed below.

entries.name: Lucky Strike
entries: When you make an attack roll against a creature, you can expend a fortune die to make a Luck check in place of the normal attack roll. On a hit, this attack triggers your Sneak Attack even if it normally wouldn't, provided you haven't already used it this turn.
Immediately after the attack, you can move up to half your speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

entries.name: Coven Warlock
entries: Warlocks choose their Otherworldly Patron at 1st level rather than 3rd, gaining the Coven Spells and Collective Knowledge features, as well as the Bonus Cantrip feature. The Bonus Cantrip feature and the altered Coven Spells feature are detailed below.

entries.name: Bonus Cantrip
entries: You learn the {@spell Borrow Magic|ObojimaTalesYatamon} cantrip. It counts as a warlock cantrip for you, but it doesn't count against your number of cantrips known.

entries.name: Coven Spells
entries: The Coven lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

data.name: Yatamon

entries.name: Yatamon & The Nakudama Empire
entries: AHA explorers and archaeologists have found tantalizing fragments of evidence that prove that nakudama knew of Yatamon during the time of the Nakudama Empire, although strangely, it appears that they did not live in the city. Nakudama emblems representing a person or family can be found throughout Yatamon, especially along the winding river in the green belt known as the Path of Yatamon. In ancient times, emblems were usually left to signify acts of bravery or prowess, but why the nakudama placed them in Yatamon is not clear.

Spread across the rising hills where the Gift of Shuritashi meets the Coastal Highlands, Yatamon stands as the largest city on Obojima and an enduring mystery of the First Age. Its interlaced streets are lined with shops, apartments, houses, and a vast collection of vending machines—one of Yatamon's most popular features. Although the city is large, it is not densely populated. Many of Yatamon's streets are quiet, and the houses that line them sit empty, waiting for people to come and bring life to them. In the settled parts of Yatamon, the city's residents are industrious and friendly, and every neighborhood has its own cast of characters while offering something special—from fine cuisine and exquisite crafts to delightful festivities.

Yatamon is often described to visitors as an unusual and exhilarating place with a culture all its own that moves at a different pace than the rest of the island. Messenger spirits and postal knights race through the city with letters and packages; couriers drive spirit-whelmed kei trucks and mopeds to deliver produce from farms just outside Yatamon to markets all across the city; and apprentice witches run with scrolls sticking out of their satchels, dashing from one client to the next. Yatamon is a city in motion—always at the cutting edge of Obojiman culture, even as it remains one of the island's most ancient places.

entries.name: A Place for Adventure
entries: Like moths to a lantern, adventurers from every corner of Obojima inevitably drift to Yatamon—some drawn by the chance to train under the legendary sword masters Canden and Moon, others eager to study magic at the Witchery, and a few intrepid explorers hoping to uncover the city's troves of First Age relics. But regardless of their motives, all who come to Yatamon experience the initial thrill of losing themselves in the city's colorful, meandering streets. Once there, it doesn't take long before something odd or mysterious happens—usually small and easily missed. Follow a stray cat and it might lead you to a hidden bookstore, or a bird might drop a key at your feet and call your name. Visitors soon find that in Yatamon, magic isn't always cast—sometimes, it simply happens.

entries.name: What Do Obojimans Think?
entries: Most Obojimans have heard of Yatamon—much like people in our world are aware of London, Shanghai, New York, or Tokyo. Compared to Yatamon and Sky Kite Valley, most of Obojima is rural, rustic, and slow-paced. So for those Obojimans who make the journey to visit, Yatamon can be a strange and enormous place, and at times, even bewildering. Seeing so much First Age architecture and technology concentrated in one location may feel exciting to some but overwhelming to others. There are even a rare few who believe Yatamon should be preserved as a museum rather than used as a place to live.

entries.name: Running a Game in Yatamon
entries: In the pastoral and wilderness-filled world of Obojima, to a visitor, Yatamon should feel odd, anachronistic, and subtly magical. It's a place where the many aspects of Obojima converge—First Age relics, spirits, factions, magic, demons, and ancient history—so any kind of game you want to invent is possible here.

If your players have adventurers who are from Yatamon, make sure they understand the tone and rhythm of the place. They might even see people they know when walking through a market. They may have a mental map of the city—even though it's big, a local adventurer knows how to get around without getting too lost.

For adventurers unfamiliar with Yatamon, describe the strange sounds—the fast-moving mopeds, songs from a radio speaker, the rattle and rumble of a trolley—and ask your players to describe how their adventurers react to this unfamiliar world. You might have them make occasional checks to see if they get swept up in the whirlwind of activity—a perfect opportunity to introduce a helpful NPC to the party.

entries.name: Looking Out for Your Neighbor
entries: Unlike your typical D&D fantasy world, in Yatamon (and Obojima in general), town guards, legislators, city officials, and official members of "the Law" are not part of the culture. Rather, Yatamon keeps order through neighborly responsibility, a cultural expectation that folks do what's right in the moment. For residents, that means looking out for each other, contributing to the neighborhood, and having a willing spirit. If a pickpocket strikes, the street sweeper, baker, or other bystanders will come to aid the victim. If caught, the ruffian will certainly get a stern lecture from the elderly flower shop owner, after which someone will offer the wayward soul some food, a bit of work, and a second chance. The population of Yatamon is small enough that repeat offenders become well known and eventually are politely told to leave town. More serious troublemakers are forcibly removed to well beyond the city limits.

entries.name: Helping Hands
entries: Even though there's no hierarchy of leadership in Yatamon, there are influential people—respected elders, generous folks, kindhearted spirits, and helpful kids—who are known in every neighborhood for the many ways they care for its residents. There might be a student who plants flowers in boxes along the streets or an awakened cat that walks people home on dark nights. Yatamon is by no means a utopia, and there are brutes, scoundrels, and scallywags aplenty, but people find ways to take care of their neighborhood and weather perilous moments simply by looking out for one another.

entries.name: Danger in the City
entries: Because it is located in the rolling, grassy hills of the Gift of Shuritashi, lethal danger is not something Yatamon's residents worry about—there are no cold-blooded killers here. The worst they typically face is the beetle-browed braying of some obnoxious lout or a rash of petty theft. But other dangers do occasionally arise—supernatural threats such as demons and cursed items—that cause genuine alarm throughout the community.

In the rare case of a monster attack, residents will rally together, using mops, brooms, rakes, and ladles—and any number of other improvised weapons—to drive off the threat while the fastest among them runs to fetch help from the city's factions, which often serve as a makeshift city guard when real danger comes to Yatamon.

entries.name: Adventure Inspirations
entries: Yatamon is a place where you can have a variety of adventures—from general city intrigue to urban exploration to supernatural detective mysteries. Here are a few possibilities to consider as you brew your own cauldron of story ingredients for an adventure in the First Age city:

entries.name: Exploring the Factions
entries: If your players are curious about having their adventurers join a faction, most of them have their headquarters or a main office here in Yatamon. From witch covens to the Courier Brigade, Yatamon offers the who's who and what's what of Obojima.

entries.name: Wheeling and Dealing
entries: Yatamon is filled with merchants and is well known as a place where explorers can get the best prices for their hard-won loot. It's also where witches and other magic-users can find the rarest items and ingredients for their spells and potions—or at least get information on where to find them. Haggling is an art form in Yatamon, so expect to lay on the charm or risk getting fleeced like a sheep dragon. Sending the adventurers to Yatamon in search of an item—and having them barter for it—can be a fun part of a larger adventure.

entries.name: Undiscovered History
entries: Whether it's First Age relics, the empire of the nakudama, or cryptic glyphs from the First Dara, there are many mysteries to uncover in the city—items and lore that the island's prominent research guild, AHA, and other factions would be grateful to study. Yatamon is also rich in First Age tech, though not everyone knows how to use it. Many of these treasures languish in dusty corners of backyard sheds or are unknowingly used by residents of Yatamon as wall hangings, garden decorations, or pet toys.

entries.name: Find a Master
entries: Be it learning which coven is right for you or joining the sword school of Canden and Moon, Yatamon is an outstanding place to find masters of the island's various crafts and skills.

entries.name: Dara Glyphs
entries: All across Obojima, dara glyphs make for great adventure hooks or side quests for a dara player character. The wanderings of the First Dara are well known, and dara glyphs have been found throughout Yatamon—but with so many nooks and alcoves in the city, there are certainly more waiting to be discovered. A dara glyph could present a mystery, bestow a magical boon, teach a new skill or ability, or contain a vital clue.

entries.name: First Age Weirdness
entries: Because Yatamon is steeped in the mysterious magic of the First Age, unexplained enchantments and curious magical effects can often be found throughout its streets and in the old subway tunnels beneath them. The unique nature of First Age magic makes it quite difficult to replicate— and therefore all the more desirable.

entries.name: Set Up Shop
entries: For entrepreneurial characters, there's no place like Yatamon to start a business. Whether it's a quirky restaurant, a bicycle repair shop, or a mortal–spirit relations service, there are sure to be a host of memorable customers and bristly competitors. Who knows—before long, the business might just become a local institution.

entries.name: That's the Spirit!
entries: If it's spirits the adventurers are looking for, Yatamon has the largest population of spirits in any city due to a famous portal to the Spirit Realm known as the Gap. If your adventure involves finding a certain spirit, uncovering Spirit Realm lore, or investigating a supernatural mystery, Yatamon is a great place to set your tale.

entries.name: Potions Galore
entries: Potions are commonplace in the city and used by all walks of life. From bakers to explorers, most citizens are familiar with and often rely on a handful of potions in their daily routines. This makes Yatamon a prime location to find potions or to learn the craft of making them.

entries.name: Bones of the First Age
entries: On Obojima, the most advanced technology is also its oldest. For as long as anyone can remember—and as far as historians can discern—the island has been home to First Age tech, the peculiar category of technology and architecture, the origins of which are a mystery even to Obojimans of today. Rather than treating it as an oddity, however, the islanders have embraced these First Age relics and integrated them into daily life, making Obojima a place where vaguely medieval and near-modern technology coexist.

Yatamon's residents, more than those of any other city or town, are the most nonchalant about the First Age, as they live within its remnants. Kids scramble up and play on ancient walls, while cats and dogs roam streets that have existed since before the time of the Nakudama Empire. The city hums with the sounds of spirit-whelmed objects—kei trucks zip, trolley cars rumble, and record players crackle—delighting or bewildering outsiders.

Even after centuries of habitation, Yatamon's size far exceeds the needs of its current population, and most of the city lies empty. Rows of vacant houses stand just beyond the lively neighborhood centers, and visitors are encouraged to choose a place to call their own and become part of the city.

entries.name: A City of Magic
entries: It is generally believed that the reason the city of Yatamon doesn't decay is due to the curious magic of the island itself. Obojima's will is often beyond understanding, and yet its inhabitants trust in it wholeheartedly. Most residents feel that if they were not meant to live in Yatamon, Obojima would not have kept it in such pristine condition. Others think that it is less to do with the island's magic and more to do with latent magic left over from the First Age.

Whatever the case, the phenomenon at work is scarcely understood, but most of the island's First Age technology appears to possess an inherent preservative quality that has allowed it to endure for centuries. However, that magic is not unending. Evidence of a larger city can be seen—the Fade Line, where the magic ends and Yatamon abruptly falls into ruins. This ring of rubble around the city is known to residents as Old Yatamon. The zone of ruins extends half a mile or more beyond the parts of Yatamon that are somehow magically preserved.

entries.name: A Blessed People
entries: It is theorized that the magic permeating the city may also "gift" residents the same way it enchants and preserves Yatamon and its First Age relics. Those who live in Yatamon long enough begin to develop some minor magic of their own. Many witches believe this happens because the city seems to know what its residents need and, through some unknown power, it provides a spell to help them. For example, a baker or blacksmith may suddenly gain the ability to conjure flames to aid in their work; an enterprising florist may wake up one morning with the ability to entice flowers to grow; or a hard-working gardener may, through a powerful dream, learn how to till soil in such a way that their plants produce twice the normal yield.

entries.name: City Life
entries: Walk along a street in Yatamon and you'll see rows of houses sheltered by trees, with songbirds singing from the branches. You'll occasionally see a cat sitting in the sun on one of the low walls dividing the front yards, and you're sure to get a friendly wave from a resident tending their garden or hedge. Walk down another street elsewhere in the city and you'll be in the thick of a bustling marketplace—a riot of sounds and smells— with postal knights dashing here and there with packages, and rangers carrying sacks of exotic items from across Obojima to barter with eager merchants.
City life in Yatamon is a mixture of exciting entrepreneurship, vibrant cultural exchange, and quiet domestic life. It is said that the small neighborhoods are where the soul of Yatamon dwells.

entries.name: Community
entries: Although the city is quite large, the relatively small population of Yatamon strives to foster a sense of community much like any village. They rely on their neighbors in times of need and seek friendship through festivals and shared appreciation of the arts. Neighborhoods—which over time have all taken on distinct personalities—work together to solve problems, trade goods, and maintain their part of the city.

entries.name: Caretakers of the Community
entries: The sword school of Canden and Moon has also taken on a special role within the city. In addition to physical training, the masters cultivate a strong ethic of community service in their students, and as a result, you'll often find disciples of Canden and Moon out and about, repairing broken windows, finding lost pets, and assisting the elderly.

entries.name: The Municipal Trolley Line
entries: Through the heart of the city, a modest fleet of street cars winds its way as part of the Municipal Trolley Line. Colloquially known as the "MT" or even the "Empty," the trolley serves as Yatamon's primary option for public transportation. There are stops sprinkled throughout the city, with cars arriving every half-hour (give or take). The routes cover all four neighborhoods, and there are several bridges that cross the Serpent River, offering people riding on the trolley a brief trip through the verdant spaces of Yatamon's Path that can sometimes turn out to be a wild and wooly adventure in itself.

entries.name: Who Runs Yatamon?
entries: Despite its size, Yatamon has no single leader and no official governance. Because of the nature of First Age magic, all the city's municipal functions—plumbing, sanitation, running water—operate automatically, so there's no need for anyone to manage them. Small spirits love to light the streets at night, powering the neon signs and incandescent lampposts—so even lighting is handled in Obojima's magical way.

What Yatamon does have, by way of leadership, are influential individuals who all care about the city and their neighbors in their own particular fashion, and one thing they all agree on is keeping the city from being built upon. Preserving Yatamon's unique First Age look honors both the historical and cultural value of the place—and perhaps avoids disturbing or offending the unknown power that grants First Age sites their incorruptible nature. Many Obojimans are not immune to such superstitions.

Not having any single authority or governor, there are times when a neighborhood must come together to decide what's best for the community. In such moments, a neighborhood gathering is called to determine the best course of action and who among them is best suited to address the concern. In the best of times, this cultivates a kind of harmonious chaos, as entire communities amble toward consensus. However, in times of crisis, residents often rely on the swift action of those willing to act.

entries.name: A Vast Collection of Festivals
entries: Like many villages and towns on Obojima, the people of Yatamon indulge in joyous celebrations of all kinds. Few, however, boast as vast an assortment as Yatamon, its people always ready to lay down their work and gather in the streets for camaraderie and merriment. Yatamon hosts many different festivals throughout the year, but here are just a few:

entries.name: The Dawn Blossom Festival
entries: This major springtime festival is held at the Courier Brigade headquarters. Everyone dresses in festival garb—hats that look like dawn blossom flowers and flowing robes embroidered with dawn blossom trees—and come to the town square to watch as six dawn blossom seedlings take flight aboard the brigade's lantern airship, to be planted in a random location across Obojima. Nearly everyone believes the winds guiding these airships are controlled by Obojima itself, delivering the seedlings to where they're most needed.

entries.name: The Great Slime Hunt
entries: Because they're valued by local witch covens as magic ingredients— and because they clean the city streets—slime populations are allowed to build up within Yatamon. When they get overwhelming, the head of the Witchery calls for the Great Slime Hunt, a city-wide festival during which the apprentice witches (and other enthusiasts) are issued special nets and jars to signify they're trained to hunt slimes. Participants are given one week to collect as many slimes as they can. At the end of the week, a winner is declared. Then, in a festival that culminates the hunt, the participant who caught the most slimes walks with the Witchery's Arch Doyen, Mr. Basingstoke, at the head of a procession that includes coven leaders and other slime hunters. The victor is also awarded a ceremonial slime-catching net and has their name inscribed in the Hall of Slime Hunters located at the Witchery.

entries.name: The Weaving
entries: This festival celebrates the legend of the First Weaver. It is said that long ago, the elder spirit Utmar threatened to destroy Yatamon. A sorcerer known as the First Weaver envisioned a magical garment to trap the spirit. She wove an enchanted fabric so alluring that Utmar donned it and became ensnared, ending the threat to the city. Each year, Utmar is said to return in a new guise, but successive Weavers—guided by visions—create new enchanted garments to thwart the spirit. Some believe the myth is literal and that the festival still protects Yatamon from the Great Spirit Utmar. Most, however, see the legend as a metaphor—symbolically uniting the city in solidarity and fostering community through celebration. Leading up to the unveiling of the Weaver's new garment is a parade, where celebrants create giant humanoid effigies of Utmar, each one dressed in elaborate—and often over-the-top—costumes.

entries.name: Schools & The Youth
entries: In every neighborhood, the residents select a suitable building to serve as a schoolhouse for the local youth. Here, children learn the fundamentals of life in Yatamon, the history of Obojima, and how to live wisely and kindly in a world filled with spirits and ancient magic. Lessons are led by traveling adventurers, mages, herbalists, and other community members, covering everything from practical skills like woodworking and cooking to magic basics, storytelling traditions, and how to spot—and avoid—dangerous creatures. As students come of age, they are encouraged to choose a trade or craft that aligns with their talents and interests. This marks the beginning of their apprenticeship, during which they are paired with a mentor—an experienced practitioner of their chosen path—who offers hands-on instruction, guidance, and challenges tailored to the student's growth. These mentorships are more than job training; they're often lifelong bonds, with mentors helping their apprentices master not only their craft but also their place in the greater weave of Obojima's society.

entries.title: {@font THE SLIME HUNT HAS BEEN A YATAMON TRADITION FOR OVER A CENTURY|Obojima}

entries.name: All Roads Lead to Yatamon
entries: There's a saying on Obojima: "All roads lead to Yatamon." Due to the sheer variety of things Yatamon offers, travelers eventually find themselves on a road heading to the city. When they arrive, they find Yatamon to be a jumble of people and cultures from all over the island—many of whom have heard the same call to come to the First Age city.

Some visitors fall in love with Yatamon and its people, and decide to stay. When this happens, they choose the neighborhood where they wish to settle, and their future neighbors work together to help clean up the house so it is nice and tidy when the new residents move in—an act known to locals as Appawin or "House Revival."

entries.name: A Hub of Trade
entries: Yatamon is a haggler's paradise. Among its many qualities, the city is known for its streets lined with shops and makeshift stalls, and each neighborhood has a main street that hosts an openair market every day. At night, merrymakers and shoppers alike flock to any number of night markets that are set up along winding streets festooned with colorful lanterns and lights— where performers, street food, and all manner of oddities can be found.

Although Copper Buds, Sea Petals, and Golden Flowers are the main currency, shopkeepers in Yatamon are always happy to barter for specific items; witches and foragers deal in potion ingredients, while scavengers and scrappers trade First Age wares to merchants who specialize in ancient tech.

entries.name: Food Trade
entries: Nearly every thriving village and town is essentially an extension of a bountiful farm, fishery, source of natural magic, or other resource that sustains the community. Yatamon breaks that norm, relying instead on the communities around it for nearly all of its agricultural goods. The city is supported by active trade with the farming villages beyond its limits. While there are small gardens within Yatamon, the city depends on a near-constant stream of wagons and kei trucks that bring in food, goods, and magical ingredients to keep it running.

This steady flow of goods often draws the attention of bandits— human and non-human alike. Groups of {@filter howlers|bestiary|source=obojimatallgrass;obojimatalesyatamon|tag=howler}{@sup °} poaching cattle and notorious gangs of thieves pilfering merchant wagons are a well-known problem, and they've been known to operate as close to the city as Old Yatamon—the city's outskirts. More discerning and arcane brigands—such as warlocks, witches, and demons—are always on the lookout for rangers, druids, and Courier Brigade mule trains transporting small batches of uncommon or rare potion ingredients like {@item Crackling Jasper|ObojimaTallGrass}{@sup °}, {@item Nakudama Spice|ObojimaTallGrass}{@sup °}, and the legendary {@item Wufu Whiskey|ObojimaTallGrass}{@sup °}.

entries.name: Fishing
entries: On Obojima, fishing is an integral part of the culture—whether it's a coastal town catching rust crabs and spearing pok pok fish or a village in the snowy heights hunting the dangerous {@creature bearracuda|ObojimaTallGrass}{@sup °}, each practices the tradition in some manner. In Yatamon, fisher folk primarily look to the skies for their quarry. While the Serpent River and other bodies of water provide access to freshwater fish in the city, the flying fish that roam the streets or glide across rooftops are easier targets for most anglers. Though flying fish can be found throughout the city, the general rule is that those fishing shouldn't try to catch anything longer than two feet in a crowded area, which can often lead to "dry days," where most fish worth catching aren't in a position to be caught.

entries.name: Local Delicacies
entries: When it comes to food, Yatamon is known for a few iconic offerings—{@item Happy Joy Cake|ObojimaTallGrass|Happy Joy Cakes}{@sup °}, blurry root, and a First Age delight called Midori Mountain Curry. Happy Joy Cakes were invented by a local baker known as Master Hu and have since become perhaps the most well-known treat in all of Obojima. Blurry root is an alcohol made all across the island, but most would agree that what's produced at the Sun Pig distillery in the Negi neighborhood of Yatamon is by far the most flavorful and most potent on Obojima. Midori Mountain Curry is made in a small kitchen by Mimi Matsuri, a former AHA archaeologist who stumbled upon a massive cache of First Age Midori Mountain-brand curry cubes—now the literal "secret sauce" of her burgeoning curry empire.

Of course, titles like "Obojima's Best" or "Yatamon's Finest" are often disputed, leading to rivalries and outright food wars that can grow quite heated—and occasionally turn vindictive. While the contenders try to uphold honor and decorum, the pressure to become the best can crack even the most reserved temperaments. Unfortunately, this heightened competition sometimes results in outbreaks of food-throwing, name-calling, slanderous smear campaigns, and even acts of sabotage as jealousies boil over.

entries.name: The Sour Spirit Tree
entries: In the Nasu neighborhood, there is a single tree known as the Sour Spirit Tree—the only one of its kind in all of Obojima. Each year, this remarkable tree bears several hundred fist-sized yellow fruits, known for their sour taste and invigorating effect. It is agreed that no one owns the tree and that its fruits should be enjoyed by everyone in Yatamon. Many years ago, a shrine was built around it, and a group of local monks have taken turns caring for the tree ever since. They harvest its fruit and distribute it to chefs, bakers, potion makers, and residents, who use it in dishes, cakes, drinks, and potpourri sachets. The fruit is highly coveted, with all kinds of health benefits and magical properties ascribed to it—making the monks' duty of guarding the tree a 24-hour job.

entries.name: Crime
entries: Obojima is a world essentially free of organized larceny, apocalyptic cults, and premeditated violent crime. People here are cared for, communities thrive, and life is celebrated. There is more than enough food and space for everyone, which alleviates many of the common drivers of criminal behavior. In Yatamon, the court of public opinion is enough to deter most would-be wrongdoers. And because of their tight-knit communities, neighborhoods act as extended families, ensuring every child and young adult receives the care and guidance they need to become balanced members of society—Obojimans do their best to make sure no one heads down the wrong path.

If crime is committed here, it almost never results in grave bodily harm or a city-wide calamity. The rare barroom brawl usually ends in little more than a few bloody noses and a good deal of regret. A thief, once apprehended, receives some tough love from the respected elders of the neighborhood and is met with concerted communal support to prevent a bad habit from forming.

entries.name: What Crimes May Happen
entries: Below you'll find a list of crimes that occur in Yatamon.

items.name: Theft
entries: Prized pastries, magic potions, heirloom woks, and arcane recipes are all fair game on the streets of Yatamon.

items.name: Graffiti
entries: Some kids like to rebel a bit and want to feel significant. Others are budding artists who can't resist turning a blank canvas into something for all to admire. But there's always someone who doesn't appreciate such modes of expression.

items.name: Public Nuisance
entries: Anyone annoying the general public with loud antics, obnoxious behavior, or boorish conduct is dealt with through disapproving looks, stern words, or—if all else fails—a good old-fashioned punch in the chops.

items.name: Brawl
entries: Take any dispute, add a few too many drinks at the tavern, and not even Obojimans are immune to a push turning into a shove and then a wild haymaker.

items.name: Threats
entries: While the list of Obojiman swear words is small, the expressions themselves are quite colorful and can cut to the quick—though the fiery blaze of most shouting matches is quickly doused by the freezing glares of disapproving bystanders.

items.name: Fraud
entries: Many con artists and swindlers are unaware of the trouble they cause, focusing instead on the thrill of their intricate plans, enamored with their own wit and charm, or thinking only of the clink of Gold Flowers falling into their greedy mitts.

items.name: Abduction
entries: A farmer's magic pig, a witch's spirit companion, or even a kindly neighbor might be taken by ne'er-do-wells for one reason or another. That said, most abductors resort to cartoonish bluster and idle threats rather than actual violence, and anyone taken experiences it more as an unpleasant inconvenience or a remarkably rude series of events than a true danger.

items.name: Misuse of Magic
entries: While experienced wizards and witches may occasionally be too ambitious in wielding their powers, the real trouble comes when unskilled dabblers in magic attempt to brew a potion or perform a ritual beyond their ability. It is these reckless experimenters who are usually the ones responsible for accidentally casting a curse, unleashing a monster, or setting fire to a hayfield. Streets filled with fluorescent foam, slime plagues, and other magical mishaps are often crimes of hubris, absent-mindedness, or plain-old stupidity.

Crimes committed with malicious intent—murder, arson, assault, and other acts of willful violence—rarely cross the minds or hearts of most Obojimans, who are steeped in a kind of innocence that gives the world its storybook charm. If Obojimans were capable of premeditated murder, the fairytale feeling of this world would be lost, and it would take on the hardened tone of a world governed by fear or force—great for pulp fantasy, but not for leisure fantasy.

There are exceptions, however. Demons and other monsters have no such compunctions and are perhaps the only entities on the island capable of contemplating anything akin to murder—a fact that keeps those aware of such creatures up at night.

entries.name: Spirits & The Gap
entries: Spirits come to the Physical Realm for all kinds of reasons—most are simply adventurous or curious by nature, but a few might be looking to escape something: a sad story, perhaps, or a past best left forgotten. Some spirits say they come seeking what their realm cannot offer—certain magics that can't be explored and experiences that can't be had.

The Gap, found in Yatamon's Endo neighborhood, is perhaps the best-known portal in the Spirit Realm and across Obojima. Within the Spirit Realm, the Gap serves as a makeshift train station. Spirits gather, bustling about—entering, exiting, asking directions, waving goodbyes, and waiting for someone to arrive. A great deal of trade flows around the entrance to the Gap— both in the Physical Realm and the Spirit Realm—with spirits carrying packages of all sizes back and forth to be delivered to merchants, chefs, and witches who eagerly await them.

Because of the Gap, spirits live in Yatamon in greater numbers than in any other city on Obojima. In fact, Yatamon's vibrant spirit culture is one of the things the city is best known for. The Endo neighborhood has become a thriving hub for spirits, where the customs of the Spirit Realm mix with those of Yatamon to create a unique collection of flavors, arts, magics, and more. That said, Endo is not the only place where spirits reside—Yatamon has spirits of all sizes throughout its neighborhoods, some of which have lived in the city for centuries.

entries.name: Sapient Spirits
entries: Living among the humans, elves, dara, and nakudama in Yatamon are the resident spirits who call the city home. In contrast to the countless bestial or amorphous spirits that visit from the Spirit Realm, these ones live as part of the city's social fabric, running shops and partaking of the local amenities. They might be your noisy neighbor, the local gossipmonger, a corner busker, or a member of the fire brigade. Together, their presence is not remarkable to the other residents of Yatamon, but it is an essential part of the city's wondrous character.

entries.name: Pest Spirits
entries: Like most cities, Yatamon has its fair share of pests, but in addition to the usual mice and bugs, it also has tiny pest spirits like {@creature dustbunny|ObojimaTallGrass|dustbunnies}{@sup °} and {@creature mosslings|ObojimaTallGrass}{@sup °}. Residents of Yatamon have all kinds of ways to deal with such pests—some simply shoo them away with a broom, others rely on heirloom magic charms that repel pests, but the truly desperate turn to a host of awakened cats who charge handsomely to control infestations. However, there are some residents that go along with certain types of pest spirits and, rather than chasing them away, create inviting spaces for them to gather in an effort to contain their antics.

entries.name: Elder Spirits
entries: If there are elder spirits who hold their domains in Yatamon, there is no clear evidence of their presence. Local legends, however, suggest that those who stumble into the wildest parts of Yatamon's Path or the deepest tunnels of the subway system might encounter an elder spirit. The exception to this, is the elder spirit known as {@creature Tamh Gon|ObojimaTalesYatamon}, who is known to visit in times of celebration. Though the city is not Tamh Gon's domain, the elder spirit is said to favor Yatamon above all other settlements.

entries.name: Demons in Yatamon
entries: Yatamon is home to many spirits, thus it is also host to demons. It's unfortunate, but true: where spirits reside, so too will demons. In a place as large as Yatamon, it's only a matter of time before a misguided spirit becomes infected with an insatiable urge or is driven to change by an overwhelming emotion. That said, demons are also drawn to the First Age city for a variety of reasons: abundant food, people to pester, emotions to feed on, ample places to hide—and other spirits to corrupt. Some, like the {@creature goro goro|ObojimaTallGrass}{@sup °}, feed specifically on drunkards sweetened by sake and are therefore tied to human activities like celebrations at inns and taverns.
Other demons form their bodies out of First Age objects or failed works of art, creating dangerous animated artifacts that can also hide in plain sight.

Demons are a spice that, when added to your story, can alter the entire flavor of the game. They are a very versatile monster that can serve a wide range of moods and story roles—from funny or aggravating to unsettling, dangerous, or even utterly horrifying. While Obojima is thematically a world where monsters are often seen as puzzles to be solved through clever roleplaying or by uncovering keys and clues, demons have an extra gear: players can fight and defeat them guiltfree—because demons are irredeemable. Stats for Demons can be found on page 322 of {@i Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass}.

entries.name: Demon Control
entries: Residents of Yatamon are fairly well-versed in dealing with demons, so all but the most clever are quickly discovered and dispatched. But demons are cunning, always seeking new ways to avoid detection—until their desires or compulsions compel them to reveal their true nature.

Most pest demons are of animal intelligence and can be lured and trapped fairly easily by any merchant or homemaker. But as demons grow in cunning and malevolence, professionals— armed with knowledge and powerful magic—must be called in to deal with them.

entries.name: Nakurinas
entries: Nakurinas are a group of whistle-like artifacts originating during the Age of Nakudama that can lure, capture, repel, or temporarily pacify demons. They come in all kinds of sizes and shapes and are usually carved into animal forms like fish, rabbits, dragons, or frogs. Some are long, slender, and flute-like, while others are round and as big as a pumpkin. Though each Nakurina has a sound all its own, all of them deaden every other sound nearby when played.

Demons systematically hunted down and destroyed the knowledge of their creation, and the craft was lost to antiquity— making these mastercraft whistles extremely rare and highly sought after by demons and demon hunters alike.

entries.name: Dealing with Elder Demons
entries: While the Demon Lord Oghmai was considered by many to be the last elder demon to exist on Obojima, some believe others are merely lying dormant or hiding—pulling puppet strings, corrupting spirits, and influencing mortals from their lairs in forgotten corners of the island.
Items powerful enough to affect elder demons are usually dangerous in themselves and are often guarded by spirits or locked away in secret shrines and temples.

Some demons may be so powerful that they can't be destroyed by any means known to mortals. In such cases, the only recourse is to trap the elder demon within warded objects or arcane circles—and hope the binding holds.

entries.name: Death of a Demon
entries: When a demon dies, it dematerializes and its energy disperses in a flash, a crackle, or a slow bubbling hiss, depending on its personality. If no magical care is taken to contain the demon's memories at the moment of its demise, it may imprint on a nearby material form—such as a tree, stone, or the walls of a building—effectively cursing it with their tortured memories.

The effects of these curses are as varied as the demons themselves. Some are mischievous, while others are disturbing, dangerous, or even deadly. Cleaning up these cursed items and areas requires specialized magic—from potions and magic items to ritual spells—and is often not for the faint of heart.

items.name: Charms & Talismans
entries: Over the centuries, wizards, witches, and fumoshiki have invented a myriad of ways to deal with demons—from pesky vegetable thieves to people snatchers. The number of charms and talismans crafted is so vast that many shopkeepers carry them in their shops without knowing how—or if—they work.
Here are a few examples that can be found in Yatamon, should one know what they're looking for:

items: Talismans of earth and sky—said to repel demons that were once nature spirits—are often attached to oscillating fan blades, which spin them continuously.

A specially enchanted jellyfish wind chime can be used to captivate aquatic demons—as long as it is chiming. Some pest demons find the scent of incense made from {@item Bundle of Driko Twigs|ObojimaTallGrass|Driko Twigs}{@sup °} repulsive.
Although unproven, it's said that demons find First Age confetti poppers abhorrent.
Theater masks once worn by bardic performers can be hung above doorways and are said to keep minor demons from crossing the threshold.
Rattle drum noisemakers crafted in the Spirit Realm can be used to pacify demons that feed on sorrowful emotions.

entries.name: First Age Tech
entries: First Age technology has existed on the island since before written history. It has been—and continues to be—one of the island's greatest mysteries. For some Obojimans, the wonders of the First Age still spark curiosity, but most accept it without much thought, giving little heed to something that has always been a part of their world. However, in a place like Yatamon—where there is a preponderance of buildings and items from the First Age— even the most nonchalant traveler might find themselves intrigued by a unique feature of the city.

entries.name: Whelming & Powering
entries: Whelming is a magical process in which a spirit inhabits an object, imbuing it with their energy. In the case of First Age items that have motors, wheels, cathode ray tubes, gears, or electronics, these objects can come back to life—powered by the spirit's inherent magic. While items like lamps, neon signs and bicycles can all be whelmed by a spirit, larger items may require several spirits or a single, powerful one to activate them.

The ability to whelming is common in spirits, especially among minor ones such as pest spirits, but it is not guaranteed that a spirit can—or even knows how to—whelm. When it comes to minor or animalistic spirits, whelming can be comforting or even enjoyable, which is why some choose to live inside First Age objects. In the case of more intelligent spirits, the act of whelming is often seen as a service— performed as part of a livelihood or in trade with others.

Through the study of whelming, wizards eventually devised the spell {@spell Jolt|ObojimaTallGrass}{@sup °}, which allows an object to function temporarily as if it were whelmed. This simple bit of magic is now well known throughout Obojima, and if cast repeatedly into a First Age object over the course of a year, it can power the device permanently. Alternatively, some witches have learned the art of spirit sealing, which allows them to seal a minor spirit into a First Age object—in order to power it.

entries.name: Phone Booths
entries: In Yatamon, the glass cases of First Age phone booths have been repurposed for all kinds of uses by vendors and shrine crafters throughout the city. The booths are usually repainted and decorated by their proprietors, and then given new life as simple sales stalls or as shrines to bygone spirits and community members. However, some booths remain unclaimed by individuals and are instead owned and operated by the Arcane Telecom Organization—a spirit-run business that offers services, information, and advice through their phone booths and payphones all across Yatamon.

Telecom phones, marked by their iconic green booths, can be used by any individual willing to pay the small fee for a call—and will be immediately connected to one of the many spirits who operate the private lines. Their services range from simple tasks—like offering information on the city or sending a spirit operated bicycle to shuttle you around—all the way to complicated requests, such as connecting you with a specific person or locating an object for you within the city.
Attempts have been made to provide this beloved service outside of the city limits, but the magics that power the phones aren't as stable elsewhere and often fail.

entries.name: Radio Dishes
entries: Although they're not as common as other First Age relics, the metal dishes still installed on the rooftops of buildings across Yatamon have become a useful tool for urban agriculture, as most of them are now used to house small gardens or fruit trees. Druids believe it's the magic of the First Age leaking from the dish that helps the plants grow, and some locals claim it gives the fruits produced inside the city a "First Age flavor."

entries.name: Televisions
entries: Televisions are used for many purposes all across the island, but they are especially popular in Yatamon for their ability to help nonverbal spirits communicate with others. This is true of many First Age objects, but televisions allow for both an auditory and visual representation of the spirit's messages. Because of this, televisions are kept in many shops, restaurants, markets, and even on the streets of the city.

entries.name: Vending Machines
entries: As a relic of the First Age, Yatamon has the highest concentration of vending machines in all of Obojima—in fact, it may have more than the rest of the island combined. Because humans have lived here for centuries, every known vending machine in the city has been claimed by a wizard, witch, or spirit. These machines may contain anything from potion ingredients and strange curios to snacks and drinks—whatever the proprietor wishes to stock inside. However, a few vending machines remain undiscovered, some even containing items dating back to the time of the nakudama or the First Age.

entries.title: {@font OMPO AND OTHER PEST SPIRITS SUCH AS THE BUTTON CROW ONLY CAME INTO EXISTENCE AFTER THE CREATION OF LARGE CITIES SUCH AS YATAMON.|Obojima}

entries.name: Stoplights
entries: Most stoplights and crosswalk signals have been altered and repurposed to deliver simple citywide messages. Some have been outfitted to inform the community about flying fish in the area, issue weather warnings, and signal the beginning of festivals, while others announce the sighting of a Great Beast, alert citizens to an incoming caravan, or warn of monsters in the area.

entries.name: Public Trash Cans
entries: In Yatamon, ompo—mouse-like spirits formed from scraps of fabric and other rubbish—collect at the bottoms of trash cans. Ompo consume anything and everything tossed their way, living most of their short lives inside one the many trash cans found throughout the city. When an ompo finally feels that its hunger is satiated, it leaves its trash can to explore the city and find a place to rest. There, it goes to sleep and allows its body to dissipate, releasing a subtle magic into the area around it. Most believe this is the spirit's quiet way of giving back to the island.
{@font OMPO MEANS FRIENDLY CLEANER IN TORUM|Obojima}

entries.name: Cats in the City
entries: You might not notice it right away, but just beneath your knees lies a thriving culture of cats. It exists both within and alongside Yatamon's wider cosmopolitan culture, with its beating heart at the Eminence Hotel in the Endo neighborhood. Yatamon boasts a large number of awakened cats, many of whom find employment with the city's myriad shops and services, for in Yatamon, more than any other place on the island, the presence of cats is regarded by its residents as a sign of good fortune.

entries.name: On the Nature of Cats
entries: Cats are special. Awakened or not, most possess gifts that border on the supernatural. Some can see invisible creatures and objects; others can sniff out spirits—and even identify those on the cusp of becoming demons.

entries.name: General Attitude Toward Cats
entries: When interacting with a cat, it's common to ask for its name before assuming its intelligence. This is just one of the many practices Yatamon's citizens employ to ensure the awakened cat community feels respected. Those who did not grow up in the city might not understand the complexities of the awakened cats' rich culture, and how it intermingles with Yatamon's, but the people of the First Age city are not foolish enough to assume simplicity in their feline friends. Overall, the people of Yatamon greatly respect the cats that live within the city limits, awakened or not, working alongside them and appreciating their outlook on life.

entries.name: Awakened Cats & Dreaming Cats
entries: A "dreaming" cat, according to cat culture, is one who has not been awakened. Though opinions vary from cat to cat, awakened cats generally regard dreaming cats without much thought to the difference. It's common for cats—whether dreaming or awakened—to interact regularly with one another, and they seem able to communicate with each other without any fuss.

entries.name: Working Cats
entries: Awakened cats have discovered that employment allows them to live entirely on their own terms, independent of what a dreaming cat might experience in its day-to-day life in the city. Due to their general desire for comfort, cats gravitate toward jobs in the city that suit both their skills and their temperament. Many business owners believe that it's good luck to keep a cat in the shop, and many cats collect pay to greet customers and keep an eye out for troublemakers. As elsewhere on Obojima, some cats have been enlisted to guard vending machines, while others are contracted to get rid of pest spirits. A few awakened cats even work as au pairs, helping to raise children.

entries.name: In Exchange for Service
entries: Across the island, awakened cats are commonly employed as guardians of vending machines that dispense potions and other magical miscellany. As part of the arrangement, these cats often insist on being taught a cantrip. It's therefore likely that a cat who can cast spells once served as a vending machine guardian.

entries.name: The Information Trade
entries: Several entrepreneurial cats have also cornered the information trade in Yatamon, operating their brokerages primarily out of the Eminence Hotel. They offer clients a range of intelligence-gathering services by tapping into a network of cats that work throughout the city. Their informants, detectives, and spies can track people down or uncover secrets. There's not much that goes on in Yatamon that the cats don't know about.

entries.name: The Significance of Agate
entries: The magic that awakens creatures relies upon agate as a material component. Therefore, most awakened cats treasure the stone and carry a small piece with them at all times. Some believe that they must conduct a ritual with agate, or else their awakened state might diminish. The details of such rituals vary wildly—some cats are said to stockpile the stone, arranging it in arcane patterns around them as they sleep, while others might carve it into effigies of themselves. The merits of these rituals are unclear, but the superstition certainly persists.

entries.title: {@font CAMMY OF THE AMBER PAPER COMPANY|Obojima}

items.name: Tradition of Craft
entries: Awakened cats don't only work for others—many engage in a range of traditional crafts, some of which they've become quite famous for in Yatamon.

items.name: Box Making
entries: This woodworking craft showcases impressive joinery skills that often bring woods of different hues together to form elaborate geometric patterns. These boxes are highly prized among cats as beds, though they are also coveted by the city's wider population.

items.name: Needle Felting
entries: Though cats often find it difficult to concentrate on the fiber arts—thanks in large part to the reliance on balls of yarn— one craft in which they have truly excelled is felting. Using their claws, awakened cats can rapidly create all kinds of felted objects, the most popular of which are figurines of tiny animals dressed as Young Stewards.

items.name: Game of Mouser
entries: Awakened cats produce and play a strategy game called Mouser. In the game, each player controls a cat piece, hoping to catch one of several mouse pieces on the board. The best Mouser sets are crafted by cats, and the most prized pieces are made from bone and etched by cat claws.

items.title: {@font A WELL CRAFTED MOUSER SET IS A GENERATIONAL HEIRLOOM AND CAN BE QUITE VALUABLE.|Obojima}

entries.name: Cats in Factions
entries: Awakened cats are found in many factions (see information on factions on the next page) that are active in Yatamon. Coven witches and the researchers of AHA are the most likely to include cats, but they can be found among nearly any faction. It's not uncommon to see one cat trotting down the street with an envelope in its teeth on an errand for the Courier Brigade, or another leading a gaggle of Young Stewards to a fishing spot along the river.

entries.title: {@font MR. BENNETT IS WELL KNOWN AND RESPECTED BY MANY LEADERS AND IMPORTANT MEMBERS OF YATAMON'S FACTIONS, THE MOST NOTABLE BEING HIS OLD AND CHERISHED FRIENDSHIP WITH THE WITCHERY'S ARCH DOYEN, MR. BASINGSTOKE|Obojima}

entries.name: Neko Duelist Fighting Technique
entries: A legend on Obojima speaks of a cat guardian who appears when danger arises, brandishing a sword in its teeth to drive off those who would do evil. In some tales, the cat is orange, with a notch in one ear; in others, it's all black except for one white paw. In Yatamon's version, an old alley cat with crooked whiskers and fur the color of dirty dishwater speaks in rhyme and stalks the howlers who find their way into the city from time to time. However the tale is told, all agree that the cat wields a sword like a master.

What the legends describe is a cat who has mastered the Neko Duelist swordfighting technique. The practice is one of the most closely guarded secrets in cat culture. There are only a handful of masters on the island, and their feats are legendary. On rare occasions, a master might agree to take on a non-cat pupil—but only if they prove themselves worthy of the tradition.

entries.name: Yatamon Factions
entries: This section describes factions that are unique to the First Age city of Yatamon and how they function within the city.

entries.name: Honorable Warriors In-Training
entries: In the heart of Yatamon, the Canden and Moon Sword School stands as both a prestigious martial academy and a cornerstone of civic life. While famed across Obojima for its graceful, swift style—elegant as dance, yet lethal as lightning—the school is more than a place to learn the sword; it is a training ground for character, discipline, and public service.

Students are taught that mastery lies not only in perfect form, but in honorable conduct. This philosophy is lived out daily. After rigorous morning training beneath the rustling leaves of Master Canden's maple tree, students scatter across the city to give back. Junior students patrol the city, clean streets, and help the elderly, while senior students judge festival contests, escort scholars studying Old Yatamon, and occasionally confront monsters that stray too close to the city limits.

Though neither of its legendary founders seeks power, the school's influence on Yatamon is profound. In times of crisis, it is the sword school that stands as the city's shield. Most citizens have encountered its students—whether as protectors, helpers, or even as brief classmates. Few will ever face the masters in a duel, but all benefit from their vision: a community strengthened by beauty, discipline, and service.

entries.name: Demon-Hunting Vigilantes
entries: The Yoka Scouts are a gang of about thirty teenagers and young adults whose unofficial goal is to safeguard the neighborhoods of Yatamon from demons by tracking and removing them from the city. The members of the Yoka Scouts claim to be the eyes and ears of the community, working in small groups day and night to keep constant watch over the city streets.

Despite their admirable goals and useful skills, the Yoka Scouts are not universally well received by the residents of Yatamon. While most see them as providing a valuable service—facing dangers that others would rather not face—they are also known for being reckless, sometimes leaving taverns, shops, or residences in shambles after rough-and-tumble takedowns of their demonic foes. Some wonder if the Yoka Scouts are more trouble than they're worth and would rather rely on the levelheaded, disciplined members of Canden and Moon's sword school rather than the more impulsive Yoka Scouts.

entries.name: Origin
entries: The Yoka Scouts claim that long ago, the first scout was a ranger by the name of Yoka, whose family was killed by an urugama{@sup °} while she was away. Distraught and heartbroken by the loss, Yoka snapped. She abandoned everything to search the island for the demon that had taken her loved ones, but after a decade of hunting, she was left empty-handed. With nowhere left to turn and no use for her heart, she traded it to a wise spirit in exchange for the skills of demon hunting.

entries.name: All Together
entries: The Yoka Scouts do not have a headquarters; instead they gather at various locations around Yatamon, in the ruins of Old Yatamon, and within the subway system, where they hold impromptu meetings and training sessions. Members are alerted through word of mouth spread by the younger members of the group.

The Yoka Scouts don't have a single leader; rather, they are guided by three senior members. These senior scouts have access to all of the demon-hunting lore and magic items the Yoka Scouts have collected over the years.

entries.name: Yoka's Credo
entries: "A heartless blade is a fearless blade. Only that can slay a demon." —Yoka

Holding true to their credo, the Yoka Scouts endeavor to put demon hunting above all else, each for their own reasons. Being a Yoka Scout is not merely a civic duty. For some, it's a reason to swagger; for others, a sacred calling; and for a few, a pursuit carried out with what some residents of Yatamon would call fanatical fervor.

items.title: {@font A HEARTLESS BLADE IS A FEARLESS BLADE. ONLY THAT CAN ONLY THAT CAN SLAY A DEMON|Obojima}

entries.name: Factions of Obojima
entries: This section describes factions that have a presence throughout Obojima and how they function within the city of Yatamon.

items.name: Academic Adventurers
entries: Housed within a First Age library, the Yatamon branch of AHA is focused mainly on the archaeology of the First Age—especially the technology—and on uncovering more clues about the lives and culture of the ancients. The AHA office in Yatamon houses many different examples of First Age tech, along with cabinets full of documents unearthed from that era. It is also host to an ongoing procession of symposia and exhibitions on all manner of academic topics, all of which are free to attend. Many nearby taverns are frequented by AHA members, who speculate about their latest theories and discoveries late into the night.

entries.name: Insightful Spirits
entries: During the early days of AHA, a discovery was made in Yatamon concerning the nature of spirit-whelmed technology. The companion spirit of Dr. Emily P. Whistleton demonstrated an exceptional level of understanding of a First Age device when whelming it. Soon thereafter, AHA concluded that some spirits possess an innate ability to discern the function and unique properties of First Age objects when whelming them for the first time. This discovery began a long working relationship with spirits, which continues to this day.

items.name: Knights of the Postal Service
entries: Housed in what was once a First Age bank, the Courier Brigade headquarters is perhaps the most secure place on all of Obojima. The thick steel vault doors are unlike any other metal on the island, and the brigade keeps parcels safe behind them. It's not uncommon to see a visiting blacksmith inspecting and admiring the vault's massive doors and complex lock. On the roof of the headquarters is a landing pad for the Courier Brigade's famous giant flying lantern, a main attraction during the Dawn Blossom Festival.

It is here that Courier Brigade hopefuls are trained in all the skills needed to become successful postal knights under the tutelage of Miranda Escalante, the senior knights, and even guest instructors from the Witchery and from Canden and Moon's sword school.

items.title: Yasamin: {@font KNIGHT OF THE POSTAL SERVICE|Obojima}

items.name: Youth Scouts
entries: There are chapters of the Young Stewards across the island, and here in Yatamon, each neighborhood has its own chapter where kids of all ages learn the skills and ethics of being a proper steward of Obojima. The chapters enjoy fun and friendly rivalries across the city as they practice their skills and live out their code, earning merit badges for doing good deeds. Young Stewards learn mapmaking, insect study, gardening, and a host of other skills—along with how to be a good neighbor and deal with slimes that might crawl up from the sewers or subway stations. Everyone in Yatamon knows a Young Steward or two, who are often seen walking the city in search of new ways to hone their skills and earn badges.

Young Stewards are also one of the best sources of information about Yatamon's Path and the ruins of Old Yatamon, as troops often explore and camp out in such places. Many of the artifacts housed within the AHA Library come from intrepid scouts who bring back the occasional find.

items.name: Witches Bound to Each Other by Oaths
entries: Although most witch covens are scattered across Obojima, it's rare to find all of them represented in one place—and Yatamon is one of those places. The Witchery is a school founded long ago to help budding witches discover their talents and choose a coven to serve. There are many uses for witches in the bustling city of Yatamon, as it is a hub for travelers, merchants, and adventurers in need of potions, magic items, and spellcraft. Many witches who graduate from the Witchery go on to open their own shop on the streets of Yatamon, set up a stall in the Yanari Witches' Market, or wander Obojima as roaming apothecaries, helping all they meet along the way.

entries.name: Goods, Services & Dwellings
entries: For those willing to pay, Yatamon offers a variety of goods and services. Below is a list of costs for common goods and services available in the city, along with a guide to housing in Yatamon or starting a shop there.

entries.name: Creature Beacon
entries: Arcane Telecom's simple but effective service can tell you over the phone which neighborhood a person is in. For a small fee and a detailed description of the creature you're looking for, you'll have an answer within minutes.

entries.name: Cursing Contracts
entries: Cursing contracts have existed on Obojima for centuries, though their use in today's age is uncommon due to their dangerous nature. A cursing contract binds two individuals to a written agreement, which both parties must fulfill in the allotted time or face the effects of the curse. The magic involved in this enchantment is so powerful that the resulting curses are often well beyond the caster's natural ability. Cursing contracts can be made by powerful witches and wizards throughout the city, though it may take some convincing.

entries.name: Minor Curse Removal
entries: Simple curses can often be removed by a local witch for the cost of spell components and services.

entries.name: Pathfinding
entries: Skillful awakened cats often offer their services as rangers and guides through the denser parts of Yatamon's Path and Old Yatamon.

entries.name: Repair
entries: To take a damaged First Age object or vehicle and make it operational again is no small feat—and often, it's not possible, which is why a skilled mechanic or crafter charges as they see fit when they do successfully fix your item.
For more information on repairing a vehicle that is already operational, see the {@book Vehicles|ObojimaTallGrass|9} section.

entries.name: Spell Storing
entries: For a small fee, local witches and wizards are more than happy to cast one of their spells into a cassette, VHS tape, or cartridge for casting by the customer at a later time, so long as the object can hold the magic.

entries.name: Taxi
entries: The Arcane Telecom Company offers a spirit-whelmed taxi service that will take you across the city for a small fee. These taxis take on all shapes and sizes, from bikes and motorcycles to large vans, all of which are powered and controlled by one of Arcane Telecom's skilled spirit drivers.

entries.name: Vacancy Inspections
entries: When a new citizen wishes to occupy a vacant building in Yatamon, it's common to hire an awakened cat with strong supernatural senses to inspect the building first. While searching the building, the inspector looks for unruly magic, dormant curses, hidden demons, and unwanted pest spirits. This service is commonly known as a Vacancy Inspection.

entries.name: Wax Sealing
entries: When delivering a package through the Courier Brigade, customers are given the option to "iron seal" their parcel, which magically binds and holds the object in a chest until it is delivered. Although it's less common, this same service can also be used to seal objects or doors for customers, even when not utilizing delivery services.

entries.name: Whelming
entries: Spirits throughout the city offer their skills to temporarily power First Age objects for paying customers.

entries.name: Vacant Buildings
entries: Many who visit Yatamon soon discover that, outside the dense pockets within the four neighborhoods, most of the buildings are empty, with only the occasional silent school of fish floating along the city's tree-lined boulevards. On Obojima, and especially within Yatamon, an empty building is considered an object of sadness at best and a temptation for pest spirits and demons at worst. Yatamon's locals are generally a welcoming lot, so travelers are encouraged to settle down and make the city their home. There's even an unofficial yet ongoing competition among the four neighborhoods to see which will be the first to fill all their empty houses, encouraging innkeepers and restaurateurs throughout the city to gently suggest their neighborhood to any potential home seeker.

Most empty buildings are in need of a good cleaning, and some contain odd trinkets or even First Age items left behind. Other buildings may have pest spirits or demons that need removing, and in rare cases, a monster or other dangerous creature has taken up residence—the same is true for mysterious curses or other nefarious relics of unruly magic, which is why vacancy inspections have become a popular suggestion among locals.

Once a building is ready, a person can simply choose it and make it their home, or, as is most often the case, locals will get wind of a traveler's intentions and turn move-in day into a mini festival, with neighbors pitching in to help provide everything the new occupants need to get their lives in Yatamon started.

entries.name: Local Superstitions
entries: Koroko Alleyway is a side street in Yatamon where a row of nakudama businesses has existed for centuries. For one week in late fall, all of the merchants in Koroko Alleyway hang spirals of dried fruit peels outside their shops to honor Yatamon.

On rainy days, many locals extinguish the lanterns outside their homes or turn off any device with a light bulb—offering small nature spirits a place to whelm and stay warm. To have a spirit choose to inhabit one is a sign of good fortune.

entries.name: Yatamon City Map
City Layout
entries: Yatamon is divided into four neighborhoods, each named after the main street that runs through it—Kinoko, Nasu, Endo, and Negi. Each neighborhood functions like a small town unto itself, with local elders and residents who ensure that everyone's concerns are taken care of.

Though the neighborhoods have their own flavor and particular points of interest, they each have the basic amenities and shops one would expect to find in a city the size of Yatamon. Parkland and green spaces are scattered throughout the city. Corner groceries and farmers markets handle the residents' everyday needs, while all kinds of cafés, restaurants, and taverns offer folks places to gather and enjoy local culinary delights. Each neighborhood has its share of apothecaries and healers, as well as volunteer fire brigades, nakudama hatcheries, and trolley stops.

Because it is Obojima, neighborhoods are generally safe; only those areas where Yatamon's Path grows wild, or that lie closest to the ruins of Old Yatamon, are considered potentially dangerous— especially at night.

The sections below highlight some of the noteworthy spots unique to each neighborhood. Some locations in Yatamon are described in {@i Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass}. Those locations are listed here under their respective neighborhoods; see that book for detailed information.

entries.name: The Outer Ruined City
entries: Old Yatamon lies just beyond the city proper, a stretch of ruins that extends outward half a mile or more. Most of it peeks through the grass, trees, and earth that have covered and eroded the walls, foundations, and streets of what once was the rest of Yatamon.

Old Yatamon is a silent and mysterious place where, for reasons unknown, the buildings, streets, and machinery of the First Age have deteriorated normally. This invisible boundary, where Yatamon abruptly gives way to the ruins of Old Yatamon, is known by locals as the Fade Line, a strange anomaly where the preservative magic that has held Yatamon's structures together for millennia has failed, allowing Obojima to reclaim ancient subway stations, streets, and buildings, burying them in earth and vegetation as they slowly return to the land.

entries.name: Dangers
