entries: Along with a variety of hazards—such as unstable structures and sinkholes that lead to underground spaces—Old Yatamon is home to {@filter howlers|bestiary|source=obojimatallgrass;obojimatalesyatamon|tag=howler}{@sup °}, {@creature hill dragon|ObojimaTallGrass|hill dragons}{@sup °}, and other creatures that make their lairs within and underneath the crumbled, overgrown ruins. Demons also seem to enjoy lurking in Old Yatamon, perhaps due to the absence of preservative magic or because they are attracted to the merchants with their wares who must pass through the ruins on their way to and from the city.

entries.name: The Fade Line
entries: The Fade Line is one of the great mysteries that witches and members of AHA are trying to understand. This invisible border has puzzled people for generations. Faint traces of magic can be detected in all the First Age buildings of Yatamon, but that magic wanes as soon as the Fade Line is crossed. Whatever caused the magic to disappear is a mystery lost to time. However, some theories suggest the Fade Line has shifted in the last 200 years—the most recent movement caused an entire city block to collapse, a tragedy that gave rise to the {@creature rubble golem|ObojimaTallGrass}{@sup °}, Udo (see {@book Udo's Shrine|ObojimaTalesYatamon|3|Udo's Shrine}). Because of this event, several researchers are studying the Fade Line closely in hopes of detecting future shifts early.

entries.name: The Fade Arch
entries: This stone archway stands on the Fade Line, marking the beginning of Old Yatamon. The citizens of Yatamon have turned the stone threshold into a kind of shrine that memorializes the lost part of the city. To most adults, it's a place to pay quiet respect to their home. In contrast to their parents' beliefs, the children of Yatamon hold a wide variety of outlandish superstitions and rumors about the archway—the most common being that passing under the shrine seven times in quick succession can cause all sorts of bad luck, and in the most horrible cases, the Curse of Old Yatamon.

entries.name: The Buried Market
entries: Covered by trees and vegetation lie the remnants of what was once a great marketplace. Adventurers and AHA members who know its location come here to dig among the roots and old foundations in search of First Age trinkets. However, howlers have caught on and, for decades now, have patrolled the area looking for easy shakedowns of occupied excavators—making treasure hunting in the market a dangerous affair.

entries.name: Collapsed Subway
entries: Amid a tangled snarl of roots, rusting pipes, and crumbling rubble lies a large hole in the ground that leads to what was once was an underground arcade in Yatamon's subway system. The giant hole now acts as a skylight, illuminating the abandoned machines left in the ruins. Although this might seem a prime site for excavation and exploration by AHA, many avoid this place, as it is said that {@creature urugama|ObojimaTallGrass}{@sup °} and other foul demons are known to frequent the area.

entries.name: Agumon's Crossroad
entries: Dirt roads crisscross all over Old Yatamon, but at one particular intersection, a shrine has been erected. Legend has it that the crossroad was the site of a historic battle and final stand of the hero, Agumon, who died defending the city. Obojimans still visit this shrine, leaving offerings in honor of the fallen hero.

entries.name: Beyond City Limits
entries: Yatamon rests among the southern hills of the Gift of Shuritashi, where the land gently descends toward the Shallows and the cliff faces where the southern branch of the Coastal Divers' Lodge is located. Outside the city, the ruins of Old Yatamon blend into the rolling hills and grasslands that surround it, and clumps of woodland nestle in small valleys where streams and rivers flow down to the ocean.

To the northwest lies Lake Ellior—one of Obojima's largest lakes and a site sacred to the ancient nakudama. To the east, the land grows more rugged as the rocky crags of the Coastal Highlands begin to emerge from the lush green grass of the Gift of Shuritashi.

Because of Old Yatamon's position on the other side of the Fade Line, there are places where First Age tech ceases to work. These areas seem to randomly move, causing items to fizzle and then sputter back into life as soon as the anomaly moves on, much like a cloud temporarily blocking sunlight.

entries.name: "The Path"
entries: Yatamon's Path is a greenbelt surrounding the Serpent River, which winds down from Lake Ellior, through the city, and out toward the southern cliffs of the island. Over the centuries, some of this greenery has been cultivated and shaped by various artisans, sages, and green-thumbed residents of Yatamon, who voluntarily sculpted pathways, pruned trees, and built small shrines and bridges within the park—both to entice nature spirits to dwell here and for the enjoyment of all.

Yatamon's Path features many varieties of trees, shrubs, and flowers, along with massive moss-covered boulders. Groves of maple, dogwood, cedar, ginkgo, camphor, and thick patches of bamboo grow near the meandering river. Small waterfalls and areas where the river widens and slows into ponds, and the occasional thoughtfully placed stone or wooden bench offers a place for wanderers to rest and take in the surrounding beauty.

entries.name: Serpent River
entries: Snaking through Yatamon's Path is the Serpent River—a slowmoving, clear river that originates from Lake Ellior, flows through Yatamon, and empties into the Shallows in a spectacular waterfall known as Serpent Tongue Falls. Mostly, the Serpent River is used by the locals for recreation and for transporting both people and goods.
The Serpent River is generally around 50 yards wide—narrowing to 20 yards in places and widening up to as much as 80 to 100 yards at its broadest.

Everything from freshwater fish to spirits lives in the river. In the deepest waters, the occasional behemoth—such as the {@creature Lanternback Turtle|ObojimaTalesYatamon}—has taken up residence, although most of the lairs of these potentially dangerous denizens are well known by the local rangers, Young Stewards, and druids.

entries.name: Dangers
entries: Large swathes of Yatamon's Path remain wild and uncultivated, hiding ancient secrets overgrown with vines and moss. These are the places where ne'er-do-wells skulk with their ill-gotten loot and where monsters are known to lurk in hidden lairs. Because it follows the Serpent River, Yatamon's Path extends beyond the city limits, through the ruins of Old Yatamon, eventually joining the meadows and forests to the south, where the landscape slopes down to the cliffs overlooking the Shallows.

The Serpent River is also home to water spirits and a place where more than a few monsters are known to lurk—especially in parts where the water runs deep and the current slows. {@creature Hill dragon|ObojimaTallGrass|Hill dragons}{@sup °} and {@filter howlers|bestiary|source=obojimatallgrass;obojimatalesyatamon|tag=howler}{@sup °} have been known to establish dens in the ruins of Old Yatamon, and the smells from the city—especially during festivals—are sometimes too much to resist. Sneaking in via the Serpent River is an all-too-tempting proposition.

entries.name: Notable Areas
entries: Below are just a handful of the many intriguing locations that can be found along Yatamon's Path.

entries.name: Pond of 10,000 Bubbles
entries: From the center of this pond rises a constant stream of tiny bubbles, forming a natural fountain that foams in a dazzling, reflective display before dissipating at the edge of the water.

entries.name: Okumi's Tree
entries: This ancient banyan tree now serves as a shrine dedicated to Queen Okumi of the ancient nakudama.

entries.name: Boar Bridge
entries: This bridge made of wood and woven vines is shaped like a razorback boar. Rattan canes stick up along its length like bristles on a boar's back. Sometimes, the spirit that lives in the bridge snorts—a sound considered a blessing, especially if you are crossing at the time. Children like to stand on the bridge shouting, "Snort! Snort! Snort!" in hopes the spirit will bowl them over with a thunderous snort.

entries.name: Nakudama Stones
entries: Dotted throughout Yatamon's Path—and some parts of the city—are ancient stones, most of them the size of a small gravestone, which many believe have been there since the Nakudama Empire. All evidence uncovered by AHA points to that being true. No one knows what these stones were used for, but legend has it that, every now and then, the stones hum. This legend has never been confirmed by AHA, but some locals have stories—even personal accounts—of the stones giving off an audible and strange vibration.

items: There are many subway stations throughout Yatamon and in the ruins beyond the city. Most of the stations in Old Yatamon are overgrown—appearing as large clumps of brush or mounds of moss-covered earth, with only a sign to alert passersby that a station is hidden there. The subway stations within the city proper have all been cleared of debris, but the entrance gates are almost always boarded up—to keep adventurous children out, and to keep any monsters that may lurk below, in.
Once underground, the subway system extends for miles—some tunnels may still connect to other stations across Obojima, while others have collapsed or become lairs to demons and other entities.

items.name: Dangers
entries: Generally, the subway system is deserted, with only the occasional echo from somewhere deep within the tunnels—but anything can be down here, from monsters to demons to brigands. It's widely believed that when you enter the subway, it's not a matter of if you'll find trouble, but when. And the deeper you venture into the subway system, the weirder it gets.

Because the subway is generally avoided by the residents of Yatamon, it is still filled with undisturbed objects and rooms from the First Age. This is why, although most steer clear, there are still plenty who seek to explore it.

entries.name: Turnaround Tunnels
entries: This stretch of tunnels on the third level down has a knack for getting travelers hopelessly lost. Once inside, it becomes seemingly impossible to retrace one's steps or follow the logic of a map. The walls of the Turnaround Tunnels are scrawled with the desperate ravings of those stuck within the subterranean labyrinth. Some who return from the ordeal claim to have followed a mote of pink light, while others say that a pink light led them to peril. One person says that they were guided out by a green carpet of {@creature mosslings|ObojimaTallGrass}{@sup °}.

entries.name: Blue Line Howler Camp
entries: Deep under Yatamon lies a derelict station along the Blue Line where a group of a dozen or so {@filter howlers|bestiary|source=obojimatallgrass;obojimatalesyatamon|tag=howler}{@sup °} have established a camp. Led by the scheming Tufkit, the howlers survive by eating vermin and fungi, and by extorting the occasional surface dweller who strays too deep into the subway tunnels.

entries.name: Station 26
entries: In Yatamon's Path, there is a grove of {@creature Watchwood Tree|ObojimaTallGrass|watchwood trees}{@sup °}. Within this grove sits an overgrown subway station entrance that few people know about. Its name has been worn away over the years; the only thing that remains legible is the number "26" pressed into the station's concrete entrance. Most of the twisting maze of corridors within Station 26 is flooded— sometimes deep enough that explorers must swim to reach the main platform, where a shrine to an {@creature Elder Dragon Frog|ObojimaTallGrass|ancient dragon frog}{@sup °} stands. Who tends to the shrine is unknown to the people of Yatamon, but a recent rumor suggests that the head of the Witchery, Mr. Basingstoke sees to the shrine personally at the behest of his octopus familiar, Sorrow.

entries.name: Radish Boys' Hang Out
entries: One of the shallower tunnels running beneath Yatamon's Negi neighborhood is the hideout of a group of thieves known as the Radish Boys. Their base is a pair of linked train cars that can be relocated when things get too hot. The Radish Boys are notorious for targeting Courier Brigade wagons in hopes of stealing ingredients, which they later sell at the Yanari Market. The gang is led by a radish spirit turned demon named Feronus, who seems to have an axe to grind with the Courier Brigade.

entries.name: Gilly's Restaurant
entries: On a well-lit platform that looks as though it was cleaned yesterday sits a 25-foot-long railcar that has been pulled off the tracks. The neon sign across the top of the railcar reads "Gilly's Restaurant," named for the spirit who runs it. What makes the place so remarkable is that the actual restaurant lies in the Spirit Realm. When customers are led through the railcar's doorway, they pass through a portal into a small, cozy, and tastefully decorated dining space. Few people know of Gilly's, and those who do wish to keep it a secret, as a nearly private passageway between the realms is quite a luxury in Yatamon.

items: 05 {@font KNIFE|Obojima} SHOP SALLY & EDGE'S KNIFE SHOP
07 {@font SAMI'S|Obojima} GARAGE SAMI'S FIRST AGE GARAGE
09 {@font GREEN GLASS|Obojima} INN GREEN GLASS INN

entries: Nestled along the southeast border of Yatamon, Kinoko is a humming tangle of industry—a haven for crafters, tinkerers, and visionaries. Winding alleys lead to forges, workshops, and cafés. The scent of Happy Joy Cakes mingles with wood smoke and the myriad smells of cauldrons bubbling with the latest concoctions. The many artisans of Kinoko shape the district's character with their creations, and the streets are adorned with sculptures, storefront signs, and murals. Ancient buildings such as the AHA Library and the shrine of the rubble golem Udo serve as quiet reminders that this neighborhood balances bustling modernity with reverence for a mysterious past. Whether you're seeking fashionable First Age garments, a legendary pastry, or a mastercrafted blade, Kinoko has something for every adventurer.

entries.name: 01 Bridge Cat
entries: See the {@book Yatamon section|ObojimaTallGrass|4|Yatamon} in {@i Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass} for more information.

entries.name: 02 Himitzu's Arcane Izakaya
entries: See the {@book Yatamon section|ObojimaTallGrass|4|Yatamon} in {@i Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass} for more information.

entries.name: 03 Happy Joy Cake Bakery
entries: See the {@book Yatamon section|ObojimaTallGrass|4|Yatamon} in {@i Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass} for more information.

entries.name: 04 Gam Fugu Theater

entries: {@b Tone - Lively, Entertaining, Hip}

Gam Fugu, the venue owner and frequent stage performer of his self-named theater, has been running shows at his establishment in the Kinoko neighborhood for three decades. The theater is a staple of the area and is frequented by locals and tourists alike for its well-curated performances from across the island— the most notable of which is the monthly play produced by the masked theater group and trio, "Dolly Dolly Dolly."

entries.name: 05 Sally & Edge's Knife Shop

entries: {@b Tone - Industrious, Focused, Familial}

Tucked away in a twisting alleyway, a steady hammering can be heard from the bladesmith Master Edge and Sally, his granddaughter and apprentice. Master Edge has worked out of their small shop for nearly fifty years and took over ownership after his father passed away. Now Sally trains alongside him and will eventually take over his title.

Neighbors and frequent customers of the shop claim that Master Edge's knives never grow dull and that every blade he forges is meant to find its owner. These claims and praises have even spread beyond the city limits.

entries.name: 06 Stonesthrow Thrift & Threads

entries: {@b Tone - Calm, Expressive, Welcoming}

In a prominent storefront on one of Kinoko's busiest streets, there is a large shop that sells original and reproduction First Age clothing. The establishment specializes in bringing garments from the past back to life and is known to have some of the finest tailors in Yatamon, second only to the craftsmen at Hyousou. Stonesthrow's claim to fame is their ability to recreate an article of clothing from a single photo or piece of media. Most citizens of Yatamon would say that its presence in the city for the last 150 years has helped bring First Age fashion back to the island and inspired many other artists to pick up the art of First Age garment reproduction.

entries.name: 07 Sami's First Age Garage

entries: {@b Tone - Friendly, Rough-and-Tumble, Industrial}

Sami's First Age Garage is well known throughout Yatamon as the place to take First Age vehicles for repairs. The proprietor of the garage is Sami Elizondo, a young woman and local celebrity. Sami's family has studied this strange technology for generations so that Yatamon can keep its wheels rolling, and because of this, the Elizondo family name is well respected throughout the city.

Sami's garage is like a submarine's engine room—compact, organized, and stuffed to the brim with tools and parts. Her friend and cat associate, Sancho, is always nearby, lying in the sun and idly monitoring the garage's customers. In addition to watching over the garage for suspicious activity, Sancho is on the payroll of the feline information brokers Hana and Luna, who operate out of the Eminence Hotel.
Kinoko: Bicycle Alley
{@b Tone - Colorful, Eccentric, Innovative}

items: Dappa's Bicycle Alley is a tangle of canvas roofs strung up between two industrial buildings in the heart of the neighborhood. Dappa is a soft-spoken nakudama artisan with wiry arms, owl-like spectacles, and grease-stained reproduction First Age coveralls. He is known across the city for the signature style of his custom-built reproduction bicycles, as he crafts every cog, spoke, and gear by hand using traditional nakudaman methods—wood-laminating, lacquering, and special joinery. People in the know recognize a Dappa bicycle immediately.

What makes Dappa's creations so cherished is not just their artisanal elegance or comfortable ride; it's the vehicle's special connection to spirits. Before Dappa completes a bicycle, he crafts a charm and places it in the heart of the bike's frame. This charm acts as an offering to any minor spirits parallel to him in the Spirit Realm. The bicycle is complete when a spirit accepts Dappa's offering and crosses between realms to take up residence within the bike. These whelmed bikes have become known as "Whisper Wheels" and can manifest a number of minor properties after the rider bonds with the bike. Whisper Wheels are highly prized, as Dappa makes only a few of them per month.

entries.name: Popular Vendor
entries: Recently, a young mage set up a vending machine in Bicycle Alley after getting permission from Dappa himself. The machine has gotten quite a lot of attention as of late, as the young mage has a seemingly endless supply of First Age soda, which he regularly keeps stocked in the vending machine. The talk around town has brought a lot of extra attention to Dappa's shop, which Dappa appreciates, but when asked about the mage in question, Dappa simply states that "the kid likes his privacy."
The mystery surrounding the young mage has only garnered more attention, and many people are now questioning how long this supply of treats will last.

items.name: Dappa's Innovations
entries: Dappa's workshop is full of sketches of wild designs—a nakudamanstyle "sailbike" with extendable wings; a fish-shaped Courier Brigade postal cycle; and his most ambitious design, two-, three-, and four-seater tandem cycles. Dappa is dedicated to perfecting his craft but is also curious about other forms of transportation like mopeds, kei trucks, and trolleys, though he is happy to leave the creation of those to other artisans. Still, he is obsessed with understanding the complex machinery of these First Age vehicles and will eagerly trade stories, blue-prints, or relics with any traveler who shares his curiosity.

entries.name: Runaway Bike
entries: A brand-new Whisper Wheel meant for a local's daughter has vanished, but Dappa says it wasn't stolen—it rode away on its own. Dappa has requested that you find the errant spirit who has heisted this bike before it causes trouble, or worse—the pest spirit turns to more nefarious endeavors.

entries.name: Drag Race
entries: A rival mechanic has built a terrifying, jet-black bike powered by a volatile demon. He has challenged Dappa to a race during the Festival of Turning Wheels. Dappa's racing days are behind him, and although many friends and neighbors have offered to race in his stead, he can't bring himself to endanger any of them over something as small as his pride.
Kinoko: Kinoko Street
{@b Tone - Welcoming, Quirky, Intriguing}

The Green Glass Inn is a favorite within the Kinoko neighborhood for out-of-town visitors as well as the locals who come to Matsu's Izakaya on the ground floor. The inn is run by {@b Kikio (female)}, a bubbly elf who thrives on the positive interactions she has with her customers.

Matsu's Izakaya is run by {@b Matsu (male)}, a red dara, and budding master chef, by his own words. As cheerful and talkative as Kikio is, Matsu is the opposite, brusque and fiery—as he cooks his culinary delights—glaring at those he thinks don't truly appreciate his cuisine.

The top three floors of the inn are rooms for the guests, most with windows that look down on Kinoko Street below. The accommodations themselves are a mix of First Age luxuries such as Arcane Telecom phone booths which are installed on each floor and well made furniture crafted by local craftsmen from the Kinoko neighborhood.

entries.name: Reputation
entries: Though it's not as large or as popular as other inns and lodges in Yatamon, the Green Glass Inn's unique look, good food, and inviting hostess make the establishment a favorite spot for eccentric types and solo travelers passing by.

entries.name: Lost & Found
entries: In Kikio's small office, she keeps a chest of items left behind by customers over the years. Too kind to throw them away or sell them, she keeps the trinkets no matter the value— unbeknownst to her and Matsu, the collection she's gathered over the years is worth a small fortune at this point.

entries.name: Jukko (male human)
entries: Jukko is a permanent resident in Room 2-F and can usually be found sipping sake at Matsu's. He is a witch in the Patchwork Robe Coven and was once an adventurer who lost his arm to a {@creature goro goro|ObojimaTallGrass}{@sup °}. He is now retired from adventuring but still keeps a watchful eye on the neighborhood. Recently, the story of how he lost his arm made its way around the area, and now a group of young Yoka Scouts can often be found pestering him for advice on fighting demons.

entries.name: Talwyn the Drunken Bard (male human)
entries: Talwyn is a washed-up bard who Kikio has a soft spot for, and she lets him trade songs for a few free drinks each night. Matsu thinks Talwyn is an insufferable roach but puts up with him out of his respect for Kikio. Talwyn is an affable enough person, and every now and then sings a song that hearkens back to the talent of his youth. He knows a hundred bawdy songs, but his favorites are mellow and contemplative.

entries.name: Under Her Nose
entries: A group of would-be thieves and ruffians has recently rolled into Yatamon after being booted from a brief stint in the Mariners' Guild. After looking for work and a place to stay, one of the thieves caught word of a stash of loot being held in Kikio's office. They have now booked a room in hopes of sneaking into her office and making off with the loot.
Kinoko: City Center

Once a public library built during the First Age, the AHA Research Academy building is one of the iconic landmarks of Yatamon. Located in the heart of the city, this building now serves as the Yatamon field office of AHA—the Archaeologists, Historians, and Archivists—a semi-academic, semi-adventurous group trying to decode the secrets of the long-fallen First Age civilization. Because Yatamon itself is a First Age city, it is uniquely suited to studying the enigmatic era, its advanced technology, and the mysterious culture of its people.

Its distinct masonry, ornate stonework, and spectacular glass window designs give it a unique atmosphere for any visitors who wish to experience a First Age building as it might have appeared thousands of years ago. The scent of old books, carpeting, and other artificial smells of First Age buildings strangely still lingers in the air. Unknown symbols, old logos, and faded posters remain plastered across the walls.
AHA has transformed the library into a research outpost filled with artifacts, documents, and devices that AHA members have unearthed and continue to find in and around Yatamon.

entries.name: Alice
entries: On rainy nights, a dot-matrix printer the AHA members call Alice sparks to life and churns out peculiar symbols and what is thought to be messages in the language of the ancients. The spirit that whelms Alice is a simple animal spirit, so nobody knows where it's drawing its information from— or why the ink occasionally glows blue.

items.name: Reputation
entries: The AHA Research Academy is held in high esteem by scholars and witches across the island who see the guild as doing valuable and important work, and generally, people seem to approve of their investigations throughout the city, even if those activities occasionally interrupt their daily lives.

entries.name: The Central Stacks
entries: Once home to countless shelves of First Age books, the stacks now house bound copies of AHA research papers and excavation reports, as well as cabinets filled with maps, annotated diagrams of thousands of First Age objects, and in-depth studies of logos and letterforms. Additionally, strange blinking gadgets sit beside half-understood manuals, scrolls, and a trove of cassette tapes. However, First Age books still have a home within the stacks, with the bestdocumented— and therefore most valuable—volumes in the vast collection kept under lock and key in glass display cabinets at the end of each row.

entries.name: Missing Books
entries: Why the library's collection of books is missing is up for debate, but the theory with the most support involves a certain spirit who lived during the first hundred years of the Age of Humanity. Documents recount tales of a spirit with a peculiar desire for books. In some of these accounts, the spirit collects books for its personal library—in others, it has an insatiable craving for books and devours them in great mounds. Some historians from AHA believe that this spirit, described in these stories, passed through Yatamon before its death and could explain the library's missing collection.

entries.name: The Sample Repository
entries: The Sample Repository is a long room filled from floor to ceiling with card catalog drawers—each labeled with their expedition number—now meticulously repurposed to store artifact fragments, mineral samples, scraps of scrolls or fabrics, and pieces of First Age tech. Objects stored within the repository are typically smaller than an apple, barring a few exceptions, and in most cases are individually labeled and entered into AHA's only fully functioning computer terminal, where members can digitally catalog the samples and keep track of their location within the repository.

In addition to storing all samples collected within the city limits, the building's Sample Repository also houses a majority of the organization's small assets, which in total add up to 12,752 samples held within the drawers of the repository. Due to the nature—and, in some cases, danger—of certain samples, some drawers are sealed by magic wards and are accessible only to specific AHA researchers.

entries.name: The Testing Chamber
entries: A small room on the second floor of the library houses a half dozen microfiche machines, as well as several VCRs, cassette players, and a projector that the team uses to test found media to determine whether it's functioning. In this room, researchers with an understanding of magic also test objects such as cassettes and VHS tapes for spells or enchantments that may have been stored within the object.

entries.name: The Lounge
entries: A cozy space with First Age-inspired decor, The Lounge is used for gathering and for the display of a rotating selection of ancient artifacts. It is set up to resemble a living room with furniture salvaged from First Age ruins: CRT televisions, recliners, old snack machines, and board games. AHA members relax here, discussing theories over crackling First Age music from a speaker or the white-noise static from a CRT television.

entries.name: The Historical Engineering Lab
entries: This room acts as a workshop and repair facility. It has rows of long wood tables, and its walls are lined with shelves, cabinets, and tools. This is where AHA members study and repair mechanical and electronic items from the First Age. Resident AHA specialist Kial Dara works day and night within the lab and is seen by their colleagues as its caretaker. With more than a few magic mishaps, repairing these devices is not without its risks, as some ancient tech can react in dangerous ways when fused with arcane magic, so Kial and the other researchers must proceed with caution when attempting to power these devices.

entries.name: Why AHA Collects
entries: There are many branches within AHA's organization, each driven by their own research and preservation goals. Below are some of the leading reasons AHA might recover an item from the field:

items.name: Discovery
entries: The object is previously unknown or an undocumented variant.

items.name: Significance
entries: The object is connected to a historical figure or group and sheds light on their life or culture.

items.name: Condition
entries: The object is in a condition suitable for display, operational study, restoration, or spare parts.

items.name: Utility
entries: The object may directly assist with AHA research or operations.

items.name: Hazard
entries: The object poses an immediate danger if left in the field.

entries.name: Hika the Librarian (female nakudama)
entries: Hika is a bubbly nakudama who organizes the Central Stacks. She is curious and talkative but prone to overanalyzing and oversharing.

entries.name: Yanni (male human)
entries: Yanni is a wiry historian who loves exploring the ruins of Old Yatamon and cataloging any First Age customs he discovers while combing through old documents and media. He's currently writing a book on the cultures of the First Age and can often be found in the Lounge or Testing Chamber, working on the latest draft of his manuscript.

entries.name: Nikola Chek (female human)
entries: Nikola is a bit of a thrill-seeker who loves excavating First Age sites and secretly sells minor items she finds to vendors at the Yanari Witches' Market. She's often found in the Sample Repository cataloging her latest finds. Charming but selfish, with a knack for deflecting blame, Nikola loves the thrill of making a clandestine deal.

entries.name: Scavenger Hunt
entries: Kial has recently fixed a two-way radio, which has sparked to life with chatter. Someone in the city is connected to Kial's radio, but based on what they've said so far, Kial believes they're unaware of that fact. Kial has tried to respond but has had no luck contacting the mysterious voice. Normally, radios brought to life through enchantment don't function beyond emitting static, so they are eager to understand what makes the mystery voice's radio different. Kial has requested that you use context clues from the mysterious transmissions to find their source within the city and deliver a message.

entries.name: Cursed Charm
entries: Several weeks ago, while tending to the stacks late at night, Hika was overwhelmed by a sudden and intense sensation of fear. Though it lasted only a brief moment, she knew something terrible had transpired. Since that night, Hika has felt uneasy and, despite her desire to tell everyone, decided to keep the incident hidden from her colleagues, as she believed she had insufficient evidence to support her worries. That was until earlier this morning, when Hika uncovered a cursed charm hidden within the stacks. She is not sure who put it there, but after spending some time with it, she is certain the item is intended to attract a demon to its location. Now knowing her unease was justified and worried that one of her colleagues may have placed the charm, Hika has requested outside help to resolve this issue.

entries.name: Desperate Message
entries: While listening to a new stack of media recently brought into the Testing Chamber, a researcher found a message left in a garbled voice on one of the cassettes. The person claims to be from the Endo neighborhood and became lost in the ruins of Old Yatamon while collecting ingredients. However, after asking around, the researcher can find no record of anyone missing from that neighborhood.

items.title: {@font KIAL RARELY TAKES ADVICE FROM OTHERS APART FROM THEIR OLD FRIEND AND RIVAL BILL|Obojima}

items.name: Kial Dara (dara)
entries: Kial is a gruff red dara who maintains the Historical Engineering Lab and repairs First Age tech. Kial is pragmatic, blunt, and often frustrated due to their fiddly line of work— though they can be briefly charmed with a well-crafted tool. Constantly tinkering with cursed vacuum tubes, hot coils, and capacitors, Kial is often covered in burns from the more volatile First Age items.

entries.title: {@font WE BURN INCENSE AND LEAVE THESE SWEETS IN REMEMBRANCE|Obojima}

entries.name: The Giant Rubble Golem

entries: Kinoko: The Fade Line
{@b Tone - Tragic, Solemn, Unsettling}

Where the Kinoko neighborhood meets the ruins of Old Yatamon is a massive pile of stone and bricks where a huge apartment building once stood. Atop this pile of rubble, surrounded by broken lampposts and overgrown grass, sits a {@creature rubble golem|ObojimaTallGrass}{@sup °} known as Udo. The golem remains perfectly still on its hill in a slumped position, but its head slowly shifts to watch travelers who pass close by.
Over time, residents have carefully maintained a shrine near the site, leaving the area around Udo untouched, as many have reported an overwhelming feeling of sadness when approaching the golem.

entries.name: Origin
entries: No one knows exactly what caused the incident, but some witches and wizards speculate that over 150 years ago the large residential building here fell apart when the magic that preserves First Age materials faded from it, causing the whole structure to collapse in an instant. As with all rubble golems, the emotions of the people lost within the ruins fused with the stone to create a living memorial that the residents of Yatamon now leave offerings to.

entries.name: Reputation
entries: Most residents of Yatamon know about this place, and many come here to pay their respects. There are even some distant relatives of those who died in the disaster who still come regularly to give offerings to their great-great-great-great-grandparent lost in the collapse. Everyone knows that approaching Udo or entering the site with the intent to rob the ruins is a bad idea— even the most hardened thieves feel the shame of even thinking of such a disrespectful act. But there are a few who have tried, only to be overcome with a terrible feeling of sorrow and dread as they neared the golem, a wrenching of the heart that made them turn back and never enter Udo's domain again.

entries.name: The Shrine
entries: At a respectful distance from the edge of the site, a shrine was built long ago by what were most likely the relatives and friends of those lost in the disaster. The shrine has a fairly tall stone gate that holds aloft a number of colored talismans. Past the gate, at the top of a small manmade mound, is an area paved with flagstones that overlooks the site where Udo sits, holding its eternal vigil.

Many see the shrine as a memorial and a place to reflect on the ephemeral nature of life. Others avoid it, as they feel pity for Udo the golem, whom they see as bearing an immense burden of sorrow. They can't bring themselves to visit the shrine because they wish too deeply there were some way to release the poor creature from its perpetual watch.

entries.name: Udo
entries: Udo is large for a rubble golem; even when sitting, it casts a broad shadow. It usually remains very still, and birds often sit and sun themselves on the arms and head of the hulking pile of stones. Every now and then, Udo will slowly pick through a few of the broken bricks that lie strewn around it, as if looking for something.

Udo will converse through head nods and hand gestures with those who approach it, but only if the golem has something to say. Should anyone try to remove anything from the ruins, Udo will move to attack. Until that happens, Udo remains still, but watchful.

entries.name: Udo's Aura
entries: Udo has an aura about it. Those who remain in Udo's presence for an extended period of time are often overwhelmed with grief and sorrow. This emotional burden can be debilitating and has been described by Master Canden as "a fatigue unlike any training or battle could produce."

entries.name: The Rubble
entries: Udo sits at the center of a hill of rubble that covers roughly 300 square feet. The rubble is mostly moss-covered piles of stone and wood, with the occasional metal beam or crumbled wall sticking out of it. Some ancient bits of broken furniture can be made out, along with the hollowed husk of a rusted furnace.

Should Udo rise, there is a hole beneath where the golem sits that leads into the hill of rubble. If someone were brave enough to enter and risk the unstable wreckage around the hole, they could explore the demolished interior of this ancient apartment building.

entries.name: Artifacts
entries: While there are artifacts and items (First Age and otherwise) to be found in the rubble, Udo will either have to give permission (which is highly unlikely) or be defeated in order to search the ruins and obtain them without being attacked by the golem. Unless there is a special circumstance in which removing an item helps alleviate suffering or brings someone a sense of connection to a missing family member, any item taken from the ruins will bear a Curse of Shadow (see below).

entries.name: Curse of Shadow
entries: The Curse of Shadow causes terrible nightmares that weigh on the cursed creature day and night. A creature cursed in this way can only benefit from one {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} per day (but not both). The curse lasts until it's ended by a level 5+ spell that removes curses. Alternatively, the curse can be removed by returning the item to the exact place it was taken from.

entries.name: Vormus (demon)
entries: Vormus, a charismatic demon{@sup °}, has begun to obsess over the idea of what might be hidden within the rubble of the collapsed building and is now consumed with the desire to obtain it. Unable to devise a plan to defeat the golem, the conniving demon is now considering the subway system as a way to circumvent Udo and gain access to the ruins.

entries.name: Muriel Zinn (female elf)
entries: Muriel is an elf witch from the League of the Gilded Gourd coven who has been studying the Fade Line. The coven knows that this collapse took place over 150 years ago, at a time when few records were kept. Since then, the Fade Line has not moved, as no new buildings or structures at the edges of Yatamon have crumbled to anyone's knowledge, but Muriel is concerned that should the Fade Line suddenly shift, more buildings might instantly crumble and collapse. Muriel, unlike most, has an extraordinary ability to stay within Udo's presence for long periods of time without feeling the effects of his aura, which has been a boon to her research and has allowed her to make more progress on this project than any other researcher before her.

items: 12 {@font LULA'S|Obojima} LULA'S SPIRIT DINER & GAMBLING HALL

{@b Endo is one of Yatamon's most curious neighborhoods}—a place where flavors of the Physical Realm and the Spirit Realm mix to create a banquet of otherworldliness. At its heart is the Gap, a mysterious crack in a stone wall that opens into the Spirit Realm and Yatamon's sister city, Nomyata—a bustling spirit enclave filled with shrines, businesses, and spirit culture. Tourism goes both ways: Obojiman travelers come to Endo to travel to the Spirit Realm, while curious visitors from the Spirit Realm come to Endo to experience the chaos and color of the Physical Realm. Around this crossroads, Endo hums with charm and mystery: browse enchanted VHS tapes at Lord Gudo's Arcanum, watch tailors spin magic silk at Hyousou, or witness witches crafting brooms at Hetty's Broomery. From the quirky Goodie Mart Museum to the sacramental brews of the Blurry Root Still House, Endo is a rare and vibrant blend of cultures.

entries.name: 12 Lula's Spirit Diner & Gambling Hall
entries: See the {@book Yatamon section|ObojimaTallGrass|4|Yatamon} in {@i Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass} for more information.

entries.name: 13 Gojo's Ramen Bucket
entries: See the {@book Yatamon section|ObojimaTallGrass|4|Yatamon} in {@i Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass} for more information.

entries.name: 14 Lord Gudo's Arcanum

entries: {@b Tone - Overwhelming, Shifty, Magical}

Inside Lord Gudo's Arcanum, you see before you a maze of aisles that contain VHS tapes, cassettes, and cartridges, all of which Lord Gudo (also known as Ray) has carefully cataloged. Lord Gudo is also a member of AHA and hires adventurers to find more of these items—perhaps some box in a barn or some ancient ruin out on the shores of Lake Ellior; the next big cache is waiting for discovery.

entries.name: 15 Goodie Mart Museum

entries: {@b Tone - Esoteric, Mysterious, Odd}

Using ancient images and decades of research, a diligent group of AHA historians have restored this First Age market to what they believe is as close to what it originally looked like thousands of years ago. The AHA members come here, dressed up in period clothing to re-enact what the First Age ancestors might have been like and what this market could have sold. First Age products like soda, bubble gum, and milk bottles are on display here along with mock up items that are made by AHA members that replicate items yet to be found.

entries.name: 16 Hetty's Broomery

entries: {@b Tone - Kindly, Informative, Helpful}

Hetty has been making brooms for discerning witches and warlocks since she was a teenager, taking over from her mother who is now living in Sky Kite Valley. The Broomery has a nice offering of pre-made brooms for sale, but Hetty is always ready to take on a custom order and craft a broom out of any materials a customer might bring. The Broomery is essentially Hetty's workshop and customers are always welcome to come and watch Hetty work. She offers classes to those who are interested in pursuing magic broom making.

entries.name: 17 Arcane Telecom Headquarters

entries: {@b Tone - Loud, Uninviting, Chaotic}

The central operations of the Arcane Telecom Organization are run out of a partially functioning First Age telephone exchange building. Inside, a dozen or more spirits answer phones, make connections, send messages, and order services for the clients that call in. Using this special building is what allows the organization to function, as the structure and its interior systems are seemingly connected to every wired phone booth in Yatamon. Spirits of every shape and size work as operators day and night, with few exceptions, and it's standard practice for the organization to maintain enough staff to handle emergencies. The call room itself is often filled with a hazy smoke and powerful aroma, as cigarettes and pipes are passed around. The constant hum and unsettling crackle of the magic powering the electronics can barely be heard over the chatter of operators and incoming calls—to the uninitiated, it's a sensory nightmare.

entries.name: The Bosses Domain
entries: Down a wide, dimly lit cement stairwell that leads to the basement of the headquarters building is the private office of Mr. Dasper, the proprietor and founder of the Arcane Telecom Organization. The door to the room, which is clearly marked with his nameplate, is made from solid steel and lacks any evidence of a handle or method by which you'd open it. No one from the organization has met Mr. Dasper in person; however, everyone is familiar with his enchanting voice and friendly demeanor. He often calls up from his office to give direction or make requests, usually regarding questions or conversations individuals have had without him.

It isn't known whether Mr. Dasper leaves his office, or is even in it to begin with, but a handful of spirits do have theories—the most popular of which is that Mr. Dasper is an elder spirit, and the headquarters is his domain, allowing him to power the phone system and oversee his subordinates.
Endo: Shiniri Street
{@b Tone - Mystical, Lively, Bewildering}

At the dead end of what was once a fairly nondescript alleyway sits a stone wall split by a long crack going through its center. This break in the masonry is known as the Gap, one of the rare persistent entryways to the Spirit Realm and the most active portal on the island. Since its discovery, this spectacular phenomenon has brought a flux of spirits and physical beings across the threshold connecting the realms, allowing travelers to pass freely between the two like never before.

entries.name: Shiniri Street
entries: The alleyway that leads to the Gap is found off of Shiniri Street—a long road where spirits have established residences as well as shops, inns, and other small businesses. This colorful area is an explosion of decorative signs, neon lights, storefronts, bars, and mouth-watering street food. The street serves multiple purposes for the spirit community, as it's both a place to share their unique culture and a way to help new arrivals from the Spirit Realm adjust to the bewildering, fast-paced, and ever-changing world of the Physical Realm. Those spirits who venture onto the island for the first time can take solace in the fact that a community has formed within the city to help them adjust.

Every portal is wholly unique and requires its own method of activation, usually an offering, ritual, or key. Portals like the one used by the ferry that travels to the spirit market Uluwa require a key, which comes in the form of a ticket stub. The Gap is special because, unlike other portals, nothing is required of a traveler to use it.

entries.name: Nomyata
entries: At the opposite end of the Gap, in the spirit realm, lies Nomyata, Yatamon's sister city. Originally a merchant camp that formed around the wooded area in the Spirit Realm where the portal stands, Nomyata is now a bustling city in its own right, albeit one much smaller than Yatamon. Canvas tents and simple structures eventually gave way to eccentric homes and peculiar businesses, combining the special flair and style of both realms into one busy hub. Though Nomyata is quite lively at nearly all hours, few people actually call the place home, and because of that, it's often compared to a train station.

entries.name: The Gap in Nomyata
entries: The portal found in Nomyata looks quite different from how it appears in Yatamon. Instead of a brick wall, viewers in the Spirit Realm see a perfectly rectangular window into the Physical Realm, overlooking the city alleyway from the portal's perspective. Built around that window is a wooden archway shaped from hardwoods native to the spirit realm, signifying the gateway's importance. Carved into the top of the archway in the Torum language is the word "Obojima."

entries.name: Conniving Creatures
entries: Somehow, a group of {@filter howlers|bestiary|source=obojimatallgrass;obojimatalesyatamon|tag=howler}{@sup °} has slipped through the Gap into Nomyata during a lull in travel. They were first discovered over two weeks ago and have since run amok throughout the city. Locals would trade just about anything to see them driven out.

entries.name: Cursed Fruit
entries: A group of faceless spirits, dressed in trench coats and bowler hats, recently began frequenting markets, restaurants, and food stalls near the Gap. They sold a never-before-seen fruit they claim to have discovered in the spirit realm—a curiosity that quickly grew in popularity and became the talk of the town before the merchants selling it suddenly vanished. Since their disappearance, anyone who tried the fruit has now become irritable, aggressive, and, in some cases, manic. After learning of this, the Arch Doyen of the Witchery, Mr. Basingstoke, has become increasingly worried that a large-scale curse has been enacted upon the people and that, in time, the symptoms will worsen. Too busy to investigate personally, he's offered a reward to anyone who can provide information about— or reveal the location of—the missing fruit merchants.

entries.name: The Urn Incident
entries: A merchant unknowingly attempted to bring a clay urn into the Spirit Realm that had a demon sealed inside it. As the merchant began to pass through the portal, the urn suddenly shattered, freeing the demon and sending the surrounding area on both sides of the portal into a panic.
Endo: South Path
{@b Tone - Industrious, Arcane, Artistic}

Hyousou was once a First Age concrete warehouse building that has since been repurposed to house a magical tailoring workshop dating back to the very first humans to settle Yatamon. The interior doors and walls are now beautifully painted silk screen partitions that form a maze of rooms filled with looms, glowing dye tubs, and worktables. Clinging to the exterior walls of the building in floating decorative pots are dozens of mulberry trees, each with scores of silkworms that generate yard upon yard of delicate silk.

entries.name: Festival of the Glimmering Garment
entries: The Festival of the Glimmering Garment is the re-enactment of an old legend in which the elder spirit, Utmar, came to destroy Yatamon after the citizens foolishly woke the spirit from its slumber. In the midst of this danger, a brave sorcerer known as the First Weaver had a vision of a garment woven with enchantments that would trap Utmar and prevent the city's destruction.
The First Weaver wove a garment so beautiful and alluring that Utmar could not resist wearing it, and in doing so, the spirit was trapped and the city was saved.

Every year thereafter, the spirit came back in a different guise attempting to trick the First Weaver. Each time, she received a new vision of enchanting patterns that would lure Utmar and bind the spirit once again. This visionary legacy has been handed down from Weaver to Weaver for generations.

Some believe the legend of Utmar is historically factual and that the Weaver and the festival remain critical to the city's survival. Most, however, see the story as a metaphor and the festival as a joyful reason to gather—fostering city-wide solidarity against an unseen foe.

entries.name: Reputation
entries: Most residents of Yatamon have heard of Hyousou, the Weaver, the enchanted garments, and have been to the annual festival, knowing the legend well. Outside of Yatamon, Hyousou is less well known, but certain wandering bards may have heard the legend of the First Weaver or attended the Festival of the Glimmering Garment.

entries.name: The Weaver's Den
entries: This simple room is the only elevated space in the building and overlooks the maze of silk walls that form the workshop. Inside stands the Weaver's humble magic loom, which has been passed down for generations and is used to weave the costume for the Festival of the Glimmering Garment. The loom is also where the Weaver receives their visions.

entries.name: Pattern Library
entries: Beneath Hyousou is a locked and warded vault where racks of ancient garments and their patterns are kept from the very first costume to the present day.

entries.name: The Dye Room
entries: Built into the colorfully stained floor of this room are deep clay pots containing all the dyes needed to color the silk made in Hyousou. Lining the walls are workbenches, drying racks, and apothecary cabinets, each made from mulberry wood collected from the grove.

Kept nearby are arguably the two most important ingredients needed to produce the dyes: sulfurous water from {@book Hogstone Hot Springs|ObojimaTallGrass|4|Hogstone Hot Springs}{@sup °} and the potent alcohol Blurry Root, made by the neighboring Sun Pig Distillery.

entries.name: The Workshop
entries: This maze of interconnected rooms bustles with tailors, spinning wheels, and looms. In one of these rooms, silkworm cocoons are boiled, soaked, and spun into silk thread.

items.name: Amishka, the Weaver (female human)
entries: Amishka is the current Weaver, an elegant and intense woman with long silver hair who is, without fail, always dressed immaculately. She speaks with a calm, even tone, choosing her words with the precision of a well-seasoned leader. Despite being restrained with her designs, Amishka is more social than previous Weavers, and is happy to receive visitors sharing the phenomenal textile art produced at Hyousou along with its history.

As a baby, Amishka was found outside the gates of Hyousou by the head tailor, Koji, and was taken in by the Weaver at that time, Lady Otua. Amishka grew up within the walls of Hyousou, and as a little girl, she ran around the dye vats, stared at the strange complexity of the looms, and explored every nook and cranny of the First Age building. While Lady Otua was her primary mentor and teacher, everyone at Hyousou took part in raising young Amishka, preparing her for the moment when she would embrace her destiny—for Lady Otua had already foreseen that Amishka would become the next Weaver.

entries.name: Koji (male human)
entries: Koji is the Head Tailor of Hyousou and runs the entire operation with a calm assurance that comes from a deep understanding of the inner workings of Hyousou and the inevitable uncertainty of the world around it. Koji has known Amishka her whole life, as well as the Weaver before her. Beyond his official duties as Head Tailor, he serves Amishka as a wise counselor and friend.

entries.name: Yem, the Pattern Keeper (spirit)
entries: Yem is an ancient spirit that has been at Hyousou since the time of the First Weaver. Like clockwork, Yem appears to record the final pattern of the magical garment the Weaver creates for the Festival of the Glittering Garment. Yem magically etches the final pattern into its body, which is filled with sparkling constellations of past designs. Physical copies of the garment patterns are drawn by hand by Koji, who, after the festival is complete, stores both the pattern and the magical garment in the underground vault of the Pattern Library.
Yem does not speak, nor does it interact with anyone. It merely appears before each festival to perform its cryptic duty, then fades back into the Spirit Realm.

entries.name: Mira (female elf)
entries: Mira is a druid and arborist who cares for the sacred and priceless mulberry grove, along with its many thousands of silkworms—whom Mira seems to talk to more than people. Given the speed at which the silkworms consume mulberry leaves, Mira must spend most of her day performing rituals to encourage the fast growth of replacement foliage—a task she must accomplish daily lest the grove be devoured.

entries.name: Silkworm Thief
entries: Mira believes someone has been smuggling silkworms out of the grove for some time now, as the silkworm population has begun to diminish. Suspecting the thief is one of the tailors, Mira asks the adventurers to investigate without revealing their purpose or their connection to her.

entries.name: Trip to Hogstone
entries: It is that time of year when Hyousou needs more water from Hogstone Hot Springs to replenish the dye vats. Adventurers are needed to help the workers make the long journey across the Gale Fields to the hot spring within the foothills of Mount Arbora.
Endo: Eminence Blvd.

Dubbed the "Cat Hotel," this peculiar establishment is a landmark gathering spot for awakened cats, whether they are visitors to the city or working cats just off their shifts. The Eminence is a First Age structure that looms like a great wedge on the corner of a triangular block, its narrow streetfacing facade adorned with tall windows that rise from the ground floor to the roof to collect the afternoon sun.

The remarkable quality of the Eminence becomes apparent once inside. Past the reception desk in the foyer and through a doorway obscured by a beaded curtain, you enter the hustle and bustle of the hotel interior. Each of the nine floors has an interior balcony that overlooks the common area on the first floor, where cats gather among the handful of small tended gardens to chatter into the small hours of the morning.

The Eminence boasts dozens of rooms, the precise number of which is impossible to discern within the labyrinthine structure. At any given time, between fifty and a hundred cats are staying at the hotel, though the number swells in the evenings as dozens more descend upon the establishment for nighttime entertainment after the workday ends.

Yatamon's cat culture runs through the Eminence. Cats who work throughout the city often wander in to socialize or to simply find a warm spot to curl up in for a little while. The hotel is also the hub of the cats' famed information trade—anyone seeking an information broker would do well to start at the Eminence.

entries.name: Reputation
entries: Non-cats who visit the Eminence often describe feeling as though they were somehow intruding. They speak of an ambient strangeness—like being watched, judged, and ignored all at the same time. There is an overwhelming sense that everything that transpires within the hotel is on the cats' terms, including business. The Eminence has a reputation as a place exclusive to cats, visited by non-cats only when they are recklessly curious or truly desperate.

entries.name: A Place for Cats
entries: Everything—from the posh furniture to the dishes and cutlery—is made at a cat's scale. The foyer has a handful of folding chairs for non-cat visitors, but there are otherwise no accommodations for bigger folk.

entries.name: Hotel Staff
entries: Attending to the needs of the guests are a clone of Viota, who runs the front desk; numerous cat bellhops; and a host of tiny spirits commanded by Viota, who see to the housekeeping.

entries.name: The Information Trade
entries: The Eminence Hotel is the nexus of the information trade dominated by cats in Yatamon. Several brokerages take meetings with clients in the common room, and some even maintain a permanent table there. Cat informants come and go throughout the day to deliver reports to their bosses, while more freelance-minded cats may sell their information to the highest bidder.

entries.name: Common Room
entries: Beyond the foyer, the hotel's opulent common room spreads out beneath the balconies that ring the upper levels. The mustard stone floor is punctuated with the occasional built-in garden, and the walls are adorned with swords far too small for human hands. The room is anchored at one end by a fountain that sends bubbles floating up from its three fluted pinnacles. An array of cushions forms a semicircle around a fireplace midway through the room, where storytellers and musicians perform nightly, and patrons gather at the dozens of low tables arranged between the fountain and the hearth to chat, gamble, and conduct business.

entries.name: Solarium
entries: The Solarium occupies the uppermost floor of the hotel, resting like a shimmering crown on its roof. The entire space is enclosed in soft yellow glass, making it exceedingly warm for most non-cats. The air is sweet and dewy among the many rare ferns and flowers grown here. This is the most beautiful place in the Eminence—and its most guarded—for it's here that a store of agate is kept for the casting of the {@spell Awaken|XPHB} spell on willing cats. Cats coming to the hotel to become awakened will undergo the spell in the Solarium, but anyone snooping around up here uninvited is likely to be questioned by a trio of {@creature Awakened Cat Neko Duelist|ObojimaTalesYatamon|Awakened Cat Neko Duelists}.

entries.name: Room 303
entries: This room is always occupied, and the door is always locked. Anyone who draws too close—or stays in one of the adjacent rooms—is struck with a sudden sleepiness. Those who fall asleep nearby are visited by vivid dreams (see Adventure Hooks below for examples). Keen-eared guests hear a low, steady rumble from within Room 303, and if they ask about the noise, the staff simply replies, "please do not disturb the guests." Stranger still, each afternoon, a procession of pest spirits resembling tufts of fur emerges from beneath the door and makes its way to the front desk, each one carrying a coin that, taken together, is the exact amount of a night's stay.

entries.name: Hana and Luna, Information Brokers (awakened cats)
entries: Though most cats in the hotel are guests, Hana and Luna are among the handful who reside here. Like many other cats, they conduct their information brokerage out of the common room, operating from their usual spot by the fireplace. The pair maintain a vast network of spies and informants throughout the four neighborhoods. Though they are not the only game in town when it comes to information gathering, they are the most renowned. Hana is cautious and highly suspicious of others— especially her clients. She prefers to listen rather than talk, and when she does speak, her voice carries an icy edge. Luna is the adventurer of the two, preferring fieldwork over paperwork. She is observant but easily bored.

entries.name: Viota, Hotel Front Desk (spirit)
entries: This clone of Viota, like all such clones, is a spirit composed of black, shadowy vapor with golden eyes and the silhouette of a human girl. She is amiable and welcoming, doting on all cats with genuine affection. During conversation, she will occasionally appear distant. Her magical sympathetic connection to the other clones forces her attention to some far-off place. These reveries don't typically last long; however, they may alter her mood. Viota also seems to have complete control over the helper spirits that work in the hotel. Learn more about the {@creature Clone of Viota|ObojimaTallGrass}{@sup °} in {@i Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass}.

entries.name: Balazare, the Sword Master (awakened cat)
entries: Debonair and clever, Balazare is one of the few sword masters who holds the secrets of the Neko Duelist sword style. They come and go as they please, always in an array of cat guises and always wielding their signature pairing of shortsword and dagger. They are highly discerning when it comes to prospective pupils and favor an encouraging, playful approach to instruction. Their magical ability to travel freely between the Physical Realm and the Spirit Realm means that they are known to turn up anywhere, at any time, to offer their pupils an impromptu lesson.

entries.name: Gato Hibi (awakened cat)
entries: The current owner and hotel runner of the Eminence is a boisterous and charming awakened cat by the name of Gato Hibi. Gato has owned the eminence for seven years, having taken over when the previous hotel runner suddenly passed. Since then, Gato has worked alongside a handful of elder cats and spirits who worked closely with the previous ownership to keep the hotel's traditions alive and the building's peculiar needs met. Gato spends most of his day solving the many small problems that arise at the hotel and entertaining his guests. Whenever he can, Gato stops to chat in the lobby or play a game of cards, which has prompted the regulars to affectionately give him the title "the worst card player to walk on all fours."

entries.name: Hostile Takeover
entries: A group of awakened cat ruffians claim the hotel as their own and begins running casino games out of the common room, driving out other businesses, cheating those who choose to play, and intimidating the other guests.

entries.name: Welcome to the Brokerage
entries: Luna, the information broker, invites the adventurers to the hotel to discuss business. She and her partner are looking for non-cat informants to surveil a trio of nakudama suspected of planning a heist at the Dawn Petal Monastery. One of the suspects is allergic to cats, which is why Luna is offering six Gold Flowers to do the job and report back.

entries.name: Vivid Dreams
entries: Adventurers who stay at the hotel might be visited by peculiar and vivid dreams. The psychic energy emanating from Room 303 inspires such dreams, which may transport the dreamer to far-off places on the island. Here are some examples of dreams:

items: The dreamer sits before an endless feast on the deck of a ship with bright blue sails and a crew of spirits.

The dreamer watches a massive migration of giant jellyfish as it fills the sky, stretching far across Obojima. A nameless shadow drifts among the jellyfish. The dreamer is both exhilarated and filled with a sense of dread.
The dreamer is overwhelmed by the booming sound of a heartbeat they are certain is coming from deep within Mount Arbora.
The dreamer is late for their train at a station high in the clouds, watching the doors close as the platform begins to drift away.

entries.name: Witchy Origin
entries: Though the exact details vary in each telling, it's generally agreed that the Eminence was founded by a witch who awakened all the cats she could find in Yatamon. Soon after establishing the hotel, the witch disappeared. Cats don't know where she went, and her name has been lost—a fact that some cats believe points to foul play. It's not uncommon to hear cats in the common room speculating about the witch's whereabouts.

entries.name: True Body
entries: Rumor has it that the sound coming from Room 303 is the snoring of the Bridge Cat, and that somehow the room and cat spirit are connected. The hotel has been this way for as long as anyone can remember, and some even believe the hotel was built around Room 303 to protect it.
Endo: Hill Rd.

On a wooded hillside on the outskirts of the Endo neighborhood stands the Sun Pig Distillery, a cluster of interconnected wooden buildings predominantly constructed from aged, dark timber. The roofs of the distillery are made of weathered clay shingles that, in certain areas, are covered with a layer of moss. Large, sliding wooden doors can be opened to allow the passage of oversized vats and the circulation of air—thick with the sweet, earthy scent of fermentation. Here, skilled artisans known as the Zako meticulously brew one of the island's most potent alcohols, Blurry Root.

The primary structure, a long, wide room known as the Fermentation Hall, is easily the largest building. Its walls and ceiling are subtly discolored from years of exposure to yeast and steam from the dozen or so vats clustered here. Adjacent is the Still Room, which features a tall stone chimney that gently releases wisps of steam into the crisp Obojima air.

The trees and bushes surrounding the distillery grasp at the buildings with their branches and foliage. Well-worn flagstone paths snake between the structures, with one leading to a secluded root cellar half-buried in the hillside. Behind its heavy wooden doors is a geothermally cooled storage cellar filled with enough Blurry Root to last several brewing seasons.

Nearby, the brewers have a carefully maintained garden that supplies some of the herbs and aromatics needed for the drink's production. From a crystalclear spring that bubbles out of the hillside, a stream flows through the property, and some of its water is diverted for use in distilling. This is the "life water" used to make all the Blurry Root produced here.

entries.name: Konotori, Fumoshiki, & the Sacraments
entries: Konotori is an ancient organization with a long history dating back to the beginning of the Age of Humanity. Since its conception, the group has sought to maintain a balance between nature and the people of the island. Through ritual and ceremony, the Fumoshiki—Konotori's most trained practitioners— enact the "Will of Obojima" by righting wrongs, breaking incantations, ending evil practices, and laying to rest sources of unease on the island. The Sun Pig Distillery has played an important role in the success of Konotori and the Fumoshiki over the years.

The Fumoshiki employ many tools and techniques in their rituals, but few are as important as the Sacred Sacraments. These ceremonial components include three specialty alcohols the group has used for centuries, one of which is Blurry Root. Since the distillery was founded, Sun Pig has worked alongside Konotori, supplying the organization and its Fumoshiki with a steady stream of Blurry Root, as well as aid within the city whenever necessary.

entries.name: Reputation
entries: The Sun Pig Distillery holds a reputation for unwavering dedication to perfecting a beloved libation. While the distillery's ties to the Fumoshiki may be somewhat enigmatic to outsiders, Blurry Root is still widely known and enjoyed by people throughout the city and across the greater island. Many attribute this quality to the brewer's ancient methods and high-quality ingredients.

entries.name: Secrets of Distilling
entries: The true secret behind Blurry Root's potency lies within the walls and rafters of the distillery. Throughout the year—but especially when the brewing begins—a colony of minuscule spirits that inhabit the grain of the wood appears. These spirits often materialize as motes of light or hair-like glowing threads that drift toward the open vats. The master distiller who first discovered the phenomenon once said, "Blurry Root is an offering, and these spirits are drawn to the purity of that offering." Now, centuries later, the Zako revere the tiny spirits believing it is they who provide the unique fermentation that makes Blurry Root so special.

entries.name: Balance in All Things
entries: The brewing techniques of the Zako are passed down through apprenticeship. No written record exists to describe the precise movements, specific ingredients, and finishing processes involved. Even the emotional state of the brewer is taken into account, as the Zako maintain that being rooted in the task at hand—and not lost in one's emotions—is not merely a matter of efficiency. A balanced mind is needed to create an environment in the Fermentation Room where the brew can prosper. Without this mindset, one cannot successfully brew Blurry Root. Thus, not everyone can be a Zako; some simply lack the temperament for it.

entries.name: The Root Drying Room
entries: A cool, earthen-floored glass room is arranged with baskets of herbs, lengths of Kojo Root hung to dry, and bundles of freshly gathered components. Carefully controlled windows encourage the circulation of the earthy, fragrant air, while the sun ever so softly warms the room and dries the botanicals.

entries.name: The Fermentation Hall
entries: A long hall filled with rows upon rows of massive wooden vats, some almost as tall as a person, each bubbling with fermenting Blurry Root mash. The air here is thick with a sweet, yeasty aroma, and the rhythmic sounds of the bubbling liquid are almost meditative.

entries.name: The Cleansing Room
entries: In a short building located in the middle of the distillery, a series of heated clay stills, crafted in the shape of an hourglass gourd, gently bring the fermented Blurry Root mash to high temperature, purifying the alcohol and bringing out its signature flavor.

entries.name: The Tasting Chamber
entries: This small, elegant room is furnished with low tables and cushions, where samples of finished Blurry Root are carefully assessed by the Zako for quality. This is also where restaurateurs, shop runners, and innkeepers come to taste the latest batch before selling it in their establishments.

entries.name: The Zako Quarters
entries: A modest, communal living space attached to the distillery, where the Zako brewers and distillers reside. It is clean and functional, with simple sleeping mats, a shared kitchen, and a small shrine dedicated to the island.

entries.name: Master Oya (male human)
entries: Master Oya is a kind and stoic man whose hands are permanently stained with the faint burgundy hue of fermented Blurry Root. He oversees all production at the Sun Pig Distillery and carries a vast library of knowledge in his head. Intensely dedicated to his craft, he is constantly teaching junior brewers the many subtleties of the work as he wanders the grounds each day. He respects the Fumoshiki deeply, and will do whatever he can to aid them in their work, but his first duty will always be to the distillery, to Blurry Root, and to his Zako students—even Fumoshiki masters are not above receiving a lesson from Master Oya.

entries.name: Kiyomi (female human)
entries: Kiyomi is an enthusiastic apprentice brewer who loves the intricate process of distillation and has a keen intuition for the subtle shifts in fermentation. She's eager to prove herself worthy of becoming a master distiller, but she's torn: Kiyomi also harbors romantic dreams of living the wandering life of a Fumoshiki.
Master Oya has high hopes that Kiyomi will one day take his place as master of the distillery, but he doesn't let this stand in the way of her other dreams.

entries.name: Jinso (spirit)
entries: Jinso serves as the primary contact between the Sun Pig Distillery and Konotori. Jinso arrives periodically— often unannounced—to collect completed batches of Blurry Root sacrament, relay messages, or herald the arrival of a Fumoshiki. Highly observant, Jinso generally speaks in metaphors and carefully guards any Fumoshiki secrets.

entries.name: Harku, the Root Gatherer (awakened cat)
entries: Harku is a Zako ranger who spends most of her days foraging for wild Kojo Root, the main ingredient required for alcohol production. Harku knows every nook and cranny of the forests surrounding Yatamon and possesses an almost supernatural ability to locate the highest-quality plants. She believes the roots want to be found and that they leave signs for those patient enough to notice them.

entries.name: A Root of Discord
entries: Harku, the root gatherer, reports that the foraging grounds where she gathers Kojo Root have recently become home to a bestial spirit wreaking havoc on the flora and fauna of the woods. A Fumoshiki master was sent to investigate, but hasn't returned in several weeks. Now deeply worried, Harku has asked the adventurers to join her so she can find the missing Fumoshiki and put an end to the unruly spirit's tyranny over the woods.

entries.name: The Righteous Zako
entries: A disgruntled Zako, frustrated with the lack of direct recognition for their vital work, has begun secretly selling their "special" Blurry Root to less reputable dealers in the Yanari Market. Master Goh has currently banned them from entering the Fermentation Room, and they are close to being removed from the distillery altogether. To prove everyone wrong, they are attempting to improve Blurry Root in their own small batch brews, but their crude attempts to mimic the magic techniques are creating bitter, unstable brews. The party is asked by Jinso, the Fumoshiki liaison, to discreetly intervene.

entries.name: Strange Brew
entries: A recent batch of Blurry Root has gone wrong—those who drink it experience the same dream of a weeping dara beneath a tree scarred black by fire. Master Oya has been moved by this dream but has no understanding of how to ease the dara's sorrow.

items: 29 {@font ACADEMY|Obojima} CANDEN & MOON'S ACADEMY OF SWORDS

{@b If the Kinoko neighborhood is the industrious hands of} Yatamon, then the Negi neighborhood is its backbone—a place of discipline, pageantry, and duty. This is a neighborhood where banners and uniforms are a common sight and, when the Great River Tournament is happening, the sound of roaring crowds fills the air. Anchored by its Grand Tournament Arena, the Courier Brigade Headquarters, and Canden & Moon's Sword School, Negi is a neighborhood where everyone seems to move with a sense of purpose. While every street here may feel like a festival route, you'll almost always find a postal knight or a sword student carrying out their everyday duties amid the pageantry.

entries.name: Points of Interest
entries: Beyond the banners, a ride on a spirit-whelmed trolley or a visit to the Dawn Blossom Guild Hall or one of Negi's many shrines offer moments of quiet reflection. For more lively entertainment, the neighborhood's numerous taverns are the best spots to hear stories of past champions and legends from the Great River Tournament, often told in colorful songs and chants over copious amounts of laughter and ale. Negi balances its ceremonial and official nature with an undercurrent of humble service—a neighborhood where strength is not used for domination, but for stewardship of Obojima's traditions and future.

entries.name: 22 Jenni's General Store
entries: See the {@book Yatamon section|ObojimaTallGrass|4|Yatamon} in {@i Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass} for more information.

entries.name: 23 Trolley Depot

entries: {@b Tone - Loud, Industrial, Bustling}

This First Age trolley depot is a brick building sitting at the top of a steep street. The depot is not only a transport hub and a machine shop where the trolley cars are maintained, but also a favorite stop among locals and visitors alike for its commanding view of the city and its beloved shaved ice vendor, a jolly mallard spirit named Stanwick.

Spirits have run the trolley depot for as long as anyone can remember, although one human, Maxine, now works as a docent for visitors. Rumor has it that the depot was once filled with boxes of items and documents from the First Age, but long ago they were moved into the Spirit Realm for storage.

entries.name: 24 Parma & Wilkum's Woodcraft

entries: {@b Tone - Warm, Well Kept, Friendly}

Parma Dasberry, a third-generation awakened cat and master joiner, and Wilkum Goji, a stout nakudama and secondgeneration woodcutter, have been friends since their fathers introduced them as children. Years later, after each had taken over their family businesses, they decided to collaborate, combining their practices and forming a woodworking shop where they sell handmade gift boxes, beds, and other wooden accessories. The establishment is well-loved within the neighborhood, and it's even becoming a tradition among locals to present special gifts in a handmade Parma & Wilkum box.

entries.name: 25 Red's Recovery Room

entries: {@b Tone - Cozy, Dive Bar, Home-Style}

Red's Recovery Room is a clapboard hotel named after a First Age saloon that the owner, a dara named Moku Dara, saw in the liner notes of an old cassette tape. The Recovery Room serves food and drink all day and night, and Moku brews his own special beer, known as Recovery Ale, which most customers come to enjoy. He is a first-rate chef and always has the grill sizzling or the pot bubbling with an assortment of delicious dinners. The hotel also has six comfortable rooms for travelers wishing to stay.

entries.name: 26 Dawn Petal Monastery

entries: {@b Tone - Reverent, Mystical, Secretive}
