The Dawn Petal Guild is housed in a small monastery surrounded by a grove of dawn blossom trees. The guild members form the order of druids responsible for minting the magic currency on which Obojima's economy is built. The coins symbolize parts of the sacred dawn petal tree—the bud, the petal, and the flower. The druids take gold and copper ores, along with a special kind of sand, and refine each of them into the pure metals and shimmering glass from which the different coins are minted. The coins are then enchanted with the island's energy, making them almost indestructible and impossible to counterfeit. Every year, among their other ceremonial duties, the druids' central role is to officiate the Dawn Blossom Festival with the Courier Brigade, delivering dawn blossom seedlings all across Obojima.
Negi: City Center
{@b Tone - Fast, Official, Focused}

Where the two largest streets in Yatamon cross, stands the headquarters of the Courier Brigade, a repurposed First Age bank whose iconic stone facade reflects the steadfast reliability of the postal knights and their duty to Obojima. Inside the marble-floored lobby, merchants, farmers, and artisans line up with their packages so that a courier clerk can catalog and stamp them before distributing the parcels to the couriers who are ready to be sent to the farthest reaches of the island.

In the back of the building, behind a row of teller windows, lies a large bank vault with a circular steel door and a heavy brass handle. Carved into the door's outer plating is the Courier Brigade's insignia and motto, "Deliverance Through Delivery." Like their First Age counterparts, the Courier Brigade uses the vault to house valuables; in this case, these are packages deemed highly important, valuable, or sensitive by one of the courier clerks. Packages are held in the vault until ready to be assigned to a courier; during this time, it is guarded by a lance of postal knights. In addition, the organization has deployed numerous enhancements of their own creation to magically protect the vault. These include all manners of divination disruption, several boons of durability, the inability to pass between realms while inside, and the barring of invisible creatures from entering.

entries.name: Reputation
entries: In Yatamon, the headquarters is a well-known landmark, and the Courier Brigade is renowned across Obojima for its integrity and efficiency in delivering packages, supporting commerce, and providing safe escort. The Brigade's postal knights are respected for their dedication and are often seen as symbols of trust and courage; parents frequently tell tales of their exploits to inspire children—many of whom dream of being postal knights when they grow up.
The headquarters, with its formidable vault, is thought to be impregnable when locked, a notion that is tested from time to time.

entries.title: {@font DELIVERANCE THROUGH DELIVERY, THE MOTTO OF THE BRIGADE, IS FOUND REPEATEDLY THROUGHOUT THE HQ BUILDING AND IS EVEN HIDDEN WITHIN THE MAGICAL SEALS THAT PROTECT THE VAULT.|Obojima}

entries.name: The Courier Brigade's Flying Lantern
entries: The iconic flying lantern of the Courier Brigade is a newer development in the group's long history, as it's only been operational for the last twenty years. However, in that short time, the paper lantern, or "sky gondola," as some postal knights call it, has become one of the most recognizable symbols of the Courier Brigade. The lantern is sparingly used due to the difficulty with which its fuel source, the Kyojin Candle, is made; nonetheless, its existence has opened up a whole realm of possibilities for the organization and has saved countless postal knights from many perilous situations. When not used in fieldwork, the lantern is often used to transport high-ranking postal knights back and forth from Yatamon to Fort Harglo in the Gale Fields and is considered by many to be Postmaster General Miranda Escalante's personal vehicle. You can learn more about the flying lantern in the {@book Vehicles section|ObojimaTalesYatamon|5}.

entries.name: The Grand Lobby & Teller Rows
entries: For anyone who hasn't seen First Age architecture and building materials, the lobby is an impressive sight—its high ceilings and polished marble floors speak to the grandeur of a bygone age. Now, it's filled with the murmur of voices, the rustle of paper, and the rhythmic thumps of packages being stamped. The long rows of teller windows are typically staffed by diligent, uniformed courier clerks.

entries.name: The Rooftop Landing Pad
entries: The vast, open roof of the headquarters makes a perfect landing pad for the flying lantern, marked with a glowing "X"—thanks to a special concoction from the Witchery. While the flying lantern is docked here, several bollards with thick ropes secure it to its moorings.

entries.name: The Training Grounds
entries: A sprawling park stretches directly behind the building and has been reconfigured by the Brigade for training purposes. It features obstacle courses designed for both foot and mounted couriers, a stable for flightless bird mounts, and areas for rope work and climbing maneuvers. The air here often rings with the sound of clashing practice blades, the shouts of new recruits, and the thuds of falls and failed attempts.

entries.name: The Dispatcher's Tower
entries: This multi-story wooden structure is modeled after the towers found at the Broken Bird Airfield and is built behind the headquarters, overlooking the training grounds and landing pad. Its observation deck is filled with maps, charts, colored flags, and a complex system of First Age "speaking tubes" (a public address system) made operational through the joint efforts of AHA and the Tall Hat coven. This system allows the operator to broadcast announcements throughout the Courier Brigade headquarters and training grounds.

entries.name: The Couriers' Mess Hall
entries: A large dining hall was built on the training grounds, where members of all ranks gather for meals. Apart from dining, it's a place for camaraderie through storytelling and sharing news from across Obojima, with walls adorned with maps and mementos from past deliveries.

entries.name: Caddaway (spirit)
entries: Caddaway is a large bull spirit and the companion of Miranda Escalante, though he sees himself as her guardian. Caddaway wasn't always a part of the Brigade. Before he became attached to Miranda, he was a powerful nature spirit who often found himself at odds with the postal knights traveling through his domain. Until Miranda befriended him, the Brigade had marked him as a dangerous spirit, with orders to flee on sight. Now, at Miranda's behest, Caddaway works alongside couriers, though most believe he still despises many of the knights.
When Caddaway isn't with Miranda, he can be found sleeping in the back of the vault.

entries.name: Hoshino (male human)
entries: Hoshino is a kind but intensely focused man in his late fifties, with a neatly trimmed beard and a perpetual furrow in his brow. He is the head origami mage of the Yatamon division and spends most days working in an offshoot building of the headquarters. His work primarily focuses on designing arcane envelopes, developing specialty papers for letters, and creating magics that can be woven into the folds of package wrapping.

entries.name: Chief Dispatcher Ami (female elf)
entries: Ami is a highly intelligent and exceptionally organized young woman who has been placed in charge of the headquarters' daily operations by the Postmaster General. As Chief Dispatcher, she manages the flow of all incoming and outgoing packages, memorizing routes and timetables with uncanny precision. She knows every courier by name and is the first to notice if one is late or goes missing. Ami thrives on the chaos, taking a particular joy in shouldering the immense mental load that is required by her position. On several occasions, Mr. Bassingstoke has expressed to Ami and other highranking officials that her mental prowess is being squandered at the Brigade and that, with his tutelage, she could become one of Yatamon's most talented mages. However, this information has done nothing to dissuade Ami from her line of work.

entries.name: Knight Commander Rai (male human)
entries: Knight Commander Rai has a booming voice, a weathered face, and eyes like a hawk. As the postal knight in charge of new recruits, Rai oversees the training grounds, where he teaches them the core skills of the postal knights. He pushes his recruits hard but cares deeply for their safety and success, and even has a soft spot for newcomers with "the will to fight." He is perhaps the most skilled swordsman in Yatamon outside of the sword school, though he would never claim as much himself.

entries.name: Captain Riku (male nakudama)
entries: Captain Riku is the reliable and loyal pilot of the flying lantern and a dedicated postal knight. He navigates Obojima's skies with impressive skill and knows the wind patterns of the Gale Fields better than anyone. Being a natural storyteller, he often regales his anxious passengers with tales of exciting aerial deliveries, cloud-dwelling spirits, and close encounters with the great beasts.

items.title: {@font AMONG BANDITS, MIRANDA ESCALANTE IS KNOWN AS STEEL TOE MIRANDA|Obojima}

items.name: Postmaster General Miranda Escalante (female human)
entries: Miranda Escalante is the current leader of the Courier Brigade's Yatamon division. She rose through the ranks as a postal knight and, as a natural leader, began to make a name for herself. She earned the respect of her fellow couriers by designing innovative formations, establishing new routes, inspiring cadets to join, and, above all else, protecting her companions. Her charisma and strength led her to her position, and by the time she was ready to take it, not a soul in the organization would deny her claim. As the Postmaster General, she's honest and forthcoming, striving to lead the division with confidence and doing all she can to prepare her knights for the journeys ahead.

entries.name: The Missing Messenger & the Secret Package
entries: A decorated postal knight carrying a top-priority package entrusted to them by Postmaster General Escalante vanishes mid-delivery in a notoriously dangerous region. The adventurers are hired to accompany a group of postal knights and retrieve the missing courier and the package.

entries.name: Lantern Sabotage
entries: Just before a critical delivery, the flying lantern suffers a mysterious malfunction. It's not a simple mechanical error— the handcrafted gears that raise and lower the lantern's candle have been removed. The adventures have been hired discreetly by Captain Riku to investigate the airship, uncover the saboteur, and learn why this particular delivery was stopped in the first place.

entries.name: Postmaster's Test
entries: The latest batch of new recruits has been sworn in as postal knights, but Postmaster General Escalante is worried that Knight Commander Rai granted them the title too early. To test this concern, she has assigned the new postal knights the evening watch at the headquarters and, at the same time, has hired the adventurers to break in and steal a fake package from the vault—with the caveat that no one gets hurt and no damage comes to the building.

entries.name: The Great River Tournament

entries: Negi: Path

Each spring and autumn, Obojima turns its eyes to the Grand Tournament Arena, one of the largest structures on the island and one of the few buildings in Yatamon not crafted in the First Age. Inside it, the celebrated sporting event known as the Great River Tournament is held. The arena is nestled along a bend of the Serpent River where the Negi neighborhood blends into the forested greenery of Yatamon's Path, making the grounds around it a lush and beautiful parkland.

At the arena, warriors, monks, farmers, fishers, and former adventurers are called to compete in a series of ritualistic contests as teams, vying for the coveted Fourfold Chalice. These groups are formed by the tournament's Abaro (game runners), each carefully created to embody the essence of one of the island's four honored river spirits: the swift and selfless blue back salmon, Din; the tenacious and aggressive giant hog, Yon; the wise and tactical serpent dragon, Mu; and the agile and cunning monkey, Go.

During the off-seasons, the teams are formed anew, allowing unexpected pairings and surprise rivalries to emerge, heightening anticipation for the event as the teams train and practice. The victorious team doesn't just win gold and fame; they also earn a ceremonial blessing from the Abaro, which is believed to bring good fortune until it is granted to the next game's winners.

entries.name: Reputation
entries: Across Obojima, the Great River Tournament is legendary. As the games draw near, the air around the arena crackles with anticipation, a blend of hushed reverence and boisterous excitement. Many travel from nearby towns and settlements, and those who can't attend often wait with bated breath for bards and storytellers to visit their local tavern and recount tales of the tournament. It is uncommon for any Obojiman not to have heard of the Great River Tournament.

entries.name: The Four Games
entries: Every tournament consists of four games in which the contestants compete in feats of strength, skill, and intellect—sometimes against each other and sometimes against the arena itself. The games themselves take inspiration from the four great rivers and their many attributes.

entries.name: Canyon Dash
entries: This game tests a team's ability to navigate a shifting, disorienting maze while protecting a delicate cargo: a shallow bowl of water. The team that manages to arrive at the center of the maze with the fullest bowl of water within the allotted time wins. This game is a clash of patience, strategy, and wrestling, as teams send out their largest and fiercest members to engage opponents while the swiftest protect and carefully carry their bowl through the maze.

entries.name: Sky Pole
entries: In this game, one member on each team must balance on a tall wooden beam while their teammates below must defend them against their opponents. A variety of specialty items, such as {@item Nakudama Bubble Rod|ObojimaTallGrass|Nakudama Bubble Rods}{@sup °}, ropes, weighted bags, ladders, and saws, are hidden throughout the arena to use. The last team with a player balanced on their beam wins.

entries.name: Channel Dig
entries: This game is a race against other teams to dig and shape a new river channel across a massive sand replica of Obojima. As the game begins, the teams are placed at the base of Mount Arbora and must dig their way south using nothing but their hands. Like hidden traps, boulders are buried just below the surface of the island, and any team unlucky enough to discover one must dig it up before moving on. Periodically, limited supplies of shovels and other tools are dropped into the arena, which the teams must fight to secure. The game ends when a team digs its channel to the edge of the island and pulls the rope of a single central pulley, suspended just above the game area, releasing water stored at the top of Mount Arbora into its river channel.

entries.name: River's Bounty
entries: This game is a high-energy free-for-all in which teams fight to secure the river pearl and fill their decorative vase. The river pearl—a polished granite sphere one foot in diameter—is placed on top of a sand plinth in the center of the arena. When the game begins, teams rush to seize it. While the river pearl is touched only by members of a single team, a spigot above that team's large decorative vase begins to flow. The game ends when a team fills its vase.

entries.name: The Fourfold Chalice
entries: The winning team of the games is granted the honor of participating in the Ceremony of the Chalice, a ritual in which the performers drink from the Fourfold Chalice, a vessel divided into four chambers—each filled with water from one of the four great rivers. When the winners drink from the chalice, the waters flow together in a symbolic gesture that signifies the competition is over and the divisions among competitors are dissolved.

entries.name: Preparing for the Games
entries: Once teams are chosen by the Abaro, rigorous training begins both in the Grand Tournament Arena and in designated training areas around the city.

Competitors are known as Quadai, and they prepare themselves in mind, body, and spirit in various ways. Though each team is formed early in the off-season, Quadai often prefer to train alone or in small groups until the games draw near, at which point the team practices together. Although the games remain the same, the organizers of the tournament—the Grand Tournament Society—often make adjustments to keep the audience engaged. These variations are secretly revealed to the Quadai one month before the games begin.

entries.name: Mysticism & Magic
entries: Behind the ceremonial rituals, colorful chants, and celebratory dances lies a sacred pact. The Grand Tournament Arena is hallowed ground, protected by old oaths sworn to the island's four great river spirits. No magic may be used during the games—unless it's woven into the rules. Breaking this taboo is an insult to the spirits and could call forth their wrath.

Each spirit—Din (salmon), Yon (boar), Mu (serpent dragon), and Go (monkey)—has a shrine hidden from spectators beneath the arena. These shrines are where the teams prepare before and during the games. The teams are also sworn to keep the locations of these shrines secret. A team whose actions honor and exemplify its mascot's strengths during the games may empower these shrines, gaining a temporary magical boon from one of the river spirits.

Various spells are triggered during the different matches, first agreed upon by the Abaro and other officials before the games are announced. Most of these spells are produced by centuries-old enchantments built into the arena and are triggered by the chants of the crowd. Occasionally, a spell seems to choose favorites, perhaps due to the influence of the great river spirits at work within the arena.

Outside spells are forbidden during the tournament itself, but some Quadai bend the line with clever potions and enchanted items blessed beforehand by local witches— pushing the rules to their limits during preparation before matches.

entries.title: {@font THE TOTEM OF YON, THE BOAR SPIRIT, IS FREQUENTLY GIVEN SNACKS TO SATIATE THE TENACIOUS SPIRIT'S HUNGER|Obojima}

entries.name: The River Pillars
entries: Located just outside the main arena gates, four carved wooden pillars have been erected to represent each of the great river spirits. These statues are not mere decorations—during the tournament, their eyes glow when the corresponding team wins an event, allowing those outside the venue to learn of the victors quickly. Devout players and citizens often leave flowers, fruits, and small, hand-carved wooden animals as offerings here.

entries.name: The Dawn Petal Pavilion
entries: The Dawn Petal Pavilion is a serene grove of ancient dawn blossom trees, standing just outside the main entrance to the Grand Tournament Arena. Here, a group of Dawn Petal druids perform an opening ritual before each day of competition and a closing ritual afterward, blessing the competitors. The grounds are adorned with fresh flowers and intricate paper crafts, while softly burning incense fills the air.

entries.name: The Celebratory Gate
entries: A massive, intricately carved wooden gate serves as the main entrance to the Grand Tournament Arena. During tournament days, it's draped with vibrant banners and ribbons, and often hosts a small band of musicians playing festive tunes beneath it. This is where the impressive procession of players enters the arena on opening day.

entries.name: The Betting Pavilion & Bazaar
entries: Tucked under a long red awning near the east wall of the arena, the Betting Pavillion is a bustling, smoke-filled area where bets are placed, odds are whispered, and rivalries flare. Merchants from across Obojima lay wagers and gossip in equal measure. The air here is thick with excited chatter, clinking coins, and the enticing aromas of street food.

During tournament season, a bazaar springs up around the arena grounds. Local artisans, bakers, and tailors sell everything from plush mascots to sashes and painted banners in team colors, good luck charms, and savory skewers.

entries.name: The Grand Arena
entries: The circular arena is around 300 feet in diameter and is sunk nearly 10 feet below the first row of tiered seating, keeping any water used in the games away from the crowds and giving spectators an overhead view. The arena's standard seating accommodates thousands of cheering spectators, while private rooms and secluded specialty seating allow for several hundred more. During matches, the energy in the arena is electric, and its symphony of roars and gasps echoes throughout the nearby neighborhoods in Yatamon.

entries.name: Practice Grounds
entries: The Practice Grounds are a sprawling outdoor area behind the arena where Quadai hone their skills. It features various obstacles, heavy practice dummies made from tightly bound straw, a small muddy pit for wrestling practice, and a wooden climbing wall for agility exercises. During the weeks leading up to the tournament, passersby can hear the grunts of exertion from competitors and the cheers of supporters as they encourage their favorites.

entries.name: Grand Abaro Tsurei (male human)
entries: Tsurei is a stoic monk and the most revered Abaro to ever run the games. While the tournament is underway, he is dressed in ceremonial garb: a cascading set of golden robes and a tall, embroidered hat made to look like the churning waters of a river. He carries a Kyūryū—a river staff used to indicate the winner of a match and the tournament—and is widely respected for his impeccable fairness.

entries.name: Elder Aiko (female human)
entries: Aiko is a Dawn Petal druid who shares ceremonial duties with Grand Abaro Tsurei. She is clad in flowing ceremonial robes adorned with intricate petal embroidery and carries a magnificent fan, intricately carved with images of the four river spirits. She serves as chief officiant, overseeing all rituals and presenting awards. She has a deep understanding of the subtle workings of the Grand Tournament and its connection to the nature spirits.

entries.name: Kenji Karuka (male nakudama)
entries: Kenji is the Head Arena Custodian, a gruff and honest fellow who knows every nook and cranny of the arena and has a keen eye for talent. He also runs a discreet but thriving betting operation from a small, unassuming booth near the back entrance. He has a network of informants who keep him apprised of injuries and player morale.

entries.name: Ben Boarashi, the Bristleback Basher (male human)
entries: Ben is a former Quadai Champion who now helps officiate. A fierce brawler covered in scars, Boarashi often wears his ceremonial bristle armor and delights fans of all ages with his iconic thunder snort. Rumor has it that he once suplexed an oni into unconsciousness. He has a secret rivalry with Saliah that dates back years.

entries.name: Keela Karmandi, the Cartwheel Kid (female elf)
entries: Keela is a wiry, hyper elf with a perpetually curious glint in her eyes. As a Quadai renowned for her agility and acrobatic feats, she often performs daring maneuvers that leave the crowd breathless. Keela has a jovial personality, always ready with a joke or a playful taunt, and is fiercely loyal to her teammates.

entries.name: Dugo Dara, the Blue Flash (dara)
entries: Dugo is a Quadai and blue dara, known for unusually quick and nimble movements. They are renowned for their speed and slippery evasions, making them a nightmare to catch in maze and balancing contests. Dugo secretly uses a special herbal paste during the balancing contest, a closely guarded secret.

entries.name: Saliah Sato, the River Serpent (female human)
entries: The picture of elegance, Saliah is a woman of lean build with sharp eyes and a calm demeanor. As a Quadai, she's a master strategist, celebrated for her tactical brilliance and ability to outthink her opponents. She's won the chalice numerous times and has been given the formal title of champion within the tournament. Saliah is always impeccably dressed in her ceremonial attire and presents herself in a regal manner. However, those connected to the shadier side of the awakened cat community know her better as the "gambling maniac" with a knack for losing and a growing debt to some unsavory cats.

entries.name: Choro Saltado (male human)
entries: Choro is a young Quadai and a kind and eventempered individual whose relaxed demeanor would fool anyone into thinking he has no ambitions in life. To the contrary, Choro desires nothing more than to attain the title of champion and become one of the great Quadai of his era. He can be quite aloof about his personal life and prefers to spend most days training alone. One truth he will readily admit is his love of food. Most nights, he can be found sampling the newest dish at Yamago's Delicatessen.

entries.name: Sabotage
entries: A disillusioned former player, bitter about an old injury, is rumored to have hired someone to secretly sabotage the contest to ensure certain teams lose. The adventurers must investigate without interrupting the games and determine whether the rumor is true and, if so, uncover the former player's motivations.

entries.name: Enchantment Malfunction
entries: One of the game's enchantments has gone haywire during a match, causing several injuries and magically freezing half a dozen players in the arena. When the Abaro running the games went to investigate, they found the glyphs that activate the enchantments sundered and replaced with makeshift magics, and the arena custodian, Kenji, lying unconscious nearby. Eager to free their players and complete the match, the Grand Tournament Society has hired a number of talented witches to dissolve the magics lingering in the arena and is seeking help to uncover the plot against the tournament and its players.

entries.name: The Missing Lucky Charm
entries: A wealthy Quadai from Opal Falls approaches the party, distraught. His family's priceless River Stone, a lucky charm said to bring victory in the River Trials, has been stolen. He offers a hefty reward for its safe return before the grand finale.

entries.name: The Debt Collector's Demand
entries: Saliah Sato, the celebrity Quadai, is being blackmailed by a crime boss cat who demands that she intentionally lose the final match to clear her gambling debts. Her longtime friend, an awakened cat named Rabi, has secretly reached out to the adventurers asking for help, hoping they can find a way to free Saliah from the debt without tarnishing her name.

entries.name: Last-Minute Adjustments
entries: The tournament is just a few days away, and catastrophe has struck—a celebration in honor of the performers has left many Quadai and attendees seriously ill. The problem was traced to a young food vendor who enhanced their famous stew with several potions and magical ingredients, resulting in numerous extended cases of Potion Sickness. Most of the affected Quadai have already been replaced, but open slots remain on each team and must be filled before the start of the games.

entries.name: Spiritual Spectators
entries: Some believe the four great river spirits secretly manifest as spectators during each tournament. One rumor even goes so far as to say that Go, the monkey river spirit, once wrestled in disguise simply to feel the adulation of the crowd.

entries.name: Great Spirit Ka
entries: An old wives' tale claims that hidden within the depths of the arena is the final resting place of a secret fifth river spirit—a blind eel known as Ka, said to represent the rivers that flow below the surface of the island.

entries.name: Original Quadai
entries: Popular bardic stories tell that the first Quadai were all paladins of the great rivers and battled to settle which of the four spirits was strongest. That battle has since been carried on in the form of the Great River Tournament.
Negi: The Wood

There is a wealth of information on Canden and Moon in {@i {@book Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass|ObojimaTallGrass}} . We recommend reading the relevant sections of that book to fully understand the school.
{@b Tone - Serene, Disciplined, Purposeful}

Within the Negi Neighborhood, amid a grove of carefully selected trees and a manicured garden that doubles as training grounds, stands a work of art that blends modern design with that of the First Age. The Canden and Moon Academy of Swords—a martial arts school dedicated to the refinement of mind, body, and spirit—is housed in an ornate, hexagonal structure built atop the remains of a First Age boarding school that once engulfed an entire city block. While the school is famed across Obojima for its unique approach to sword mastery, to the residents of Yatamon, Canden and Moon's is more than just a school; it's a pillar of the community.

Governed by the motto, "right conduct and proper form in every situation," the Canden and Moon's Academy of Swords cultivates not only martial prowess but also a deep commitment to community service. As students learn the discipline and techniques of the sword—many choosing to live at the school while attending—they are expected to contribute to Yatamon's well-being, regularly assisting locals and performing acts of kindness beyond the school grounds as part of their training. To the masters of the school, service is just as important as the sword.

There are many across Obojima who have spent at least a summer studying at the school, a testament to the school's widespread influence and its reputation for instilling discipline, good character, and its philosophy of communal care. Only a few go on to take up a training sword, fewer still an actual sword, and only the most dedicated become masters themselves. Even if one never achieves true mastery of the blade, the lessons learned with Canden and Moon shape individuals into principled members of society.

entries.name: Reputation
entries: Canden and Moon's Academy of Swords is the largest sword school on Obojima and is widely considered the most prestigious. Masters Canden and Moon are revered figures, seen as benevolent protectors of Yatamon, whose counsel is sought by many. While the school's sword style is known for its elegance and precision, it faces some criticism from rival schools for emphasizing form over practicality, though this critique is often dismissed by those who have witnessed its effectiveness in action.

entries.name: A Tragic Past
entries: Decades ago, in their youthful prime, Canden and Moon were involved in a duel with an elder demon that escalated disastrously. Even then, both masters were unbelievably skilled, but their swordcraft was untempered by any philosophy. Their reckless duel, fought in a small, isolated village, brought a curse upon the land and surrounding forest—a curse that, over the span of a year, caused the inhabitants of the village to fall ill and eventually die.

This incident is the traumatic origin of their motto, "right conduct and proper form in every situation." Both masters still carry immense guilt, believing that their unchecked power and arrogance led to the village's demise. They have since worked tirelessly to atone, dedicating their lives to service and teaching the responsible use of power. To this day, they perform a yearly, arduous pilgrimage to the now-desolate "Empty Village," alongside a band of Fumoshiki, in hopes of sealing the lingering curse and appeasing the tormented spirits that still inhabit the area.

entries.name: The Grounds
entries: The grounds surrounding the school resemble a well-manicured garden. Maple, pine, cypress, ginkgo, camellias, and flowering cherry trees are expertly arranged throughout, while mosscovered boulders and rounded shrubs accent the space. At one end, a serene, shallow pond, surrounded by smooth river stones and a small bamboo grove, is often used for quiet contemplation by both masters and students. At the other end, an ancient maple tree rises from the center of a rock garden, where daily drills and demonstrations take place.

entries.name: Dormitory
entries: The dormitory occupies multiple levels of the school and offers comfortable, albeit spartan, living quarters for students. Each room has a small window overlooking either the garden or the city streets.

entries.name: The Library
entries: A well-stocked library is maintained within the school, filled not only with texts on sword techniques and martial history but also with volumes of philosophy, poetry, history, and civic governance, some of which were penned by Master Canden himself.

entries.name: The Overview
entries: On the highest floor of the school is an interior training hall used by the masters to teach their most skilled students. When not in use, Masters Canden and Moon sometimes observe the gardens from this vantage point, watching over the students and taking note of their progress.

entries.name: Master Canden and Master Moon
entries: To learn more about the Masters of the school read their entries in {@i {@book Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass|ObojimaTallGrass}}.

entries.name: Zenna Wixin (female elf)
entries: Zenna is a senior student on the cusp of mastery, known for her dedication and athleticism. Though her skill equals or exceeds that of others who have mastered the school's sword technique, she has failed the final trial seven times. Master Moon has told her that she must adopt the philosophy of the school as her own if she ever wishes to best a master, but Zenna's stubbornness has prevented her from truly accepting that guidance.

entries.name: Elijah Koro (male human)
entries: Elijah is a boisterous, strong-willed student who excels in brute strength and direct combat but struggles with the elegant, fluid movements of the Canden and Moon style. He frequently chafes under the discipline of the masters and craves opportunities to prove himself in combat, often volunteering for "monster watch" duties. He's popular with the younger students but often receives silent disapproval from Master Canden for his lack of form.

entries.name: Haru Dara (male dara)
entries: Haru is a quiet and unassuming dara who maintains the gardens. He was one of the first students to join the school when the masters started teaching decades ago, and although he came to realize that the sword was not his calling, he never left their side. Instead, he offered his skills to help the school grow and flourish. Years later, he serves as the groundskeeper and remains a dear friend of the masters.

entries.name: Nanny Kimi (female human)
entries: Nanny Kimi is a kind but stern older woman who helps out around the school. In addition to aiding the masters with whatever tasks require attention, she is also known as the school's "mother" and cares for students whenever possible. She spends most of her days completing small tasks and running errands. She has a private room on the first floor of the school, where she lives, and a dedicated space on the grounds for a small, vegetable garden she calls her own.

entries.name: Starfall
entries: Starfall, the legendary, ceremonial blade traditionally used for the master duels, is stolen from a locked display case in the school's private armory. The masters discreetly reach out to the adventurers to retrieve it.

entries.name: Lost Expedition
entries: A team of AHA researchers, escorted by sword school students, goes missing in a newly discovered section of the subway tunnels beneath Yatamon. The masters dispatch the adventurers alongside a senior student to find them, suspecting that something more dangerous than typical monsters lurks below.

entries.name: The Master's Challenge
entries: A powerful, arrogant martial artist arrives in Yatamon, publicly mocking the Canden and Moon style as "flashy" and "impractical." They issue a formal challenge to either master. While the masters themselves are formidable, Nanny Kimi implores the adventurers to investigate the challenger's true strength or uncover any underhanded tactics they might employ.

items: {@b Nasu is a lively, enchantment-rich district in the heart} of Yatamon, known far and wide as the home of the Witchery, the city's great academy of arcane learning. Students in mismatched robes with their spirit-companion sidekicks bustle along its streets, darting between lectures to local markets like Yanari, where they search for ingredients and grab a treat before dashing back to class. Those not in school often find themselves partaking in the delights of the arcane arts at one of the many shops and services, and those not partaking are honing their craft in those same establishments. But as with everything in Yatamon, one cannot visit Nasu without experiencing the wonders of the past—from the serene Dara Cultural Center to the coin-operated laundromat of Shoko's Egg Farm. Here, even the oddest relics of the First Age—like the blinking facade of the Witchery or the iron machines within the Yatamon Daily Observer building—still operate with the vigor of a new age. Strange, brilliant, and unpredictable, Nasu thrives on arcane energy and youthful ambition.

entries.name: Magic as Art
entries: The Nasu neighborhood is known for its magical entertainments and expressions. Due to the Witchery and Yanari Market, there are many students and practitioners of enchantment who perform demonstrations of the arcane arts and create permanent installations of magic throughout the neighborhood. An adventurer walking through Nasu might see buildings that change color when it rains, magical light shows at night, statues that animate to give information, and wizards crafting bubble sculptures to delight children in the park.

entries.name: 30 The Beehive Inn
entries: See the {@book Yatamon section|ObojimaTallGrass|4|Yatamon} in {@i Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass} for more information.

entries.name: 31 Fenwick's Catmint Emporium

entries: {@b Tone - Relaxed, Comfortable, Moody}

In an alley nearly too narrow for humans to slip through is a colorfully painted, cat-sized door that opens into a lavishly decorated room filled with cushions, low tables, warm overhanging lamps, and heavy drapes—a room of comfort built for cats. Walkways and private booths are mounted to the walls for high-paying patrons to get away from the floor chatter and enjoy the overlook of the establishment. Fenwick, the proprietor, is an awakened cat—and a rare calico—who grows and sells the finest catmint in all of Yatamon and built his Catmint Emporium when he was just a youth. The Emporium is a pillar of the feline community and is frequented by all walks of life.

entries.name: 32 The Block

entries: {@b Tone - Busy, Friendly, Daily Living}

In northern Nasu there is a First Age apartment complex known by the residents of Yatamon as the Block. This large five-story building is home to over 300 people, many of whom run workshops from their homes where they make and sell goods to those who wander down the halls. In combination with the other businesses, markets, and artisans that operate out of the small apartments, the Block has become a central hub for this part of the neighborhood and for those who live in northern Yatamon. In recent memory, a school was also founded on the second floor of the building, which popularized its second nickname, "the city in the city."

entries.name: 33 Dara Cultural Center

entries: {@b Tone - Mysterious, Sacred, Educational}

New buildings and changes to Yatamon's streets don't happen often, as the people of the First Age city don't often find the need to build with such a well-made city left for them to use. But there are exceptions, and one of them is the Glyph Pillars. There are twenty-four Glyph Pillars arranged in concentric circles, each bearing a dara glyph like those placed in Roa Kala by the First Dara. The site is maintained by dara sages who teach non-dara about their history and culture, and they encourage any dara to commune with the glyphs.

entries.name: 34 Shoko's Egg Farm

entries: {@b Tone - Down to Earth, Friendly, Kind}

The ancient machines of the Kwikie Kleen Laundromat are now used to house chickens, ducks, and geese for Shoko's Egg Farm. The kindly old spirit that runs the farm, Mr. Shoko, has done so since he came to the city nearly 135 years ago. As he tells it, when he came to Yatamon from the Spirit Realm to start a new life, he took up residence in the laundromat, and it was there that he met a young chicken who set him on his new path. Now, all these years later, Shoko's Egg Farm is cherished by the surrounding neighborhood. The eggs at Mr. Shoko's farm are completely free to anyone who wants them, but the locals always insist on giving Mr. Shoko something in return.
Nasu: Wickwood Ave: 035
{@b Tone - Inviting, Bright, Playful}

On the cracked pavement of Wickwood Ave, in the shade of a large kojobi tree, sits a well-known delicatessen run by the charming Chef Yamago Luki. The stall shows its age—wood paneling worn smooth by years of visitors, canvas signs tattered and stained by exuberant customers after tasting one of Chef Yamago's delicious treats. But those rough edges are more than offset by the blooming flowers and climbing foliage that make sitting at Yamago's bar such a pleasant experience.

Even so, the stall could be stripped of all its charm, and the people of Yatamon would still flock to try Chef Yamago's unique creations. Unlike other food vendors, the peculiar ingredients he uses in his food are more common in potion brewing than cooking. By name alone, Chef Yamago's dishes don't sound especially appetizing—yet locals swear by his creations.

entries.name: Chef's Special
entries: The menu at Yamago's Delicatessen is in constant flux, as Chef Yamago tends to make whatever he feels like at the moment. Some days it's grilled claysnake and fried noodle eel; other times, his bar is filled with pastries and other baked goods. Regardless of what he decides to serve, he receives little to no complaints from his patrons.

entries.name: Missing Merchant
entries: Chef Yamago was supposed to receive two crates of {@item Bundle of Peeping Willow|ObojimaTallGrass|peeping willow}{@sup °} late last night, but the merchant never showed up. The chef happens to know this gentleman personally and says this is out of character. Yamago is willing to trade some high-quality potion ingredients if someone can confirm that the merchant is okay and put his worries to rest.

entries.name: Vengeful Patron
entries: Overnight, pest spirits made off with all of Chef Yamago's cutlery. Though the culprit is unknown, the chef suspects a belligerent patron he threw out yesterday may be behind it.

entries.name: Chef Yamago Luki (male nakudama)
entries: Chef Yamago Luki, the boisterous nakudama with a fondness for smoking and gossip, has been running Yamago's Delicatessen for the past ten years—since he won it in a game of cards while traveling with the Courier Brigade. In that decade, the chef has made a name for himself as the master of odd ingredients, creating delicious treats and meals from plants and creatures he's discovered on his travels.
Though he appreciates the praise, admiration has never been his goal—Yamago simply enjoys the craft of cooking and will keep at it until he gets bored of it.
Nasu: Main Street
{@b Tone - Vibrant, Gritty, Exciting}

The Daily Observer HQ is a small building on Main Street where the lights are on 24 hours a day. It's here that the sleepless reporters craft the Yatamon Daily Observer, a biweekly paper that gives the latest updates on markets, local happenings, new shops, rumors and gossip, upcoming festivals, and more.

Inside the building, the main room with its wood-plank floor hums with quiet activity, illuminated by overhead lamps with green glass shades. Half a dozen or so reporters work diligently on their stories at wooden desks strewn with papers and First Age writing implements. Sheets of paper are pinned to the walls with notes, tips, and page layouts for the next edition. A door in the back leads to the press room, where a large First Age machine sits—a metal contraption weighing over a ton— waiting to spring to life at a moment's notice when the latest edition is ready to go to print.

entries.name: Clarion Call
entries: Every so often, the Yatamon Daily Observer prints a special insert in the paper called the Clarion Call, a series of requests for explorers, adventurers, and arcanists who can help with problems near and far. Should any wish to be gainfully employed, keep an eye out for the latest insert posted at the neighborhood taverns and at the Courier Brigade HQ.

entries.name: The News Paper
entries: The Yatamon Daily Observer has the feel of a First Age newspaper—a form that Edwin chose to emulate based on research during his time working with AHA. The printing press, powered by Murph, churns out each edition before the team assembles and folds the papers by hand. Here are several recurring columns and features:

entries.name: Neighborhood Watch
entries: Community reports from each of the neighborhoods.

entries.name: Ms. Morita's Hot Takes
entries: Reviews of local inns and taverns.

entries.name: Market Chat
entries: The latest news from the Yanari Witches' Market.

entries.name: Spirit Whispers
entries: Recent happenings at the Gap and surrounding area.

entries.name: Festival Time!
entries: Upcoming festivals and celebrations and any Tamh Gon sightings.

entries.name: Monster Eye
entries: A recap of any monster and demon activity in and around Old Yatamon.

entries.name: Edwin "Ed" Murto (male elf)
entries: Ed is a thoughtful, hard-working elf who some might say is overly dedicated to his vision of bringing information and entertainment to the residents of Yatamon. He's often a quiet observer in life, but when needed can bring an impassioned, charismatic speech to any occasion. At the moment, he's working with AHA and the Courier Brigade who often bring him new leads for stories— the most recent being unusual rumors from the southernmost part of the Brackwater Wetlands of an abnormal sludge that has washed up on shore after the freakish earthquake and tsunami.

entries.name: Origin of the Yatamon Daily Observer
entries: Long ago, when AHA first assembled in Yatamon, archaeologists unearthed a large and technical First Age machine from underneath the ruins of Old Yatamon. At this time, AHA was collecting more First Age objects than they knew what to do with, and so they decided to table their examination and store it in the Research Academy Building to be studied at a later date. The device languished for decades before a young and idealistic archaeologist, Edwin "Ed" Murto, rediscovered the machine while cataloging the stored inventory in the Academy basement. Curious, he and his companion spirit, Murph, spent some time with the machine, visiting on occasion and allowing Murph to whelm the contraption whenever they did. Eventually, the two surmised the machine's capabilities, and after some testing, used the printing press to replicate the first-ever document in the basement of the AHA Research Academy Building. Ed, who was already intrigued with stories and the latest happenings in the world, saw an opportunity to share tales of Yatamon with all who were interested. Ed would later strike a deal with the leaders of AHA, and begin the Yatamon Daily Observer soon after.

entries.name: Bringing Obojima to Your Kitchen Table
entries: As Editor-in-Chief of the Yatamon Daily Observer, Edwin assembled a team of young, idealistic reporters from all over Yatamon, each with a passion for fact-finding and adventure. Residents of Yatamon love reading stories from the reporters—tales of exploring the arcane pools in the Land of Hot Water, of their harrowing brush with {@creature Jumaga|ObojimaTallGrass}{@sup °} at the Ledge of Offering, or of the nomadic sword masters Tellu and Scale. As readership grows, Ed is always on the lookout for bigger stories and new reporters to add to the staff.

entries.name: Murph (spirit)
entries: Murph is an amorphous spectral spirit with exaggerated facial features and an affinity for First Age hats, which he's never seen without. Murph has been good friends and business partners with Ed for the last decade and has been an integral part of the Daily Observer's success. When Murph isn't running the printing press, he's helping Ed direct the team or taking meetings on behalf of the Daily Observer. Many of the reporters see Murph as Ed's louder and more eccentric half.

entries.name: Ms. Morita (female human)
entries: Ms. Morita is a tough-as-nails journalist and an active member of the Fish Head Coven. She's the Yatamon Daily Observer's resident expert in the arcane, researching rumors of rare ingredients, the latest news from the Witchery, Yanari Market happenings, and the most recent spell mishaps in the city.

entries.name: Mugo Dara (male blue dara)
entries: Mugo is a wanderer by nature who writes a column about the First Dara titled "Path of the First." Each installment is filled with stories of Mugo's travels as he tries to retrace the footsteps of the First Dara. He also features interviews with Roa Kala elders, reports of his latest glyph findings, and dara tales and myths.

entries.name: Raymond Flerb Esq. (male nakudama)
entries: Raymond is a hard-hitting, hard-smoking reporter who is always wearing the same suit that looks like he's been sleeping in it for weeks. Ray knows all the streets of Yatamon, having had a couple dozen jobs in his youth, and is well-connected with the seedier side of the First Age city.

entries.name: Sally Pipps (female human)
entries: Sally is a plucky, whip-smart reporter who uses her connections at the Courier Brigade to plan and research her fieldwork so she can bring stories from all over Obojima. She'll report on any story worth telling, though her passion is anything related to dangerous creatures.

entries.name: The Witchery

entries: Nasu: City Center

Once a First Age movie theater, the Witchery is now a beacon of arcane learning and coven cooperation in the city of Yatamon—a school for young witches to learn and practice their crafts under the tutelage of some of the finest spellcasters on the island.

From the outside, the old building still bears its original neon-lit facade with the First Age symbols marking it as the "Olympia Theater," now enchanted with magics that make the lettering flicker and change color. Wide steps lead up to several sets of ornate metal-and-glass doors that welcome all into the lavishly decorated lobby of Obojima's most famous arcane academy.

entries.name: Interior
entries: For any traveler who hasn't been inside a First Age building, stepping through the double doors feels like walking into another world. An enormous red carpet flows across the floor like the shimmering skin of an elder spirit as floating light bulbs illuminate the interior, and clusters of companion spirits nap on chandeliers or follow students through the halls. Over the years, witches have embroidered constellations and runes on the floor and embellished scenes from the legendary accomplishments of historic coven members on large tapestries that line the walls.

At all hours of the day and night, the smell of incense and herbs comes from censers that hang from the Witchery's high ceiling, and the complex, bubbling aroma of multiple cauldrons wafts through the halls.

entries.name: The Witchery History
entries: After a few decades of heated rivalries that would occasionally escalate into serious arcane scuffles, the Fish Head Coven's Council of Three and Thirty declared their intent to coexist in peace with the other covens. Thus, a few wise witches from the different covens came up with the idea to create a center to educate new witches, foster an environment of friendly competition between the covens, and teach young witches about the joys (and dangers) of magic. After some searching, an abandoned theater was chosen—mostly because it was large, ideal for hosting classes, and stood on neutral ground. They called it the Witchery.

entries.name: Student Life & Friendly Competitions
entries: Once their applications are accepted, students train for several years in the basics of magic. Only after proving their aptitude for witchcraft and completing several mandatory classes do students get the chance to join a coven. Each coven decides which students they wish to formally extend offers to, after which the students choose from the covens interested in them. Nearly all students receive an invitation from at least one coven, with many being presented with several offers.

entries.name: Rivalry with Yanari
entries: Despite having some top-tier potion brewers, the Yanari Witches' Market is considered a cauldron of bad habits and sloppy witchcraft by the faculty of the Witchery, and this has created a bit of a rivalry between the two. Although there are master brewers at the market, students are discouraged from attending the market's frequent potion-brewing battles, which are patrolled by Witchery faculty. Attending any of these so-called "brewing battles" is forbidden, and any student caught doing so is sure to receive a withering gaze from a coven instructor and can expect disciplinary action.

entries.name: Coven Culture in the Witchery
entries: Although all the covens share the space, each manages to contribute its own particular brand of magic and culture without dominating the school or losing their identity. Students often display subtle signs of coven preference in their garb (cloudshaped pins, quirky hats, carved gourd necklaces, etc.), but for the most part, each coven is well represented, and the choice at the end of the year is a hard one for most of the graduating witches.

entries.name: Points of Interest
entries: The Witchery is an enormous building of strange design with an even stranger interior filled with secret hallways, catwalks, and locked rooms hidden within the First Age architecture.

entries.name: Lobby
entries: The lobby is 100 feet wide with a high ceiling of 25 feet or more. The floors and walls are covered with patterned red fabric in different textures and styles, which, if inspected closely, reveal the First Age theater's distinct buttery scent. Lining the walls are a dozen chalkboards that display the day's classes and schedule. The high ceilings are adorned with ornate gilded molding, which has tarnished over the years. Floating amid the large chandeliers are hundreds of small glowing light bulbs, which slowly circulate through the building as if on a lazy river.

In the back of the space is a long stretch of glass cabinets that display scrolls, tomes, equipment, and other magical trinkets the students might need as they progress throughout their studies. Next to it, a bulletin board lists odd jobs for students wanting to earn an extra sea petal or two.

entries.name: Classrooms
entries: The six classrooms most often used by teachers from the major witch covens are located in the theater's largest auditoriums. In each, a stage has been built in front of the large white screen where lectures and demonstrations take place. The rooms are relatively soundproof, allowing for lessons that incorporate thaumaturgy, explosions, and pyrotechnics—whatever the faculty deems appropriate. Above the seating area, a balcony section provides space for visiting elders and high-ranking witches to sit in and observe classes as they take place. In addition to these six large classrooms, there are eight smaller lecture halls that are used by many different covens, including some of the lesser-known ones from across Obojima.

entries.name: Second Floor
entries: An elevator powered by a silent, spectacled potato spirit wearing a bellhop's hat opens onto a hallway that leads to the Witchery's many "viewing booths," rooms each with a small window that overlooks a classroom. Each booth houses rolls of First Age pictures and a single projector. One of these small booths has been fashioned into a study room called the "Illusionists Loft," where advanced students learn about light, sound, and First Age illusions using one of these spiritwhelmed projectors.

entries.name: The Wayward Student
entries: Rumor has it that a student has been learning dangerous potion-brewing techniques from an unsavory witch at the Yanari Market. If this horrendous rumor is true, Mr. Basingstoke wants nothing more than to put an end to it.

entries.name: Too Many Basingstokes
entries: A witch claiming to be Mr. Basingstoke is asking for help reinstating him as Arch Doyen of the Witchery after being deposed. The problem is that Mr. Basingstoke has not, in fact, been deposed and is currently in the school leading the faculty. Which of the two Basingstokes is the real one?

entries.name: A Feud Between Witches
entries: A friendly demonstration of magic from two faculty members goes awry, leaving students trapped in bubbles that have started to drift out into the city. Rather than snapping to their students' aid, the two witches from rival covens blame each other and nearly come to blows. Someone must help wrangle the students and calm the tempers of the witches responsible before someone gets hurt.

entries.name: NPCs (Faculty & Staff)
entries: The faculty are all elders or leading witches of the six covens. They are tasked with recruiting the best and brightest from all over Obojima and instructing them in the ways of potion brewing, witchcraft, and First Age magic.

entries.name: Mikari Karabi (female human)
entries: Mikari was once a Rockwinder who led pilgrims to the Ledge of Offering and told them tales of {@creature Jumaga|ObojimaTallGrass} the Sky Salamander. One day, she escorted a member of the Cloud Cap Coven, who recognized her innate magical potential. They struck up a fast friendship, and soon after Mikari began an apprenticeship with the master. Since that time, she has had a desire to pass on the gift of magic to those who show a passion for the art. Mikari's teaching style reflects this, as she often invites her most promising pupils to lead classes on arcane topics where they excel.

entries.name: Wayla Wix (female human)
entries: Originally from Sky Kite Valley, Wayla started off as an apprentice building kite planes when she had an encounter with an elder wind spirit that lived near the shoreline. This experience, in Wayla's words, left her with a special relationship with magic that she could not fully understand at first. So she sought out a witch from the Patchwork Robe Coven, and after many years has gone on to become one of their most powerful spellcasters.
She is a patient instructor, always trying her best to emulate her own mentor. During lectures, she paces around the auditorium, unable to keep still for more than a few seconds.

entries.name: Mochi Hoba (male nakudama)
entries: Ever the explorer, Mochi Hoba was a shoo-in for the Tall Hats and fit right in with their wandering style. Mochi learned the basics of magic from his grandfather, who came from a long line of nakudama mages. Mochi has always liked being the center of attention, and being surrounded by a crowd of eager minds is his happy place. He is known in the Witchery for wearing the tallest hat he possibly can without toppling over. As an instructor, he is gregarious and animated, happily pursuing any tangent if it gives him a chance to impress his students by dropping a name.

entries.name: Fiona Boggs (female elf)
entries: Fiona Boggs usually shuffles around the Witchery carrying some kind of amphibian or reptile that has escaped its terrarium. For a swamp witch, Fiona has a cheery disposition and loves to take her classes out into the field to get covered in mud. She can often be heard saying, "There's magic in the mud!" Her constant companion is Draggle, a crow rumored to be a polymorphed adversary.

entries.name: Andus Ferdle (male human)
entries: Rough around the edges but always wearing a smile, Andus wanders the Witchery in his autumn-toned robes stitched with curling vines and trailing leaves. Small gourd spirits follow him around, sometimes attaching themselves to his coat, and his wide-brimmed hat is always full of seeds and crumbs for birds. Among his magical accomplishments, Andus is, ironically, most well-known for baking the most amazing pies. As a teacher, he is notorious for speaking softly and chuckling to himself, as if at a joke only he can hear. By the end of a lecture, the entire class is commonly huddled together around his lectern, desperate to glean what words they can.

entries.name: Melda Prumple (female human)
entries: Melda Prumple is a tall woman with a regal bearing who feels a keen responsibility to properly represent the most powerful coven in Obojima. She is a descendant of the famous Granny Prumple, author of Granny Prumple's Almanac of Island Ingredients: The How-Tos and What-Fors on the Craft of Potions, in Seven Volumes, a fact she finds hard to keep to herself. Melda is brave and forthright and has, more than once, shooed a {@filter howler|bestiary|source=obojimatallgrass;obojimatalesyatamon|tag=howler} out of the city. She has no patience for what she calls the "fool's hobbies," among them being idleness, excuses, and, worst of all, the inclination to be a chatterbox. You'll find no such nonsense among the students during her lessons.

entries.name: Mr. Basingstoke (human)
entries: The seemingly ageless Mr. Basingstoke has led the Witchery for decades. He belongs to no coven, and his impartiality has garnered the respect of coven witches. He has an imperious air despite being softspoken. Nobody knows his first name or age, though both students and faculty love to speculate on the possibilities. He is always accompanied by Sorrow, his octopus spirit companion.
Nasu: Wisteria Blvd.
{@b Tone - Quirky, Puzzling, Magical}

At the intersection of Wisteria and Vine is the Instaprint Camera Store, a two-story building where an eccentric wizard known as Oculus performs experimental magic with an assortment of First Age objects called Instaprint Cameras. Inside, his shop is part workspace, part study, and part storefront, and it's here that Oculus, over the years of running this business, has perfected his trade.

Before Oculus, Instaprint cameras were rarely used due to the scarcity of the First Age film that the cameras needed. The devices themselves were common enough, but to most people, they were nothing more than a paperweight. This changed ten years ago when Oculus discovered how to reproduce the film using specialty paper and a collection of arcane enchantments of his own design. Now, after a decade of running his shop, Oculus offers a dozen types of film, numerous camera accessories, and a camera repair service.

entries.name: The Rather Strange Story of Filmont Fudd
entries: The Instaprint Camera store was once the home of a human man named Filmont Fudd, a Witchery dropout who enjoyed the workings of magic but could never pass any exams. Over time, he became obsessed with a device he bought one evening at the Yanari Market—an Instaprint camera. It ignited his mind and imagination, throwing him into a frenzied desire to uncover all aspects of the device. He took everything he learned from the Witchery and began his studies.

Most knew Filmont to be an odd duck—there would be weeks when no one would see him come out of his house—neighbors would listen at the door but would only hear him muttering over the sounds of fizzing and crackling energy, occasionally seeing flashes of bright light through the drawn curtains. The baker across the street would leave food outside the door for Filmont, only to find the dishes cleaned and stacked the next morning.

By the time Filmont finally had a breakthrough, he had... changed. His hair had turned stark white, and his odd quirks and mannerisms were now exaggerated to the nth degree, in addition to all the new ones he had picked up. When asked, he said that he had a vision from the ancients of the First Age who showed him how to use these devices, and that from now on, he was to be known as the wizard, Oculus. From that point on, Oculus would steadily release new types of film for Instaprint cameras from his home turned storefront, and after years of selling to people and educating them on the use and application of the camera, he eventually brought this lost device back to life.

entries.name: Types of Film
entries: Enchanted film allows instaprint cameras to do some amazing things. All film created by Oculus develops in 12 seconds at which point the effects of the film become active. Some film is more difficult to produce than others, which is why Oculus sells them in different quantities. In the following table you'll find a list of film types Oculus currently offers at his shop:

entries.name: Standard Film (10 per pack) ........................ 1 GF
entries: Captures a permanent photo of the area, provided there is enough light.

entries.name: Darkvision Film (10 per pack) ...................... 5 GF
entries: Captures a permanent photo of the area, unless it's {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB} by magical Darkness.

entries.name: Revealing Film (5 per pack) ....................... 25 GF
entries: Darkvision Film that reveals {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB} and {@condition Invisible|XPHB} creatures and objects as glowing silhouettes.

entries.name: Tracking Film (3 per pack) .......................... 25 GF
entries: Standard Film that grants the creature holding the photo {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks to track a creature in the photo. This effect lasts for 30 days before reverting to a standard photo.

entries.name: Identifying Film (2 per pack) ..................... 25 GF
entries: Standard Film that, when used to photograph an object, produces a brief description on the back of the photo of what the object is and who owns it.

entries.name: Arcana Film (5 per pack) ............................. 25 GF
entries: Darkvision Film that reveals a faint aura around any visible creature or object in the photo that bears magic.

entries.name: Anti-Illusion Film (5 per pack) ................... 50 GF
entries: Revealing Film that also reveals illusions in the photo with a save DC of 14 or lower.

entries.name: Curse-Binding Film (individually sold) ... 150 GF
entries: Arcana Film that targets one cursed creature or object in the photo with a {@spell Remove Curse} spell. The curse is then bound to the photograph but rendered inert.

entries.name: Memory Film (individually sold) .............. 200 GF
entries: Darkvision Film that, when scribed with the name of a creature and used to photograph an area, produces a description of what that creature did in the area in the past 24 hours, if anything.

entries.name: The Rambling Sage
entries: In the southern part of Yatamon stands the Rambling Sage, a statue of unearthly detail and aliveness that depicts an elderly man who is holding a book in one hand while the other hand points skyward. The man is dressed in elaborate robes and appears to be frozen in mid-stride with a gaze of wonder on his face, hence the name Rambling Sage. Many tell the tale that he was a man of great influence who wandered into town and was petrified by magic too powerful to undo.
Nasu: Parking Structure
"{@b Oh, you'll hear the market long before you see it.}"
items.from: {@b —a common answer when asking for directions.}

entries: {@b Tone - Bustling, Magical, Festive}

Built within the many floors of a First Age parking garage, the Yanari Witches' Market is a sea of color, sounds, and smells amid the noisy clamor of hawkers, buskers, buyers, and sellers. It's the place in Yatamon (and perhaps all of Obojima) to find potion brewers, potion ingredients, and all kinds of arcane tools and trinkets.

During the day, Yanari Market is a friendly and fun gathering place where people wander through rows of market stalls, chatting with vendors and purchasing their treasures. On the top level of the market, food vendors cook their sweet and savory delights that attract hungry residents and visitors from blocks away.

Once the sun sets, spirit-whelmed neon signs flicker to life, and the market takes on a different aspect, one more akin to a festival. On a stage in the corner of the market's fourth floor, musicians entertain the patrons, and "hospitality fires" are lit throughout the outside of the market to warm the crowds on cooler nights. These fiery beacons create small, spontaneous communities as visitors cluster around them, invariably sharing their stories and turning strangers into friends. The market continues like this late into the night, sometimes even until sunrise.

entries.name: The Yanari
entries: Scuttling among the vendors, customers, and gawking visitors are hundreds of small, teddy-bear-sized creatures known as yanari who magically feast on the rumble of the crowd. Attracted to the noise, these tiny spirits have gathered at the market since its inception and are the reason for its name.

At peak market hours, yanari can be found skittering across the market floor, narrowly escaping being trampled underfoot, and crawling along the drainage pipes that weave along the inside and exterior of the market structure. Yanari are generally seen as a nuisance, and though they are better behaved in the market, they still get into trouble. Vendors often find them hiding inside cabinets or pots, overindulging in sound, which acts as an intoxicant for them. It's not uncommon to open up a piece of furniture or a large item, only to find several yanari inside, drunk with ecstasy.
Outside the market is a four-foot-tall statue of a yanari known by the locals as "Yando."

entries.name: Reputation
entries: Throughout Obojima, the Yanari Witches' Market is well known as a place for finding magic and arcane items—especially potions and enchanted First Age objects. Within Yatamon, the market is the top recommendation as "the go-to place" for any visitor to the city, as it showcases all the best that Yatamon has to offer in culture, food, and festivities. However, over the years, Yanari has also drawn a less savory crowd, who use the market as a place to craft deals, sell stolen goods, and make wagers. Although this aspect of the market is mostly unseen, from time to time Yanari's underbelly rears its head.

entries.name: Market Basics
entries: The Yanari Market is located in a four-story parking garage filled with colorful flags, creeping ivy, spirit-whelmed neon signs, and talismans of good fortune. The market is open before sunrise and closes well after sunset, and it seems to be perpetually surrounded by a throng of visitors milling about, eating food, trading items, and admiring their purchases.

The market generally closes several hours after sunset and opens one hour before sunrise, but the times are never exact and depend on the whims of Mistress Clove, the enigmatic spirit who many say runs the Yanari Market.

The parking garage is a square structure about 80 feet tall at its highest point and 75 feet on each side, covering a small portion of a city block. Throughout its open hours, every level is usually packed with people from all over Obojima, jostling about as they move from one stall to the next, making the market the most popular place in Yatamon, and a prime spot for pickpockets, swindlers, and other larcenous lackeys.

entries.name: Why Adventure Here?
entries: The Yanari Witches' Market is a versatile tool in the GM's toolbox. It's filled with magic items, adventure clues, rumors, challenges, and side quests, and is operated and frequented by every type of person imaginable. It serves as an ideal location for the beginning, middle, or end of a quest and can easily connect multiple ongoing storylines. Here are a handful of suggested uses for the location:

entries.name: Quests
entries: People from all over the island travel to Yanari for one reason or another. Whether it's for potions, enchantments, food, or otherwise, they come to the market with a desire in mind. If they can't find their quarry readily available on one of the market levels, they look to the vendors and locals for help, making Yanari a thoroughfare for quests and trade. Speaking with vendors or Mistress Clove is a surefire way to be introduced to a paying patron with a quest.

entries.name: Potions and Ingredients
entries: If one needs a potion, ingredient, or advice on brewing, Yanari is sure to be the place where they'll find their answer. Common and uncommon ingredients from all regions are plentiful in the market, and rare ingredients are just an introduction away. Potions are often brewed on request and served quickly, making Yanari a plentiful resource for any postal knight, merchant, or adventuring party.

entries.name: Gearing Up
entries: Enchantments, magical tools, and arcane trinkets are easy to find on the market's first floor. Local explorers, craftspeople, and farmers frequent this level for spells and wares to aid them in their line of work. Others come to sell their goods or make trades, which means new stock is constantly flowing through the stalls.

entries.name: Competition
entries: Brewing competitions, cook-offs, musical battles, and ingredient hunts are all common occurrences in the market. Most are small, light-hearted skirmishes between friends or rivals, while others are larger-scale tournaments involving multiple challengers and a hefty prize. No matter the scale, the market serves as a lively platform for competition.

entries.name: Information
entries: Yanari is home to a wide cast of characters with a slew of valuable knowledge, crucial lore, or key clues that might help an adventuring party.

entries.name: Guest of Honor
entries: A celebrity witch, famed adventurer, master chef, or renowned performer may also show up at the market to dazzle the crowd with a demonstration of their talent or to captivate patrons with their stories. Because of this, the market attracts serious scholars, adventurers, and admirers from all over Obojima who hope to see one of these masters practice their craft.

entries.name: Nefarious Things
entries: Generally, Yanari feels like a giant, upbeat party. However, hidden within the crowds, the market has a seedy underbelly that operates beneath the hustle and bustle, where less than savory people are dealing in all manner of foul and dangerous things. Cursed items, sealed demons, and stolen goods are all traded behind stalls, in darkened corners, and under tables within the Yanari Market.

entries.name: Corruption
entries: Although most people don't know what the Corruption is, vials of the substance, corrupted ingredients, and sickly animals stricken by the negative effects of the Corruption have already started making their way into the market. A majority of it is coming from the Yanaris' seedy underbelly, but some is unknowingly brought in by merchants and ingredient collectors.

entries.name: Market Levels & Stalls
entries: The Yanari Market has four levels, the fourth being the top of the parking garage—an openair space where each stall is covered by a colorful tent, the shell of a wagon, or some other creatively modified vehicle. The interior levels all feature tall ceilings lined with metal conduits and drainage pipes, which are used to hang decorations and serve as highways for the yanari that skitter about the market.

There are over a hundred stalls, each with its own schedule. Some vendors show up every other day, some are gone for weeks at a time, and some are only open once or twice a month, taking the rest of the time to replenish their stock. Lines for vendors such as these are long and form early.

Each stall is a riot of self-expression. Some are neat and orderly, while others are a fascinating kaleidoscope of chaos. As a matter of courtesy, vendors try to keep their wares from spilling out into the alleys and pathways between the stalls, but as space is so limited, market-goers often find themselves stepping over, around, and through stacks of various goods.

entries.name: The Yanari Whisperer
entries: Mistress Clove, the reclusive spirit who started the market and tamed the yanari, has been quietly running the event from a distance for the last fifty years. As the story goes, she began the market alongside a handful of spirits after moving to Yatamon from the Spirit Realm. As the number of patrons grew, so did the number of vendors, and in time, the popular market began to take shape as something truly special.

Unfortunately, the market's success brought on a new challenge: the pest spirits known as yanari. Drawn by the crowd, the yanari wreaked havoc on the market, and soon after, its popularity began to falter. Many vendors tried to drive the pest spirits away, but none were successful, and the market suffered as a result—that is, until Mistress Clove did the impossible and charmed the chaotic creatures.

Rumor has it that she struck a deal with Tamh Gon to model a charm after his enchanted chimes. Whether that is true or not, the Mistress somehow crafted a bell to pacify the yanari and return the market to its former glory. Since that day, she has stepped away from vending and instead taken on the role of the market's caretaker.

entries.name: Enchantment Alley
entries: Following lanterns, self-stirring pots, fortune charms, magical jackets, and all manner of arcane trinkets are waiting to be discovered amid the myriad stalls of Enchantment Alley. Each stall has its own theme, a specifically curated selection of items and objects, and a merchant with eccentricities to match their wares. Besides the useful items for sale on this level, you'll also find witches and mages alike who offer their services as enchanters. Whether you'd like a specialty item made for you, need maintenance on an item you already have, or desire the removal of an enchantment, the vendors on level one are sure to be helpful.

entries.name: Scribes Pillar
entries: Many years ago, an incident on the first level of Yanari destroyed one of the building's support pillars. As the story goes, a noble book vendor, fearing the building might collapse, took action and sacrificed his collection of tomes to rebuild the structure. By stacking every novel, storybook, and manuscript he had, the vendor filled the space and bound the books to the stone with enchantments of his own design. Today, the Scribes Pillar stands as a testament to the power of enchantments and serves as a shrine to honor the sacrifice of the vendor who saved the market.

entries.name: A Cursed Clearance Sale
entries: Rumors are spreading that Mr. Lusk's cursed items have started behaving erratically—someone said that a demon's ring teleported into his pocket, and another said that a cursed spoon was following her. Many are beginning to think Mr. Lusk is in control, but others think that something more sinister is at work.

entries.name: A Mysterious Bookseller
entries: Not too long ago, a shadowy figure pushing an ornately carved wooden cart passed through the crowd at the market. On the cart were stacks of old books— some dusty and smelling of mildew, while others were charred with a smoky scent. Most people found nothing of interest, but the few who did purchase from the vendor haven't been seen since.
