Some of the other vendors are worried about their regulars not showing up to the market and have offered some of their goods in exchange for the safe return of the missing patrons.

entries.name: Noteworthy Vendors
entries: Below is a list of examples of stalls one will find on the first level of the Yanari Market.

items.name: Mr. Lusk - Cursed Curios
entries: Tucked away in the back of Enchantment Alley is Cursed Curios and its proprietor, the gaunt nakudama, Granthias Lusk. Mr. Lusk is a dealer who specializes in cursed items, and during business hours, he doesn't leave his collection for fear of such power being left unattended. Though he does, on occasion, sell one of his cursed objects, he primarily deals in curse identification and removal. His stall is an ornate kiosk made from carved and blackened wood edged with silver. A canopy of deep violet silk stretches overhead, and lanterns whelmed with blue fire spirits glow balefully over the merchandise.

items.name: Keiko Vex - Hex Marks the Spot
entries: Hex Marks the Spot is the hangout location for rebellious young spellcasters. The proprietor, Keiko Vex, is an effortlessly stylish and smolderingly charismatic human, known for their relaxed vibe. Hex Marks the Spot is covered by a sleek, black awning embroidered with sigils. The interior is lit with First Age neon that dramatically lights the enchanted items and Keiko's winning smile as they introduce their customers to cutting-edge witchery.

items.name: Lousia P. Lipkin - Lipkin's Little Luxuries
entries: Sandwiched between larger vendors, Lipkin's Little Luxuries is a charming boutique that has more than its fair share of interesting and useful trinkets. The shop's neatly arranged wooden shelves and glass cases display a variety of mildly enchanted items—teacups that keep their tea at the perfect temperature, scarves that instantly transform to accentuate an outfit, and a pen that always writes in elegant script (and never misspells a word). Lousia is a plump and cheerful human who always has insightful recommendations for her customers.

entries.name: Torm Miscle - Wondrous Earth
entries: In a wood-frame stall made from thick beams and creamtoned canvas walls is the human proprietor of Wondrous Earth, Torm Miscle, a stout, bearded man with hands that have spent decades in the earth. Displays of glittering gems and minerals are lit by amber beams of light cast from several hanging lanterns. Most of the items that Torm has for sale are naturally enchanted by the magic of Obojima itself, but there are some that have been enchanted by practitioners of the arcane arts. Torm doesn't speak much, so he lets the items sell themselves, which he has tastefully arranged on rich, warm slabs of oak.

items.name: Monseigneur Jacques Opar - Le Chapeau
entries: Perhaps the most famous vendor in Enchantment Alley is the distinguished and impeccably dressed Monseigneur Jacques Opar, a wizard turned milliner who now creates some of the most sought-after witch hats in Yatamon. Le Chapeau is an opulent pavilion of deep blue and gold, draped with silk banners and arcane symbols. Mirrors of various sizes and shapes line the walls, along with pedestals of polished ebony that display his finest wares. Though the stall sells hats of all types, it is mostly known for Monseigneur's stylish take on the iconic wide-brimmed witch's hat.

entries.name: Level 2
entries: The second level of the Yanari Witches' Market has perhaps the largest collection of First Age items in all of Obojima. For that reason alone, it is frequented by AHA historians, scholars from the Witchery, and curious enthusiasts who find this level of the market a fascinating glimpse into the mysterious past of Obojima.

entries.name: Tape Research
entries: AHA believes there is a series of VHS tapes that contain recorded messages by nakudama during the historic period when they ruled over Obojima, otherwise known as the Age of Nakudama. Researchers are trying to find these "lillypad tapes," which are mentioned several times across other written accounts of this period, but have yet to uncover any of them.

entries.name: Milla Pavlova (female elf)
entries: Milla is an AHA archaeologist whose research has led her on an expedition to find a rare First Age item—a fortune-telling machine said to contain a spirit wise beyond its years. She believes this entity, which appears to thrive on coins or paper tickets, is a potential treasure trove of information about First Age culture.

entries.name: Narvy Newman (male human)
entries: Narvy is obsessed with First Age technology and has amassed a fair amount of knowledge about it. Narvy loves to flaunt his memory of lore and share lists of random factoids about all kinds of items. If anyone shows a shred of interest, Narvy follows them around, regurgitating endless facts, the validity of which is unconfirmed.

entries.name: Zeb Skint (male nakudama)
entries: Zeb is a scam artist and counterfeiter who is trying to pass off fake flowers and petals (the money, not the flora), along with facsimiles of First Age items to visiting yokels from outside Yatamon. He's a fast talker who can spot a wide-eyed out-of-towner. He doesn't have a stall at the market, so he instead will bump into his target, forcing an "accidental" introduction.

entries.name: Dying for Art
entries: Ronnie Yan can be found all over Yatamon shooting his movies, but for his new feature, he wants more action. Ronnie would love to document your adventures, especially if you're heading into the Gale Fields or the Brackwater Wetlands—the more dangerous, the better! He's broke and needs funding, but he thinks a real adventure thriller will sell tickets like hotcakes.

entries.name: Noteworthy Vendors
entries: Below is a list of examples of stalls one will find on the second level of the Yanari Market.

items.name: Luanda Tipps - Tipps' Tailoring
entries: If you want authentic First Age garments, then Tipps' Tailoring is the place to go. Luanda, a skilled elven tailor and active member of AHA, has been repairing historic articles of clothing for half a decade. Her team of explorers scours the unused buildings in Yatamon, bringing back all manner of goods for her to repair and sell in her shop. And although her quaint setup and friendly demeanor are disarming, Luanda is a hard negotiator and charges a high price for her clothing.

items.name: Ronnie Yan - In the Can!
entries: Ronnie is a bard who buys and sells VHS and cassette tapes. Some are sold as is, to be used for entertainment, while others are enchanted by Ronnie as one-time-use spell storage. If you're looking to sell, Ronnie is always interested in blank VHS, as the bard is also one of the few people alive to have an operational camcorder. In fact, his true passion is being a movie director, and when he's not at the market, he is filming movies in secret locations all over Yatamon.

items.name: Kiba Don - First Age Furnishings
entries: First Age Furnishings and its new owner, Kiba, deal in a variety of goods from magazines to baseball bats—but they primarily sell and trade First Age furniture and home accessories. Those looking to complete a furniture set or fill their home after moving to Yatamon will often find themselves at Kiba's establishment for one reason or another. The stall's popularity has only grown since Kiba took over the business. In addition to his charm and skill as a salesman, Kiba has also garnered a reputation for his generosity after he started giving away inventory to people in need.

entries.name: Maggie Swan - First Age Cooking
entries: Maggie, a middle-aged mother of four, spends her time, alongside her gaggle of children, searching through First Age sites for high-quality cookware. Pots and pans are usually in high demand, but Maggie gathers everything from teaspoons to cheesecloth. When she can, she'll take some of her best finds and have them enchanted by the youth at the Witchery, as she wishes to encourage young students. First Age Cooking is only open on rare occasions, as cookware can be hard to come by, and it also fetches a handsome price at the market.

items.name: Rina Dee - Mystic Vision
entries: Rina is a sorcerer who deals in radios and televisions. She specializes in magic that allows her to temporarily and permanently power First Age machines and offers such skills as a service in her stall. Beyond her skills as a magical practitioner, Rina is also a well-studied tinkerer and is fascinated with "First Age transmissions"—auditory messages and music that you can occasionally hear from a functioning radio. Rina has yet to find a connection, magical or otherwise, that can trace where these transmissions are coming from and denies AHA's consensus that the messages are just memory magic.

entries.name: Level 3
entries: The third level of the Yanari Witches' Market is where the potion brewers have all set up their stalls and is undoubtedly the most famous level, as it is how the market began—a place where spirits and potion brewers gather to practice their skills, swap knowledge, barter ingredients, and compete for bragging rights. Over time, these gatherings became more and more of an event, and other vendors and arcane dabblers began to sell their wares, until it became the festive spectacle it is today.

entries.name: Market Vendors
entries: Although there are places such as the Witchery that are renowned for academic excellence in potion brewing and the arcane arts, the vendors of the Yanari Market tend to be more on the cutting edge of the craft—often ex-coven members called cauldroners with a love for potions and the arcane.

These cauldroners are an assortment of rules-breaking rebels, obsessive specialists, and eccentric savants, many of whom have garnered reputations that give them celebrity status as masters of their particular facet of "the Art."

To have a stall at the Yanari Market means that you are contributing something special to the craft, and to most folks, it is a badge of honor to say that you are a Yanari vendor— especially if you are among the colorful cast of skilled potion brewers. But this can have the opposite effect on members of academic schools such as the Witchery, who tend to look down on Yanari vendors as reckless and undisciplined. These two different approaches to potion brewing have created a contentious rivalry between the Witchery and the Yanari Witches' Market.

entries.name: Brew Battle
entries: The rivalry between members of the Witchery and vendors at Yanari market often leads to trash talk, over-the-top showmanship, and, on occasion, a Brew Battle. When insults or flashy skills aren't enough to settle an argument between members of the two groups, sometimes a challenge of skill is issued. These contests often entail seeing who can brew the most potions or the best potions, or who can concoct the most innovative potion. Whoever wins one of these contests earns considerable bragging rights throughout the arcane community in Yatamon— and possibly even outside the city as well.

entries.name: Mistress Clove's Cauldron
entries: This large, iron cauldron, draped with good fortune banners and talismans, has been here since the market's inception and is presumed to belong to Mistress Clove. Market-goers and vendors fill the cauldron with coins, good luck charms, and other small items of value, all of which are given back out to the community once the cauldron fills. This event, when it happens, is called the "Cauldron Pour," and it's one of the few festivals unique to Yanari. It represents the community's support for each other and happens several times a year.

entries.name: Grikko (yanari spirit)
entries: This yanari is notorious for compulsively drinking potions and then either experiencing an ecstatic trance, uncontrollable vomiting, or some bizarre magical effect. All the vendors on this level know about Grikko and warily keep an eye out for its thieving antics, but Grikko is crafty, sneaky, and highly motivated to satisfy its potion-guzzling lust.

entries.name: Signature Flair
entries: In their efforts to express individuality, skill, and perhaps a sense of humor, potion brewers have devised arcane ways to add a signature flair to their creations. When you open one of these potions, its particular personality will make itself known in a subtle or spectacular way.

entries.name: Noteworthy Vendors
entries: Below is a list of examples of stalls one will find on the third level of the Yanari Market.

items.title: {@font AMONG OTHER BREWERS, SEBASTIAN IS KNOWN AS THE POTION COBBLER|Obojima}

items.name: Sebastian Zog - The Bubbling Cauldron
entries: Following the teachings and ethos of the craftsman, Sebastian is a cobbler, brewing pieces and parts of other items to create his own distinct potions. Growing up the son of a merchant who ran a flea market in Yatamon, Sebastian always found himself surrounded by all kinds of trinkets, oddities, and scrap. So, when he decided to apprentice under a cauldroner, his wellhoned talent for rummaging took his potion brewing to the next level, and he began to create his own unique brand of brewing. Harkening back to his roots, Sebastian's stall in the Yanari Market, The Bubbling Cauldron, is a delightful mess of stacked crates, hanging charms, and bubbling vials. Patchwork banners and awnings made from old sails, festival flags, and embroidered shawls drape overhead and partition the stall.

items.name: Baba Vara - The Grotto
entries: Baba Vara is legendary within the League of the Gilded Gourd. Even as an apprentice witch, her knowledge of and affinity for plants were unusual for someone so young. Some potion brewers in the Yanari Market claim she is a plant spirit masquerading as a human, citing her uncanny knowledge of the island's flora and their unique properties. Her stall is less of a shop and more of a living thing—its wooden frame is covered in moss and mushrooms, with an awning made of twisting vines. The interior is filled with medicinal plants, and Baba Vara cultivates a crawling ivy that fetches items and potions for her. All her potent brews hang from the ceiling in colored glass bottles and vials, illuminated by glowing fungi and clusters of fireflies.

items.title: {@font THE CAULDRON HENRIK STANDS ON TO TALK TO CUSTOMERS IS MORE EXPENSIVE THAN A FIRST AGE CAR.|Obojima}

items.name: Henrik Villum- The Black Fen
entries: As an ex-member of the Crowsworn coven, Henrik Villum is familiar with all things that crawl and squirm within the bogs and fens of the Brackwater Wetlands. Many monsters have magical power trapped within their scales, claws, and bones—a dangerous area of study that Henrik is known for across Yatamon. Recently, however, Henrik has gone through a transformation that has diminished his normally highly regarded reputation. For reasons unknown, Henrik has been cursed by a potent magic he doesn't wish to speak of. This magic has transformed his appearance from his normal 67-year-old self to that of a 12-year-old.

Now, Henrik struggles to be taken seriously by the other cauldroners as he continues to do business through his stall, the Black Fen, a shadowy den of stitched hides, bleached skulls, and dangling bones that once punctuated his dark demeanor and now highlight the silliness of his circumstance.

items.title: {@font HOTSUI LOVES THE TASTE OF FROG SPIRITS.|Obojima}

items.name: Hotsui - Hotsui's Flashbrews
entries: As a quiet wanderer, Hotsui has always shocked those around him with his fastpaced style of potion craft. He is known to think fast, combining seemingly random ingredients when he brews—a talent that has made him famous in the Yanari Market for the sheer quantity of potions he can generate in a day. Despite this raw talent, there are those who (perhaps envious of his fame) say his brews lack depth and thoughtfulness. Despite this, no one can argue with Hotsui's popularity, as customers regularly line up whenever his mobile stall is at the market. Hotsui's stall is a wheeled wagon-turned-apothecary that is lacquered in reds, greens, yellows, and gold and covered in potion flasks, pouches of ingredients, and drying herbs. The old stall bears evidence of scorch marks and charring from the occasional mishap or explosion that Hotsui has come to be known for. Folding counters open from the sides of the cart to display a jumble of mismatched bottles, each one fizzing, sputtering, or smoking as Hotsui demonstrates his frenetic "flashbrew" techniques to the crowd.

items.name: Lady Umishi - The Warp & Weft
entries: Rumor has it that when Lady Umishi was an apprentice witch, she sought out an elder spirit high on Mount Arbora. In that meeting, it is said she traded her sight for the blessings of the spirit. Since that day, she has claimed to see "threads of magic" with her mind's eye, and by connecting the threads, Lady Umishi can "weave" potions. This mystic approach to brewing has given Lady Umishi a mesmerizing and somewhat Intimidating presence, which she admittedly loves. Her stall, the Warp and Weft, is a tranquil oasis amid the Yanari Market's bustle and chaos—a circular pavilion draped in lavish silks embroidered with arcane sigils and filled with the exotic scents of rare herbs, spices, and resins. Despite her blindness, Lady Umishi moves with uncanny precision, her hands tracing patterns in the air as she weaves magic into her brews— all of which are delicate, complex, and perhaps impossible to replicate.

entries.title: {@font THOUGH HER SIGHT IS GONE, HER VISION IS CRYSTAL CLEAR.|Obojima}

items.name: Hallie Alamilla - Feather & Fur
entries: Despite her youth and childlike exuberance, Hallie has a wealth of knowledge when it comes to the magical properties of animals. From fur to feathers, she knows exactly which combinations make the best potions. Many assume her seemingly effortless skill means her talent comes naturally, but professional brewers recognize the hard work and careful study behind her craft. That dedication has earned Hallie their respect within Yanari Market and a unique, yet important role within the Patchwork Coven. Feather and Fur is a lively, colorful stall filled with boxes, perches, and burrows where a wide array of creatures make their homes. Being a sprightly young witch, Hallie enjoys teaching her customers about the animals and strange creatures as much as she does making potions. Feather and Fur is as much a potion shop as it is a petting zoo.

entries.name: Restaurant Level
entries: Level four of the Yanari Market is a sea of mobile kitchen stalls and communal tables, along with mouthwatering smells of spiced meats, savory soups, and scrumptious pastries. The restaurant level is open to the air, so during the day, there's a picnic atmosphere, and customers are often delighted by the occasional school of flying fish as they float by. After dark, bards and storytellers often entertain the customers in a night of stargazing, music, and rambunctious tales, while vendors serve up hearty meals and fine alcohols.

entries.name: Noteworthy Vendors
entries: This is a list of examples of stalls one will find on the fourth level of the Yanari Market.

items.name: Chef Marvi Okahiro - Open Fire!
entries: Chef Marvi Okahiro, a former evocation mage, has taken his spellcasting prowess and turned it into culinary magic with his floating iron griddle cart, Open Fire!
At Open Fire!, everything is charbroiled to perfection, and Chef Marvi's fire-proof kitchen practically roars with fireballs, fire bolts, and fire storms. His specialty? Spell cooked skewers

items.name: Bippo & Dappo - Naku-Pops
entries: Run by the brothers Bippo and Dappo, Naku-Pops sells an ice-cold First Age treat with a twist! Their colorful cart houses a spirit-powered washing machine, which, due to the {@creature snowball spirits|ObojimaTalesYatamon}{@sup °} the brothers bound to the machine, now slowly tumbles and freezes cans of soda, making a slushie-like beverage the market obsesses over. You'll often find only one brother running the shop at a time, as the other is likely hunting for cans of soda.

items.name: Jongo - Château de Jongo
entries: There's one stall that looks like a miniature, quaint house with ornately decorated windows and a dramatic silhouette that is strangely empty, and that belongs to the legendary Jongo, a wandering chef and renowned food artist. Everyone who goes to the market hopes that they pick the day when Jongo returns, as he famously comes with gifts, stories, and new recipes that he makes for the adoring crowd.

items.name: Tulip Haddingway - Dumpling Boy
entries: Run by the newly appointed chef Tulip Haddingway, Dumpling Boy has been a staple on the fourth level of the market for over a decade. The beloved food stall was previously owned and run by Tulip's older brother before he passed away last summer. Since then, Tulip has worked tirelessly to learn the craft of dumplings and carry on her brother's legacy.

items.name: Chef Maki - Nom Nom Noodles
entries: The Nom Nom Noodles food cart is shaped like a giant noodle bowl tipped sideways and features two giant shrimp-shaped cutouts that float over the bowl and wiggle on occasion. Inside the circular kitchen are Chef Maki (who is known locally as the Noodle Witch) and her assistant, Bull Dara (male dara), who both work seamlessly as a team to serve up Nami's Famous Noodle Soup, which the cart gets its name from.

entries.name: The Dawn Petal Guild
entries: Even though the coins minted by the Dawn Petal Guild are used all over Obojima, the druids and the inner workings of the guild are shrouded in mystery. Whether it is to protect the secret of minting the coins or for some other reason, the gates of the Dawn Petal Monastery are kept closed, and visitors are not allowed within the walls. Only on rare occasions are the druids seen outside the monastery—the main occasion being the annual Dawn Blossom festival, where the druids act as officiants for the grand ceremony.

entries.name: About Vehicles in the World
entries: First Age vehicles can be found across the island but are most abundant in Yatamon. The average citizen's vehicle of choice is the bicycle—thanks to the ease with which craftspeople can make reproductions—though vespas, motorcycles, trucks, and cars are still common enough. While procuring and learning to use a First Age vehicle (such as a car) are challenges in their own right, the greatest hurdle for most lies in getting it operational. It's no small task and often requires several talented individuals who are both mechanically and magically gifted.

entries.name: Operating Vehicles
entries: Though there are many unique aspects to the different types of vehicles, there is a general set of rules that apply when driving any of them. Vehicle properties, which are listed later in this section, allow certain vehicles to ignore or alter some of the rules detailed in this section.

entries.name: Driving & Riding in a Vehicle
entries: All vehicles have a Crew, which is the number of creatures required to operate the vehicle. Each type of vehicle also has a maximum number of Passengers, which is the number of other Small and Medium creatures that can be transported by the vehicle at a time, in addition to its Crew.

entries.name: Mounting or Entering a Vehicle
entries: During your move, you can enter, exit, mount, or dismount a vehicle by spending an amount of movement equal to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} (round down). You can't enter or mount a vehicle if it already has its maximum number of Crew and Passengers within or on it. You also can't enter a vehicle if it has the Flipped or Locked condition (see Vehicle Conditions).

entries.name: Controlling a Vehicle
entries: If you wish to serve as a member of a vehicle's Crew, you must have at least one free hand, and you must take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to operate the vehicle on each of your turns. If the vehicle must first be powered on, you can do so as part of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you take to begin operating it. You can also power off such a vehicle at any point on your turn (no action required).
In order for two creatures to exchange control of a vehicle, one must take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action and the other must simultaneously take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to change places.

entries.name: Vehicle Movement
entries: Vehicles have two kinds of speeds: a Combat Speed for shorter-distance movement (measured in feet per round) and a Travel Speed for long-distance, out-of-combat movement (measured in miles per hour). While you're serving as a member of a vehicle's Crew or are a vehicle's Passenger, you ignore your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, instead moving with the vehicle as it moves.
A vehicle can never move more than its maximum Combat Speed in a round, regardless of whether another creature takes control of it.

If you're the sole member of a vehicle's Crew in combat, you spend its movement as you would typically spend your own movement, controlling where the vehicle moves on each of your turns; you can't take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action while controlling a vehicle to gain extra movement for the current turn. If a vehicle requires a Crew of more than one creature, one of those creatures must be designated to control the vehicle's movement.

entries.name: Running into Other Targets
entries: A vehicle's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved when it hits a creature or object that is smaller than it. It instead completely stops if the creature or object it hits is the same size as the vehicle or larger, or if the target is otherwise unable to be moved.

entries.name: Changing Direction
entries: Sharply turning a vehicle or reversing its direction during combat requires additional caution and effort. To do so, the creature controlling the vehicle must spend an amount of the vehicle's movement equal to half its Combat Speed (round down).

entries.name: Performing Complex Maneuvers
entries: If the creature controlling the vehicle wishes to perform a complex maneuver, it can make a Maneuvering check. To make this ability check, the creature rolls {@dice 1d20} plus its Dexterity or Intelligence modifier (its choice) and the vehicle's Size Modifier.

entries.name: Cargo & Towing
entries: All vehicles have a Cargo Capacity, which is the amount of weight the vehicle can carry. Cargo ignores the weight of the vehicle's Crew and Passengers, only factoring in the weight of any objects inside or on top of the vehicle that aren't otherwise being worn by a creature.

A vehicle can also tow or drag an additional amount of weight up to its Cargo Capacity. If a vehicle is carrying no cargo, it can therefore tow a total amount of weight up to twice its Cargo Capacity.

entries.name: Vehicles in Combat
entries: Vehicles use the following special rules in combat.

entries.name: Vehicle Armor Class & Hit Points
entries: Refer to the {@table Vehicles Table|ObojimaTalesYatamon} for each vehicle's AC and {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum. A vehicle is destroyed when it has 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Targeting a Vehicle
entries: Vehicles can be attacked like any other object. Spells and other effects that target creatures (such as the {@spell Fireball|XPHB} spell) can also target vehicles.

entries.name: Damaging a Vehicle
entries: Vehicles have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and Psychic damage. They also have a damage threshold, as shown in the {@table Vehicles Table|ObojimaTalesYatamon}.

entries.name: Massive Damage
entries: If a vehicle takes damage that equals or exceeds half its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum (round down) from a single attack or effect, it gains the {@condition Flipped|ObojimaTalesYatamon} condition (see Vehicle Conditions).

entries.name: Damage Threshold
entries: A creature or an object that has a damage threshold has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to all damage unless it takes an amount of damage from a single attack or effect equal to or greater than its damage threshold, in which case it takes that entire instance of damage. Any damage that fails to meet or exceed the damage threshold is superficial and doesn't reduce {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Saving Throws
entries: Vehicles always fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws, and they are immune to effects that require other saves as well as conditions that aren't detailed in the Vehicle Conditions section.
The Crew and Passengers of a Piloted vehicle automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws against effects that target them, but they take only half damage from such effects.

entries.name: Going Prone on a Mounted Vehicle
entries: If a creature on a Mounted vehicle gains the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, it can stay mounted on the vehicle, but the vehicle immediately stops and can't move until it is righted. While {@condition Prone|XPHB} on a vehicle, the creature can't crawl, and it spends an amount of the vehicle's movement equal to half its Combat Speed to end that condition, rather than spending its own movement.

entries.name: Ramming
entries: A creature controlling a vehicle can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to attempt to ram a target with the vehicle; this can't be attempted more than once per turn. If the target is a creature, it can make a Dexterity saving throw to avoid the vehicle; the DC for the save equals 8 plus the controlling creature's Dexterity or Intelligence modifier (its choice) and the vehicle's Size Modifier.

If the vehicle moved at least 10 feet in a straight line immediately before successfully ramming a target, the target takes an amount of Bludgeoning damage based on the vehicle's Size Modifier: {@damage 1d6} (Size 1), {@damage 2d6} (Size 2), {@damage 3d6} (Size 3), {@damage 4d6} (Size 4), {@damage 5d6} (Size 5), or {@damage 6d6} (Size 6). The target takes twice as much damage if the vehicle moved at least 20 feet before ramming it, or three times as much damage if the vehicle moved 30 feet or more before ramming it.

Immediately after the vehicle rams a Small or larger target, the vehicle's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced (as detailed in the Controlling a Vehicle section), and the vehicle takes {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it moved before ramming its target, to a maximum of {@damage 3d6}. This damage ignores the vehicle's damage threshold.

entries.name: Vehicle Conditions
entries: Vehicles can be subjected to the following conditions.

entries.name: Repairing a Vehicle
entries: Repairs to a damaged vehicle can be made while the vehicle is in a repair shop. Repairing 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} of damage requires 8 hours of work and costs 10 GF for materials and labor. Alternatively, a creature can repair a vehicle by making an Intelligence ({@skill Mechanics|ObojimaTallGrass}) check using {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB} over the course of 8 hours, which costs 5 GF for materials. Doing so repairs a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the result of the check –10 (minimum of 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}).

entries.name: Spirit-Whelmed Vehicles
entries: If a vehicle is operational, a spirit can whelm it, disappearing into the vehicle and powering it. To do so, the spirit must take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action while touching the vehicle. Additionally, the spirit's {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} must be equal to or greater than the vehicle's Size Modifier or the vehicle fails to power on. If multiple spirits attempt to whelm a vehicle, their combined CR must be equal to or greater than the vehicle's Size Modifier in order to power it; spirits with a CR of less than 1 count as CR 1/2 for the purpose of calculating their combined CR.

While whelming a vehicle, a spirit must take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to power the vehicle on each of its turns, and it ignores its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, instead moving with the vehicle as it moves. The spirit can see and use its other senses as if it were at the front of the vehicle. On the spirit's turn, it can choose to stop whelming the vehicle (no action required), exiting it and reappearing in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of it.

If the vehicle takes damage equal to or greater than the spirit's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum, or if the vehicle is destroyed, the spirit is shunted out of the vehicle, ending its whelm early.

entries.name: Spirits Controlling Vehicles
entries: If a spirit that is whelming a vehicle has an Intelligence of 7 or higher, it can control the vehicle as if it were a member of the vehicle's Crew (see Controlling a Vehicle). If a spirit is controlling a vehicle when the vehicle takes damage, it must make a Constitution saving throw to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}. The DC equals 10 or half the damage taken by the vehicle (round down), whichever number is higher, up to a maximum DC of 30. On a failed save, the spirit's whelm ends early.

A spirit that is whelming a vehicle that is already being operated can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to wrestle for its control (provided the spirit can normally power it). The creature currently operating the vehicle must make a Dexterity saving throw, or an Intelligence saving throw if it's whelming the vehicle. The DC for the save equals 10 + the CR of the intruding spirit. On a failed save, the intruding spirit takes control.

entries.name: Vehicle Classifications
entries: A vehicle's classification expresses how a character is situated in or on the vehicle while operating or riding in it. This classification determines how certain mechanics affect the vehicle as well as its Crew and Passengers.

items.name: Mounted
items.entry: The vehicle has no entry point and is straddled rather than entered.

items.name: Piloted
items.entry: The vehicle requires a creature to enter it in order to operate it. Creatures inside this vehicle have {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover}.

entries.name: Aquatic
entries: This vehicle can only move in the water.

entries.name: Encased
entries: This vehicle is completely closed off from the surrounding environment. Creatures inside it are {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB} and have {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} from creatures outside it.

entries.name: Feather
entries: This vehicle can't deal damage when it rams a target.

entries.name: Flying
entries: This vehicle can only move through the air.

entries.name: Nimble
entries: The creature controlling this vehicle doesn't need to spend any of the vehicle's movement to change its direction.

entries.name: Pedalled
entries: The creature controlling this vehicle can take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action to gain extra movement for the current turn.

entries.name: Simple
entries: This vehicle doesn't require the creature controlling it to take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on each of its turns; it still has the {@condition Uncontrolled|ObojimaTalesYatamon} condition if the creature controlling it has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. If the vehicle must be powered on in order to begin operating it, it still requires a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to do so.

entries.name: Wide
entries: When ramming a creature using this vehicle, each creature within 5 feet of the target must also make the Dexterity saving throw.

entries.title: {@font THE STEEL THAT FORMS THE POINTUE IS SAID TO BE TOUGHER THAN THE HARDENED BODY OF A SLAGGER|Obojima}

entries.name: Gojiki
entries: In Yatamon, there is a beautifully carved and painted wood statue of Gojiki, a companion spirit that saved 20 people from a burning building over one hundred years ago. In honoring the memory of Gojiki, open flames, incense, and smoking around the statue are forbidden and residents of Yatamon will politely inform visitors should they unknowingly violate this act of respect. The statue is surrounded by ginger biscuits wrapped in colorful paper (Gojiki's favorite snacks) that people leave for it, and passersby pet the statue for good luck, which requires a fresh coat of paint every year or so.

entries.name: Pouncing Fighting Style Feat
entries: The Pouncing Fighting Style is a feat option only made available to the Neko Duelist Fighter

entries.name: Spells
entries: This section lists new spells created in or commonly used by the people of Yatamon and its factions—including a variety of spells inspired by the First Age city and its original creators.

entries.name: Backgrounds
entries: There are many backgrounds unique to Obojima—several of which are associated with one of the island's largest factions, such as the Courier Brigade and Witch Covens. Although these backgrounds are popular in the city of Yatamon, they aren't listed below, as they already appear in {@i {@book Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass|ObojimaTallGrass}}. The backgrounds featured in this book aren't inherently unique to the city of Yatamon, but they are common among its people.
As always, feel free to use the backgrounds found in other books, and consider how they might fit into the setting.

entries.name: Magic Items
entries: In the world of Obojima, and especially Yatamon, magic items are abundant, diverse, and highly sought after—each possessing unique powers and abilities. This section lists the new magic items that can be found in Yatamon. The magic items are listed alphabetically.

entries.name: The Gap and its History in Yatamon
entries: Many rumors and myths exist about the origins of the Gap. Some scrolls say it was a place where demons were exiled into the Physical Realm, which turned the city into a haven of dangerous monsters. Others claim that demons created the Gap as a way to get back into the Spirit Realm. But whatever the origins, many legends speak of a great serpent or dragon that devoured all the demons in Yatamon, making it habitable for other peoples. Over time, the Gap became a simple portal through which spirits entered the Physical Realm.

entries.name: Disposition System
entries: The Disposition System serves as a mechanical representation of a creature's emotional mindset and manifest as a series of {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} given to the creature's stat block. Dispositions can bring a level of depth and nuance to a combat encounter, especially to a creature that an adventuring party has already faced.

entries.name: Assigning a Disposition
entries: In addition to a creature's regular stat block, you might also find one or more Disposition tables.

Each table offers a special list of {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} (called "Impulsive Reactions") the creature can take during combat, which are indicative of the emotions or motivations the Disposition represents.
For example, if a bear is awakened while sleeping, you might choose to give it the Skittish Disposition.
It's important to note that, even though a Disposition is meant to offer a mixture of roleplay and mechanics, it can affect the Challenge Rating of a creature.

entries.name: Hit Point Thresholds
entries: Hit Point Thresholds represent a moment in combat when the creature makes a snap decision based on how it's feeling.
When a creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} are reduced to or below a specific Threshold, it gains access to one of the Impulsive Reactions from its Disposition table.
For example, the moment the bear drops to 25 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it triggers its Impulsive Reaction, which allows it to move up to 40 feet away from the creature that attacked it.

When a Threshold is reached, an Impulsive Reaction is triggered, and the creature must use the Impulsive Reaction by taking its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, if available. If the creature's {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} is not available, it loses its opportunity to use that Impulsive Reaction. Once a Hit Point Threshold has been reached, that Impulsive Reaction can't be triggered again (whether it was used or not) until the creature finishes a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
If damage from a single attack or effect causes multiple Thresholds to be reached at the same time, you can choose which of the triggered Impulsive Reactions the creature uses.

entries.name: Learning a Creature's Disposition
entries: To determine the Disposition of a creature, a character can take the {@action Search|XPHB} action to make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check, provided it can see the creature. The DC to determine the Disposition of a creature is equal to 10 plus half the creature's CR.
Learning the Disposition of a creature does not inform a character of the creature's Impulsive Reactions, but it may provide insight into how the creature might act during combat.

entries.name: Creating Your Own Dispositions
entries: Below you'll find a list of guidelines to follow when designing your own Dispositions:

items: A creature must have a {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} minimum of 20 or higher for it to gain a Disposition.
There must be a minimum of 20 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} between Hit Point Thresholds.
A Hit Point Threshold must be no less than 5 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} below a creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum.
Impulsive Reactions are meant to be an extension of the creature's feelings or personality.
